verses.sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच | धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः | मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ||
verses.transliteration: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca | dharmakṣetre kurukshetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ | māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya ||
verses.translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, after assembling in the sacred place of Kurukshetra, desiring to fight, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?
verses.hindi: धृतराष्ट्र ने कहा — हे संजय! धर्मभूमि कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध की इच्छा से एकत्रित मेरे और पाण्डु के पुत्रों ने क्या किया?
verses.wordMeaning: Dhritarashtra's use of "māmakāḥ" (my sons) reveals his attachment to the Kauravas. His blindness is both physical and metaphorical — he cannot see the destruction caused by adharma.
verses.commentary: Dhritarashtra's use of "māmakāḥ" (my sons) reveals his attachment to the Kauravas. His blindness is both physical and metaphorical — he cannot see the destruction caused by adharma.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः | धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ||
verses.transliteration: yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||
verses.translation: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, slay me in battle while I am unarmed and unresisting, that would be better for me.
verses.hindi: यदि धार्तराष्ट्र शस्त्र-पाणि होकर युद्ध में मुझ अप्रतिकार करने वाले को मार दें, तो यह मेरे लिए अधिक कल्याणकारक होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna reaches the nadir of despondency. He confuses non-violence with cowardice. True non-violence is acting without hatred, not paralysis from attachment.
verses.commentary: Arjuna reaches the nadir of despondency. He confuses non-violence with cowardice. True non-violence is acting without hatred, not paralysis from attachment.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् | विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ||
verses.transliteration: sañjaya uvāca | evamuktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat | visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ ||
verses.translation: Having spoken thus, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows, and sat down on the chariot, his mind distressed with grief.
verses.hindi: संजय बोले — इस प्रकार कहकर, शोक से व्याकुल मन वाले अर्जुन ने रणभूमि में अपने बाण और धनुष छोड़कर रथ के पिछले भाग में बैठ गए।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna casts aside his weapons — the tools of his kshatriya dharma. His sitting posture signals defeat. This sets the stage for Krishna's entire teaching.
verses.commentary: Arjuna casts aside his weapons — the tools of his kshatriya dharma. His sitting posture signals defeat. This sets the stage for Krishna's entire teaching.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।

नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।।1.9।।
verses.transliteration:
anye cha bahavaḥ śhūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ
nānā-śhastra-praharaṇāḥ sarve yuddha-viśhāradāḥ
verses.translation: And there are many other heroes who are determined to give up their lives for my sake. They are all experts in using manifold missiles and dexterous in battle.
verses.hindi: ।।1.9।। इनके अतिरिक्त बहुत-से शूरवीर हैं, जिन्होंने मेरे लिये अपने जीने की इच्छा का भी त्याग कर दिया है और जो अनेक प्रकार के शस्त्र-अस्त्रों को चलानेवाले हैं तथा जो सब-के-सब युद्धकला में अत्यन्त चतुर हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: anye—others; cha—also; bahavaḥ—many; śhūrāḥ—heroic warriors; mat-arthe—for my sake; tyakta-jīvitāḥ—prepared to lay down their lives; nānā-śhastra-praharaṇāḥ—equipped with various kinds of weapons; sarve—all; yuddha-viśhāradāḥ—skilled in the art of warfare

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः।

सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान्।।1.12।।
verses.transliteration:
tasya sañjanayan harṣhaṁ kuru-vṛiddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ
siṁha-nādaṁ vinadyochchaiḥ śhaṅkhaṁ dadhmau pratāpavān
verses.translation: Then the valiant grandsire Bhisma, the senior-most of the Kuru clan, roared like a lion and blew his conch with the intention of cheering up Duryodhana.
verses.hindi: ।।1.12।। दुर्योधन के हृदय में हर्ष उत्पन्न करते हुए कुरुवृद्ध प्रभावशाली पितामह भीष्म ने सिंह के समान गरज कर जोर से शंख बजाया।
verses.wordMeaning: tasya—his; sañjanayan—causing; harṣham—joy; kuru-vṛiddhaḥ—the grand old man of the Kuru dynasty (Bheeshma); pitāmahaḥ—grandfather; sinha-nādam—lion’s roar; vinadya—sounding; uchchaiḥ—very loudly; śhaṅkham—conch shell; dadhmau—blew; pratāpa-vān—the glorious

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः।

नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ।।1.16।।
verses.transliteration:
anantavijayaṁ rājā kuntī-putro yudhiṣhṭhiraḥ
nakulaḥ sahadevaśhcha sughoṣha-maṇipuṣhpakau
verses.translation: King Yudhisthira, the son of Kunti, blew his conch, Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew their conchs, Sughosa and Manipuspaka.
verses.hindi: ।।1.16।। कुन्तीपुत्र राजा युधिष्ठिर ने अनन्तविजय नामक शंख बजाया तथा नकुल और सहदेव ने सुघोष और मणिपुष्पक नामक शंख बजाये।
verses.wordMeaning: ananta-vijayam—the conch named Anantavijay; rājā—king; kuntī-putraḥ—son of Kunti; yudhiṣhṭhiraḥ—Yudhishthir; nakulaḥ—Nakul; sahadevaḥ—Sahadev; cha—and; sughoṣha-maṇipuṣhpakau—the conche shells named Sughosh and Manipushpak;

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते।

सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक्।।1.18।।
verses.transliteration:
drupado draupadeyāśhcha sarvaśhaḥ pṛithivī-pate
saubhadraśhcha mahā-bāhuḥ śhaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛithak pṛithak
verses.translation: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, as well as the strong-armed son of Subhadra—all, O King, blew their respective conchs again and again.
verses.hindi: ।।1.17 -- 1.18।। हे राजन्! श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बी-लम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रा-पुत्र अभिमन्यु - इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलग-अलग (अपने-अपने) शंख बजाये।
verses.wordMeaning: drupadaḥ—Drupad; draupadeyāḥ—the five sons of Draupadi; cha—and; sarvaśhaḥ—all; pṛithivī-pate—Ruler of the earth; saubhadraḥ—Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadra; cha—also; mahā-bāhuḥ—the mighty-armed; śhaṅkhān—conch shells; dadhmuḥ—blew; pṛithak pṛithak—individually

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः।

धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः।।1.23।।
verses.transliteration:
yotsyamānān avekṣhe ’haṁ ya ete ’tra samāgatāḥ
dhārtarāṣhṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-chikīrṣhavaḥ
verses.translation: I wish to see those gathered here ready to fight in this battle in order to please the evil-minded son of Dhrtarashtra.
verses.hindi: ।।1.23।। दुष्टबुद्धि दुर्योधन का युद्ध में प्रिय करने की इच्छावाले जो ये राजालोग इस सेना में आये हुए हैं, युद्ध करने को उतावले हुए इन सबको मैं देख लूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: yotsyamānān—those who have come to fight; avekṣhe aham—I desire to see; ye—who; ete—those; atra—here; samāgatāḥ—assembled; dhārtarāṣhṭrasya—of Dhritarashtra’s son; durbuddheḥ—evil-minded; yuddhe—in the fight; priya-chikīrṣhavaḥ—wishing to please

verses.sanskrit:
संजय उवाच

एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत।

सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम्।।1.24।।
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
evam ukto hṛiṣhīkeśho guḍākeśhena bhārata
senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krishna drew up the best of chariots between the two armies, in full view of Bhisma, Drona, and all the other kings, O Dhrtarastra. He then said, "O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas."
verses.hindi: ।।1.24 -- 1.25।। संजय बोले - हे भरतवंशी राजन्! निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथ को खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि 'हे पार्थ! इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख'।
verses.wordMeaning: sañjayaḥ uvācha—Sanjay said; evam—thus; uktaḥ—addressed; hṛiṣhīkeśhaḥ—Shree Krishna, the Lord of the senses; guḍākeśhena—by Arjun, the conqueror of sleep; bhārata—descendant of Bharat; senayoḥ—armies; ubhayoḥ—the two; madhye—between; sthāpayitvā—having drawn; ratha-uttamam—magnificent chariot

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्।

उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति।।1.25।।
verses.transliteration:
bhīṣhma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ sarveṣhāṁ cha mahī-kṣhitām
uvācha pārtha paśhyaitān samavetān kurūn iti
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krishna drew up the best of chariots between the two armies, in full view of Bhisma, Drona, and all the other kings, O Dhrtarastra. He then said, "O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas."
verses.hindi: ।।1.24 -- 1.25।। संजय बोले - हे भरतवंशी राजन्! निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथको खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि 'हे पार्थ! इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख'।
verses.wordMeaning: bhīṣhma—Grandsire Bheeshma; droṇa—Dronacharya; pramukhataḥ—in the presence; sarveṣhām—all; cha—and; mahī-kṣhitām—other kings; uvācha—said; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; paśhya—behold; etān—these; samavetān—gathered; kurūn—descendants of Kuru; iti—thus

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।

वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते।।1.29।।
verses.transliteration:
sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṁ cha pariśhuṣhyati
vepathuśh cha śharīre me roma-harṣhaśh cha jāyate
verses.translation: My limbs have weakened, my mouth has become parched, my body is trembling, and my hairs are standing on end.
verses.hindi: ।।1.28 -- 1.30।। अर्जुन बोले - हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्ब-समुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं। हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है। मेरा मन भ्रमित-सा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning:
sīdanti—quivering; mama—my; gātrāṇi—limbs; mukham—mouth; cha—and; pariśhuṣhyati—is drying up
vepathuḥ—shuddering; cha—and; śharīre—on the body; me—my; roma-harṣhaḥ—standing of bodily hair on end; cha—also; jāyate—is happening;

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One.
verses.hindi: आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूर्य उदय हों तो जो प्रकाश हो, वह उस महात्मा (विश्वरूप) के तेज के समान होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.

verses.sanskrit:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।

त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च।।1.33।।
verses.transliteration:
yeṣhām arthe kāṅkṣhitaṁ no rājyaṁ bhogāḥ sukhāni cha
ta ime ’vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṁs tyaktvā dhanāni cha
verses.translation: Those for whose sake we desire empire, enjoyment, and pleasures, stand here in war, renouncing life and wealth.
verses.hindi: ।।1.33।। जिनके लिये हमारी राज्य, भोग और सुखकी इच्छा है, वे ही ये सब अपने प्राणों की और धन की आशा का त्याग करके युद्ध में खड़े हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: yeṣhām—for whose; arthe—sake; kāṅkṣhitam—coveted for; naḥ—by us; rājyam—kingdom; bhogāḥ—pleasures; sukhāni—happiness; cha—also; te—they; ime—these; avasthitāḥ—situated; yuddhe—for battle; prāṇān—lives; tyaktvā—giving up; dhanāni—wealth; cha—also

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यतां गतं पार्थ मायया ते तदात्मकम् | यत्तु सत्यं सनातनं तदहं वदतः स्म ते ||
verses.transliteration: adṛśyatāṃ gataṃ pārtha māyayā te tadātmakam | yattu satyaṃ sanātanaṃ tadahaṃ vadataḥ sma te ||
verses.translation: O Partha, the cosmic form you saw was manifested by My Yoga-Maya. Now I shall reveal to you My eternal form.
verses.hindi: हे पार्थ! जो तुमने देखा वह मेरी योगमाया से प्रकट किया गया था। अब मैं तुम्हें अपना शाश्वत रूप बताता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.
verses.commentary: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.transliteration: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
verses.hindi: अपने स्वधर्म में मरना भला है, चाहे वह अपूर्ण हो; परधर्म को अच्छी तरह से करना भयावह है।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.
verses.commentary: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.

verses.sanskrit:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन।

पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः।।1.36।।
verses.transliteration:
nihatya dhārtarāṣhṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana
pāpam evāśhrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ
verses.translation: If we were to kill the sons of Dhrtarastra, what joy would be ours, O Krsna? Sin alone would accrue to us if we killed these murderous felons.
verses.hindi: ।।1.36।। हे जनार्दन! इन धृतराष्ट्र-सम्बन्धियों को मारकर हमलोगों को क्या प्रसन्नता होगी? इन आततायियों को मारने से तो हमें पाप ही लगेगा।
verses.wordMeaning: nihatya—by killing; dhārtarāṣhṭrān—the sons of Dhritarashtra; naḥ—our; kā—what; prītiḥ—pleasure; syāt—will there be; janārdana—he who looks after the public, Shree Krishna; pāpam—vices; eva—certainly; āśhrayet—must come upon; asmān—us; hatvā—by killing; etān—all these; ātatāyinaḥ—aggressors;

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्।

स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव।।1.37।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmān nārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣhṭrān sa-bāndhavān 
sva-janaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
verses.translation: Therefore, it is not befitting for us to slay our kin, the sons of Dhrtarastra. For if we kill our kinsmen, O Krsna, how can we be happy?
verses.hindi: ।।1.37।। इसलिये अपने बान्धव इन धृतराष्ट्र-सम्बन्धियों को मारने के लिये हम योग्य नहीं हैं; क्योंकि हे माधव! अपने कुटुम्बियों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे?
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—hence; na—never; arhāḥ—behoove; vayam—we; hantum—to kill; dhārtarāṣhṭrān—the sons of Dhritarashtra; sva-bāndhavān—along with friends; sva-janam—kinsmen; hi—certainly; katham—how; hatvā—by killing; sukhinaḥ—happy; syāma—will we become; mādhava—Shree Krishna, the husband of Yogmaya

verses.sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ | ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ||
verses.transliteration: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
verses.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same — then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.
verses.hindi: सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि और जय-पराजय को समान करके तब युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो। इस प्रकार तुम पाप नहीं प्राप्त करोगे।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).

verses.sanskrit:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्।

कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन।।1.39।।
verses.transliteration:
kathaṁ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum
kula-kṣhaya-kṛitaṁ doṣhaṁ prapaśhyadbhir janārdana
verses.translation: Why should we not learn to shun this crime—we who see the evil of ruining a clan, O Krishna?
verses.hindi: ।।1.38 -- 1.39।। यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेक-विचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये (दुर्योधन आदि) कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, (तो भी) हे जनार्दन! कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीक-ठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होनेका विचार क्यों न करें?
verses.wordMeaning: katham—why; na—not; jñeyam—should be known; asmābhiḥ—we; pāpāt—from sin; asmāt—these; nivartitum—to turn away; kula-kṣhaya—killing the kindered; kṛitam—done; doṣham—crime; prapaśhyadbhiḥ—who can see; janārdana—he who looks after the public, Shree Krishna

verses.sanskrit:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः।

धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत।।1.40।।
verses.transliteration:
kula-kṣhaye praṇaśhyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ
dharme naṣhṭe kulaṁ kṛitsnam adharmo ’bhibhavaty uta
verses.translation: With the ruin of a clan, its ancient traditions perish, and when traditions perish, lawlessness overtakes the whole clan.
verses.hindi: ।।1.40।। कुल का क्षय होने पर सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं और धर्म का नाश होनेपर (बचे हुए) सम्पूर्ण कुल को अधर्म दबा लेता है।
verses.wordMeaning: kula-kṣhaye—in the destruction of a dynasty; praṇaśhyanti—are vanquished; kula-dharmāḥ—family traditions; sanātanāḥ—eternal; dharme—religion; naṣhṭe—is destroyed; kulam—family; kṛitsnam—the whole; adharmaḥ—irreligion; abhibhavati—overcome; uta—indeed

verses.sanskrit:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः।

स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः।।1.41।।
verses.transliteration:
adharmābhibhavāt kṛiṣhṇa praduṣhyanti kula-striyaḥ
strīṣhu duṣhṭāsu vārṣhṇeya jāyate varṇa-saṅkaraḥ
verses.translation: When lawlessness prevails, O Krsna, the women of the clan become corrupted; when women become corrupted, there arises an intermixing of classes.
verses.hindi: ।।1.41।। हे कृष्ण! अधर्म के अधिक बढ़ जाने से कुल की स्त्रियाँ दूषित हो जाती हैं; (और) हे वार्ष्णेय! स्त्रियों के दूषित होने पर वर्णसंकर पैदा हो जाते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: adharma—irreligion; abhibhavāt—preponderance; kṛiṣhṇa—Shree Krishna; praduṣhyanti—become immoral; kula-striyaḥ—women of the family; strīṣhu—of women; duṣhṭāsu—become immoral; vārṣhṇeya—descendant of Vrishni; jāyate—are born; varṇa-saṅkaraḥ—unwanted progeny

verses.sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः | स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||
verses.transliteration: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||
verses.translation: Whatever a great man does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
verses.hindi: जो-जो आचरण श्रेष्ठ पुरुष करता है, अन्य लोग भी वही करते हैं। वह जो प्रमाण स्थापित करता है, संसार उसी का अनुसरण करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.
verses.commentary: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.

verses.sanskrit:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः।

उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः।।1.43।।
verses.transliteration:
doṣhair etaiḥ kula-ghnānāṁ varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ
utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāśh cha śhāśhvatāḥ
verses.translation: By the sins of the clan-destroyers who bring about intermixing of classes, the ancient traditions of the clans and classes are destroyed.
verses.hindi: ।।1.43।। इन वर्णसंकर पैदा करनेवाले दोषोंसे कुलघातियों के सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म और जातिधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: doṣhaiḥ—through evil deeds; etaiḥ—these; kula-ghnānām—of those who destroy the family; varṇa-saṅkara—unwanted progeny; kārakaiḥ—causing; utsādyante—are ruined; jāti-dharmāḥ—social and family welfare activities; kula-dharmāḥ—family traditions; cha—and; śhāśhvatāḥ—eternal

verses.sanskrit:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन।

नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम।।1.44।।
verses.transliteration:
utsanna-kula-dharmāṇāṁ manuṣhyāṇāṁ janārdana
narake ‘niyataṁ vāso bhavatītyanuśhuśhruma
verses.translation: For those whose clan laws are destroyed, dwelling in hell is ordained, O Krishna; thus, we have heard.
verses.hindi: ।।1.44।। हे जनार्दन! जिनके कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं, उन मनुष्यों का बहुत काल तक नरकों में वापस होता है, ऐसा हम सुनते आये हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: utsanna—destroyed; kula-dharmāṇām—whose family traditions; manuṣhyāṇām—of such human beings; janārdana—he who looks after the public, Shree Krishna; narake—in hell; aniyatam—indefinite; vāsaḥ—dwell; bhavati—is; iti—thus; anuśhuśhruma—I have heard from the learned

verses.sanskrit:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।

यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः।।1.45।।
verses.transliteration:
aho bata mahat pāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam
yad rājya-sukha-lobhena hantuṁ sva-janam udyatāḥ
verses.translation: Alas! We have resolved to commit a great sin, for we are ready to slay our kin out of desire for sovereignty and enjoyment.
verses.hindi: ।।1.45।। यह बड़े आश्चर्य और खेद की बात है कि हमलोग बड़ा भारी पाप करने का निश्चय कर बैठे हैं, जो कि राज्य और सुख के लोभ से अपने स्वजनों को मारने के लिये तैयार हो गये हैं!
verses.wordMeaning: aho—alas; bata—how; mahat—great; pāpam—sins; kartum—to perform; vyavasitāḥ—have decided; vayam—we; yat—because; rājya-sukha-lobhena—driven by the desire for kingly pleasure; hantum—to kill; sva-janam—kinsmen; udyatāḥ—intending;

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन् नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः | अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ||
verses.transliteration: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
verses.translation: The soul is never born, nor does it ever die. Having come into being, it never ceases to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, and ancient, the soul is not slain when the body is slain.
verses.hindi: आत्मा न तो कभी जन्म लेती है और न ही मरती है। वह एक बार उत्पन्न होने पर फिर होने वाली भी नहीं है। यह अजन्मा, नित्य, शाश्वत और पुरातन है — शरीर के नाश होने पर भी इसका नाश नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most celebrated verses. The Self is "aja" (unborn), "nitya" (eternal), "śāśvata" (permanent), and "purāṇa" (ancient). Death is only of the body, not of the Self.
verses.commentary: One of the most celebrated verses. The Self is "aja" (unborn), "nitya" (eternal), "śāśvata" (permanent), and "purāṇa" (ancient). Death is only of the body, not of the Self.

verses.sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ | ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ||
verses.transliteration: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
verses.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same — then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.
verses.hindi: सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि और जय-पराजय को समान करके तब युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो। इस प्रकार तुम पाप नहीं प्राप्त करोगे।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).

verses.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन | मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ||
verses.transliteration: karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi ||
verses.translation: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction.
verses.hindi: तुम्हारा अधिकार केवल कर्म करने में है, फल में कभी नहीं। न तो कर्म के फल का कारण बनो, और न ही कर्म न करने में आसक्त हो।
verses.wordMeaning: The most famous verse of the Gita. Krishna teaches "Nishkama Karma" — action without attachment to results. One has control over action (karma) but not over the fruits (phala). Attachment to results causes bondage; inaction causes stagnation.
verses.commentary: The most famous verse of the Gita. Krishna teaches "Nishkama Karma" — action without attachment to results. One has control over action (karma) but not over the fruits (phala). Attachment to results causes bondage; inaction causes stagnation.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप।

न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह।।2.9।।
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
evam-uktvā hṛiṣhīkeśhaṁ guḍākeśhaḥ parantapa
na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣhṇīṁ babhūva ha
verses.translation: Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken to Sri Krsna, Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and the scorcher of foes, said, "I will not fight," and became silent.
verses.hindi: ।।2.9।। संजय बोले - हे शत्रुतापन धृतराष्ट्र! ऐसा कहकर निद्राको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन अन्तर्यामी भगवान् गोविन्दसे 'मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा' ऐसा साफ-साफ कहकर चुप हो गये।
verses.wordMeaning: sañjayaḥ uvācha—Sanjay said; evam—thus; uktvā—having spoken; hṛiṣhīkeśham—to Shree Krishna, the master of the mind and senses; guḍākeśhaḥ—Arjun, the conquerer of sleep; parantapaḥ—Arjun, the chastiser of the enemies; na yotsye—I shall not fight; iti—thus; govindam—Krishna, the giver of pleasure to the senses; uktvā—having addressed; tūṣhṇīm—silent; babhūva—became ha

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।

न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्।।2.12।।
verses.transliteration:
na tvevāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ
na chaiva na bhaviṣhyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
verses.translation: There never was a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings. Nor will there be any time in the future when all of us shall cease to exist.
verses.hindi: ।।2.12।। किसी कालमें मैं नहीं था और तू नहीं था तथा ये राजालोग नहीं थे, यह बात भी नहीं है; और इसके बाद (भविष्य में) मैं, तू और राजलोग - हम सभी नहीं रहेंगे, यह बात भी नहीं है।
verses.wordMeaning: na—never; tu—however; eva—certainly; aham—I; jātu—at any time; na—nor; āsam—exist; na—nor; tvam—you; na—nor; ime—these; jana-adhipāḥ—kings; na—never; cha—also; eva—indeed; na bhaviṣhyāmaḥ—shall not exist; sarve vayam—all of us; ataḥ—from now; param—after

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।

उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः।।2.16।।
verses.transliteration:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
ubhayorapi dṛiṣhṭo ’nta stvanayos tattva-darśhibhiḥ
verses.translation: The unreal never comes into being, the real never ceases to be. The truth about these two is seen by the seers.
verses.hindi: ।।2.16।। (टिप्पणी प0 55) असत् का तो भाव (सत्ता) विद्यमान नहीं है और सत् का अभाव विद्यमान नहीं है, तत्त्वदर्शी महापुरुषोंने इन दोनोंका ही अन्त अर्थात् तत्त्व देखा है।
verses.wordMeaning: na—no; asataḥ—of the temporary; vidyate—there is; bhāvaḥ—is; na—no; abhāvaḥ—cessation; vidyate—is; sataḥ—of the eternal; ubhayoḥ—of the two; api—also; dṛiṣhṭaḥ—observed; antaḥ—conclusion; tu—verily; anayoḥ—of these; tattva—of the truth; darśhibhiḥ—by the seers

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।

अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत।।2.18।।
verses.transliteration:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śharīriṇaḥ
anāśhino ’prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata
verses.translation: These bodies of the Jiva (the embodied self) are said to have an end, while the Jiva itself is eternal, indestructible, and incomprehensible. Therefore, fight, O Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.hindi: ।।2.18।। अविनाशी, अप्रमेय और नित्य रहनेवाले इस शरीरी के ये देह अन्तवाले कहे गये हैं। इसलिये हे अर्जुन! तुम युद्ध करो।
verses.wordMeaning: anta-vantaḥ—having an end; ime—these; dehāḥ—material bodies; nityasya—eternally; uktāḥ—are said; śharīriṇaḥ—of the embodied soul; anāśhinaḥ—indestructible; aprameyasya—immeasurable; tasmāt—therefore; yudhyasva—fight; bhārata—descendant of Bharat, Arjun

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।

न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।2.23।।
verses.transliteration:
nainaṁ chhindanti śhastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ
na chainaṁ kledayantyāpo na śhoṣhayati mārutaḥ
verses.translation: Weapons cannot cleave It, fire cannot burn It, waters cannot wet It, and wind cannot dry It.
verses.hindi: ।।2.23।। शस्त्र इस शरीरीको काट नहीं सकते, अग्नि इसको जला नहीं सकती, जल इसको गीला नहीं कर सकता और वायु इसको सुखा नहीं सकती।
verses.wordMeaning: na—not; enam—this soul; chhindanti—shred; śhastrāṇi—weapons; na—nor; enam—this soul; dahati—burns; pāvakaḥ—fire; na—not; cha—and; enam—this soul; kledayanti—moisten; āpaḥ—water; na—nor; śhoṣhayati—dry; mārutaḥ—wind

verses.sanskrit:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।

नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः।।2.24।।
verses.transliteration:
achchhedyo ’yam adāhyo ’yam akledyo ’śhoṣhya eva cha
nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur achalo ’yaṁ sanātanaḥ
verses.translation: It cannot be cleaved; It cannot be burned; It cannot be wetted, and It cannot be dried; It is eternal, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, and primordial.
verses.hindi: ।।2.24।। यह शरीरी काटा नहीं जा सकता, यह जलाया नहीं जा सकता, यह गीला नहीं किया जा सकता और यह सुखाया भी नहीं जा सकता। कारण कि यह नित्य रहनेवाला सबमें परिपूर्ण, अचल, स्थिर स्वभाववाला और अनादि है।
verses.wordMeaning: achchhedyaḥ—unbreakable; ayam—this soul; adāhyaḥ—incombustible; ayam—this soul; akledyaḥ—cannot be dampened; aśhoṣhyaḥ—cannot be dried; eva—indeed; cha—and; nityaḥ—everlasting; sarva-gataḥ—all-pervading; sthāṇuḥ—unalterable; achalaḥ—immutable; ayam—this soul; sanātanaḥ—primordial

verses.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।

तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि।।2.25।।
verses.transliteration:
avyakto ’yam achintyo ’yam avikāryo ’yam uchyate
tasmādevaṁ viditvainaṁ nānuśhochitum arhasi
verses.translation: This (self) is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchanging. Therefore, knowing it thus, it does not befit you to grieve.
verses.hindi: ।।2.25।। यह देही प्रत्यक्ष नहीं दीखता, यह चिन्तनका विषय नहीं है और यह निर्विकार कहा जाता है। अतः इस देहीको ऐसा जानकर शोक नहीं करना चाहिये।
verses.wordMeaning: avyaktaḥ—unmanifested; ayam—this soul; achintyaḥ—inconceivable; ayam—this soul; avikāryaḥ—unchangeable; ayam—this soul; uchyate—is said; tasmāt—therefore; evam—thus; viditvā—having known; enam—this soul; na—not; anuśhochitum—to grieve; arhasi—befitting

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन

माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।

आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति

श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्।।2.29।।
verses.transliteration:
āśhcharya-vat paśhyati kaśhchid enan
āśhcharya-vad vadati tathaiva chānyaḥ
āśhcharya-vach chainam anyaḥ śhṛiṇoti
śhrutvāpyenaṁ veda na chaiva kaśhchit
verses.translation: One regards This (self) as a wonder; another speaks of It as a wonder; yet another hears of It as a wonder; and even after hearing of It, one does not know It.
verses.hindi: ।।2.29।। कोई इस शरीरीको आश्चर्यकी तरह देखता है और वैसे ही अन्य कोई इसका आश्चर्यकी तरह वर्णन करता है तथा अन्य कोई इसको आश्चर्यकी तरह सुनता है; और इसको सुनकर भी कोई नहीं जानता। अर्थात यह शरीरी दुर्विज्ञेय है।
verses.wordMeaning: āśhcharya-vat—as amazing; paśhyati—see; kaśhchit—someone; enam—this soul; āśhcharya-vat—as amazing; vadati—speak of; tathā—thus; eva—indeed; cha—and; anyaḥ—other; āśhcharya-vat—similarly amazing; cha—also; enam—this soul; anyaḥ—others; śhṛiṇoti—hear; śhrutvā—having heard; api—even; enam—this soul; veda—understand; na—not; cha—and; eva—even; kaśhchit—some

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One.
verses.hindi: आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूर्य उदय हों तो जो प्रकाश हो, वह उस महात्मा (विश्वरूप) के तेज के समान होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।

ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.33।।
verses.transliteration:
atha chet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣhyasi
tataḥ sva-dharmaṁ kīrtiṁ cha hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi
verses.translation: But if you do not fight this righteous war, you will be turning away from your duty and honor, and will incur sin.
verses.hindi: ।।2.33।। अब अगर तू यह धर्ममय युद्ध नहीं करेगा,  तो अपने धर्म और कीर्तिका त्याग करके पापको प्राप्त होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: atha chet—if, however; tvam—you; imam—this; dharmyam saṅgrāmam—righteous war; na—not; kariṣhyasi—act; tataḥ—then; sva-dharmam—one’s duty in accordance with the Vedas; kīrtim—reputation; cha—and; hitvā—abandoning; pāpam—sin; avāpsyasi—will incur

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यतां गतं पार्थ मायया ते तदात्मकम् | यत्तु सत्यं सनातनं तदहं वदतः स्म ते ||
verses.transliteration: adṛśyatāṃ gataṃ pārtha māyayā te tadātmakam | yattu satyaṃ sanātanaṃ tadahaṃ vadataḥ sma te ||
verses.translation: O Partha, the cosmic form you saw was manifested by My Yoga-Maya. Now I shall reveal to you My eternal form.
verses.hindi: हे पार्थ! जो तुमने देखा वह मेरी योगमाया से प्रकट किया गया था। अब मैं तुम्हें अपना शाश्वत रूप बताता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.
verses.commentary: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.transliteration: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
verses.hindi: अपने स्वधर्म में मरना भला है, चाहे वह अपूर्ण हो; परधर्म को अच्छी तरह से करना भयावह है।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.
verses.commentary: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.

verses.sanskrit:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।

निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्।।2.36।।
verses.transliteration:
avāchya-vādānśh cha bahūn vadiṣhyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantastava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim
verses.translation: Your enemies, slandering your prowess, will use words that should never be uttered. What could be more painful than that?
verses.hindi: ।।2.36।। तेरे शत्रुलोग तेरी सार्मथ्यकी निन्दा करते हुए न कहनेयोग्य बहुत-से वचन भी कहेंगे। उससे बढ़कर और दुःखकी बात क्या होगी?
verses.wordMeaning: avāchya-vādān—using harsh words; cha—and; bahūn—many; vadiṣhyanti—will say; tava—your; ahitāḥ—enemies; nindantaḥ—defame; tava—your; sāmarthyam—might; tataḥ—than that; duḥkha-taram—more painful; nu—indeed; kim—what

verses.sanskrit:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।

तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः।।2.37।।
verses.transliteration:
hato vā prāpsyasi swargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣhyase mahīm
tasmād uttiṣhṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛita-niśhchayaḥ
verses.translation: If slain, you will win heaven; or if victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise, O Arjuna, resolved to fight.
verses.hindi: ।।2.37।। अगर युद्धमें तू मारा जायगा तो तुझे स्वर्गकी प्राप्ति होगी और अगर युद्धमें तू जीत जायगा तो पृथ्वीका राज्य भोगेगा। अतः हे कुन्तीनन्दन! तू युद्धके लिये निश्चय करके खड़ा हो जा।
verses.wordMeaning: hataḥ—slain; vā—or; prāpsyasi—you will attain; swargam—celestial abodes; jitvā—by achieving victory; vā—or; bhokṣhyase—you shall enjoy; mahīm—the kingdom on earth; tasmāt—therefore; uttiṣhṭha—arise; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; yuddhāya—for fight; kṛita-niśhchayaḥ—with determination

verses.sanskrit:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु।

बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि।।2.39।।
verses.transliteration:
eṣhā te ’bhihitā sānkhye
buddhir yoge tvimāṁ śhṛiṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha
karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi
verses.translation: This Buddhi concerning the Self (Sankhya) has been imparted to you. Now listen to this with regard to Yoga, by following which you will get rid of the bondage of Karma.
verses.hindi: ।।2.39।। हे पार्थ! यह समबुद्धि तेरे लिए पहले सांख्ययोगमें कही गयी, अब तू इसको कर्मयोगके विषयमें सुन; जिस समबुद्धिसे युक्त हुआ तू कर्मबन्धनका त्याग कर देगा।
verses.wordMeaning: eṣhā—hitherto; te—to you; abhihitā—explained; sānkhye—by analytical knowledge; buddhiḥ yoge—by the yog of intellect; tu—indeed; imām—this; śhṛiṇu—listen; buddhyā—by understanding; yuktaḥ—united; yayā—by which; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; karma-bandham—bondage of karma; prahāsyasi—you shall be released from

verses.sanskrit:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।

स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्।।2.40।।
verses.transliteration:
nehābhikrama-nāśho ’sti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpam apyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
verses.translation: Here, there is no loss of effort, nor any accrual of evil. Even a little of this Dharma (called Karma Yoga) protects one from the great fear.
verses.hindi: ।।2.40।। मनुष्यलोकमें इस समबुद्धिरूप धर्मके आरम्भका नाश नहीं होता, इसके अनुष्ठानका उलटा फल भी नहीं होता और इसका थोड़ासा भी अनुष्ठान (जन्म-मरणरूप) महान् भयसे रक्षा कर लेता है।
verses.wordMeaning: na—not; iha—in this; abhikrama—efforts; nāśhaḥ—loss; asti—there is; pratyavāyaḥ—adverse result; na—not; vidyate—is; su-alpam—a little; api—even; asya—of this; dharmasya—occupation; trāyate—saves; mahataḥ—from great; bhayāt—danger

verses.sanskrit:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।

बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्।।2.41।।
verses.transliteration:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana
bahu-śhākhā hyanantāśh cha buddhayo ’vyavasāyinām
verses.translation: In this (Karma Yoga), O Arjuna, the resolute mind is single-pointed; the minds of the irresolute are multi-branched and endless.
verses.hindi: ।।2.41।। हे कुरुनन्दन! इस समबुद्धिकी प्राप्तिके विषयमें व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि एक ही होती है। अव्यवसायी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धियाँ अनन्त और बहुशाखाओंवाली ही होती हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: vyavasāya-ātmikā—resolute; buddhiḥ—intellect; ekā—single; iha—on this path; kuru-nandana—descendent of the Kurus; bahu-śhākhāḥ—many-branched; hi—indeed; anantāḥ—endless; cha—also; buddhayaḥ—intellect; avyavasāyinām—of the irresolute

verses.sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः | स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||
verses.transliteration: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||
verses.translation: Whatever a great man does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
verses.hindi: जो-जो आचरण श्रेष्ठ पुरुष करता है, अन्य लोग भी वही करते हैं। वह जो प्रमाण स्थापित करता है, संसार उसी का अनुसरण करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.
verses.commentary: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.

verses.sanskrit:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।

क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति।।2.43।।
verses.transliteration:
kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parā 

 janma-karma-phala-pradām

 kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṁ

 bhogaiśvarya-gatiṁ prati
verses.translation: - O Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, "There is nothing else." They are full only of worldly desires and they yearn for heaven. They speak flowery words that offer mirth as the fruit of work. They view the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power. Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a focused mind.
verses.hindi: ।।2.42 -- 2.43।। हे पृथानन्दन ! जो कामनाओंमें तन्मय हो रहे हैं, स्वर्गको ही श्रेष्ठ माननेवाले हैं, वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंमें प्रीति रखनेवाले हैं, भोगोंके सिवाय और कुछ है ही नहीं - ऐसा कहनेवाले हैं, वे अविवेकी मनुष्य इस प्रकारकी जिस पुष्पित (दिखाऊ शोभायुक्त) वाणीको कहा करते हैं, जो कि जन्मरूपी कर्मफलको देनेवाली है तथा भोग और ऐश्वर्यकी प्राप्तिके लिये बहुतसी क्रियाओंका वर्णन करनेवाली है।
verses.wordMeaning: kāmaātmānaḥ—desirous   of  sense   gratification;  svarga-parāḥ—aiming to  achieve heavenly    planets;    janma-karma-phala-pradām—resulting  in  fruitive    action, good        birth,     etc.;      kriyā-viśeṣa—pompous       ceremonies;        bahulām—various; bhoga—sense       enjoyment;     aiśvarya—opulence;     gatim—progress;    prati—towards.

verses.sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।

व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते।।2.44।।
verses.transliteration:
bhogaiśwvarya-prasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛita-chetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
verses.translation: - O Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, "There is nothing else." They are full only of worldly desires and they hanker for heaven. They speak flowery words that offer mirth as the fruit of work. They look upon the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power. Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a concentrated mind.
verses.hindi: ।।2.44।। उस पुष्पित वाणीसे जिसका अन्तःकरण हर लिया गया है अर्थात् भोगोंकी तरफ खिंच गया है और जो भोग तथा ऐश्वर्यमें अत्यन्त आसक्त हैं, उन मनुष्योंकी परमात्मामें निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धि नहीं होती।
verses.wordMeaning: bhoga—gratification; aiśhwarya—luxury; prasaktānām—whose minds are deeply attached; tayā—by that; apahṛita-chetasām—bewildered in intellect; vyavasāya-ātmikā—resolute; buddhiḥ—intellect; samādhau—fulfilment; na—never; vidhīyate—occurs

verses.sanskrit:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।

निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।2.45।।
verses.transliteration:
trai-guṇya-viṣhayā vedā nistrai-guṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣhema ātmavān
verses.translation: The Vedas have the three Gunas as their sphere, O Arjuna. You must be free from the three Gunas and be free from the pairs of opposites. Abide in pure Sattva; never care to acquire things and to protect what has been acquired, but be established in the Self.
verses.hindi: ।।2.45।। वेद तीनों गुणोंके कार्यका ही वर्णन करनेवाले हैं; हे अर्जुन! तू तीनों गुणोंसे रहित हो जा, निर्द्वन्द्व हो जा, निरन्तर नित्य वस्तु परमात्मा में स्थित हो जा, योगक्षेमकी चाहना भी मत रख और परमात्मपरायण हो जा।
verses.wordMeaning: trai-guṇya—of the three modes of material nature; viṣhayāḥ—subject matter; vedāḥ—Vedic scriptures; nistrai-guṇyaḥ—above the three modes of material nature, transcendental; bhava—be; arjuna—Arjun; nirdvandvaḥ—free from dualities; nitya-sattva-sthaḥ—eternally fixed in truth; niryoga-kṣhemaḥ—unconcerned about gain and preservation; ātma-vān—situated in the self

verses.sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः | धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ||
verses.transliteration: yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||
verses.translation: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, slay me in battle while I am unarmed and unresisting, that would be better for me.
verses.hindi: यदि धार्तराष्ट्र शस्त्र-पाणि होकर युद्ध में मुझ अप्रतिकार करने वाले को मार दें, तो यह मेरे लिए अधिक कल्याणकारक होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna reaches the nadir of despondency. He confuses non-violence with cowardice. True non-violence is acting without hatred, not paralysis from attachment.
verses.commentary: Arjuna reaches the nadir of despondency. He confuses non-violence with cowardice. True non-violence is acting without hatred, not paralysis from attachment.

verses.sanskrit:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।

सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते।।2.48।।
verses.transliteration:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate
verses.translation: Abandoning attachment and established in Yoga, perform works, viewing success and failure with an even mind. Evenness of mind is said to be Yoga.
verses.hindi: ।।2.48।। हे धनञ्जय ! तू आसक्तिका त्याग करके सिद्धि-असिद्धिमें सम होकर योगमें स्थित हुआ कर्मोंको कर; क्योंकि समत्व ही योग कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: yoga-sthaḥ—being steadfast in yog; kuru—perform; karmāṇi—duties; saṅgam—attachment; tyaktvā—having abandoned; dhanañjaya—Arjun; siddhi-asiddhyoḥ—in success and failure; samaḥ—equipoised; bhūtvā—becoming; samatvam—equanimity; yogaḥ—Yog; uchyate—is called

verses.sanskrit:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।

बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः।।2.49।।
verses.transliteration:
dūreṇa hy-avaraṁ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya
buddhau śharaṇam anvichchha kṛipaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ
verses.translation: Action done with attachment, O Arjuna, is far inferior to action done with evenness of mind. Seek refuge in evenness of mind; those who act with a motive for results are miserable.
verses.hindi: ।।2.49।। बुद्धियोग-(समता) की अपेक्षा सकामकर्म दूरसे (अत्यन्त) ही निकृष्ट है। अतः हे धनञ्जय ! तू बुद्धि (समता) का आश्रय ले; क्योंकि फलके हेतु बननेवाले अत्यन्त दीन हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: dūreṇa—(discrad) from far away; hi—certainly; avaram—inferior; karma—reward-seeking actions; buddhi-yogāt—with the intellect established in Divine knowledge; dhanañjaya—Arjun; buddhau—divine knowledge and insight; śharaṇam—refuge; anvichchha—seek; kṛipaṇāḥ—miserly; phala-hetavaḥ—those seeking fruits of their work

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।

तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्।।2.50।।
verses.transliteration:
buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛita-duṣhkṛite
tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśhalam
verses.translation: A person with an evenness of mind discards both good and evil here and now. Therefore, strive for Yoga; for Yoga is skill in action.
verses.hindi: ।।2.50।। बुद्धि-(समता) से युक्त मनुष्य यहाँ जीवित अवस्थामें ही पुण्य और पाप दोनोंका त्याग कर देता है। अतः तू योग-(समता-) में लग जा, क्योंकि योग ही कर्मोंमें कुशलता है।
verses.wordMeaning: buddhi-yuktaḥ—endowed with wisdom; jahāti—get rid of; iha—in this life; ubhe—both; sukṛita-duṣhkṛite—good and bad deeds; tasmāt—therefore; yogāya—for Yog; yujyasva—strive for; yogaḥ—yog is; karmasu kauśhalam—the art of working skillfully

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।

जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्।।2.51।।
verses.transliteration:
karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣhiṇaḥ
janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṁ gachchhanty-anāmayam
verses.translation: The wise, who possess evenness of mind, relinquish the fruits born of action, and are freed from the bondage of birth, going to the region beyond all ills.
verses.hindi: ।।2.51।। समतायुक्त मनीषी साधक कर्मजन्य फलका त्याग करके जन्मरूप बन्धनसे मुक्त होकर निर्विकार पदको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: karma-jam—born of fruitive actions; buddhi-yuktāḥ—endowed with equanimity of intellect; hi—as; phalam—fruits; tyaktvā—abandoning; manīṣhiṇaḥ—the wise; janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ—freedom from the bondage of life and death; padam—state; gachchhanti—attain; anāmayam—devoid of sufferings

verses.sanskrit:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति।

तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च।।2.52।।
verses.transliteration:
yadā te moha-kalilaṁ buddhir vyatitariṣhyati
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śhrotavyasya śhrutasya cha
verses.translation: When your intellect has passed beyond the tangle of delusion, you will yourself feel disgusted with what you have heard and what you will hear.
verses.hindi: ।।2.52।। जिस समय तेरी बुद्धि मोहरूपी दलदलको तर जायगी, उसी समय तू सुने हुए और सुननेमें आनेवाले भोगोंसे वैराग्यको प्राप्त हो जायगा।
