verses.wordMeaning: yadā—when; te—your; moha—delusion; kalilam—quagmire; buddhiḥ—intellect; vyatitariṣhyati—crosses; tadā—then; gantāsi—you shall acquire; nirvedam—indifferent; śhrotavyasya—to what is yet to be heard; śhrutasya—to what has been heard; cha—and

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।

समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि।।2.53।।
verses.transliteration:
śhruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niśhchalā
samādhāv-achalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi
verses.translation: When your intellect, having been well enlightened by hearing from Me and firmly placed, stands unshaken in a concentrated mind, then you will attain the vision of the Self.
verses.hindi: ।।2.53।। जिस कालमें शास्त्रीय मतभेदोंसे विचलित हुई तेरी बुद्धि निश्चल हो जायगी और परमात्मामें अचल हो जायगी, उस कालमें तू योगको प्राप्त हो जायगा।
verses.wordMeaning: śhruti-vipratipannā—not allured by the fruitive sections of the Vedas; te—your; yadā—when; sthāsyati—remains; niśhchalā—steadfast; samādhau—in divine consciousness; achalā—steadfast; buddhiḥ—intellect; tadā—at that time; yogam—Yog; avāpsyasi—you will attain

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।

स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्।।2.54।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣhā samādhi-sthasya keśhava
sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣheta kim āsīta vrajeta kim
verses.translation: Arjuna said, "What is the mode of speech of one who is of firm wisdom, established in the control of the mind? What does a man of firm wisdom speak, O Krsna? How does he sit? How does he move?"
verses.hindi: ।।2.54।। अर्जुन बोले - हे केशव ! परमात्मामें स्थित स्थिर बुद्धिवाले मनुष्यके क्या लक्षण होते हैं? वह स्थिर बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य कैसे बोलता है, कैसे बैठता है और कैसे चलता है?
verses.wordMeaning: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; sthita-prajñasya—one with steady intellect; kā—what; bhāṣhā—talk; samādhi-sthasya—situated in divine consciousness; keśhava—Shree Krishna, killer of the Keshi Demon; sthita-dhīḥ—enlightened person; kim—what; prabhāṣheta—talks; kim—how; āsīta—sits; vrajeta—walks; kim—how

verses.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्।

आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते।।2.55।।
verses.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān
ātmany-evātmanā tuṣhṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tadochyate
verses.translation: The Lord said, "When a man renounces all the desires of the mind and is content with himself, then he is said to possess firm wisdom."
verses.hindi: ।।2.55।। श्रीभगवान् बोले - हे पृथानन्दन ! जिस कालमें साधक मनोगत सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका अच्छी तरह त्याग कर देता है और अपने-आपसे अपने-आपमें ही सन्तुष्ट रहता है, उस कालमें वह स्थितप्रज्ञ कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha—The Supreme Lord said; prajahāti—discards; yadā—when; kāmān—selfish desires; sarvān—all; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; manaḥ-gatān—of the mind; ātmani—of the self; eva—only; ātmanā—by the purified mind; tuṣhṭaḥ—satisfied; sthita-prajñaḥ—one with steady intellect; tadā—at that time; uchyate—is said

verses.sanskrit:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।

वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते।।2.56।।
verses.transliteration:
duḥkheṣhv-anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣhu vigata-spṛihaḥ
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir uchyate
verses.translation: He whose mind is not perturbed by pain, who has no longing for pleasures, who is free from desire, fear, and anger—he is called a sage of firm wisdom.
verses.hindi: ।।2.56।। दुःखोंकी प्राप्ति होनेपर जिसके मनमें उद्वेग नहीं होता और सुखोंकी प्राप्ति होनेपर जिसके मनमें स्पृहा नहीं होती तथा जो राग, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित हो गया है, वह मननशील मनुष्य स्थिरबुद्धि कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: duḥkheṣhu—amidst miseries; anudvigna-manāḥ—one whose mind is undisturbed; sukheṣhu—in pleasure; vigata-spṛihaḥ—without craving; vīta—free from; rāga—attachment; bhaya—fear; krodhaḥ—anger; sthita-dhīḥ—enlightened person; muniḥ—a sage; uchyate—is called

verses.sanskrit:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।

नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.57।।
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śhubhāśhubham
nābhinandati na dveṣhṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
verses.translation: He who has no love on any side, who, upon finding good or evil, neither rejoices nor hates—his wisdom is firmly set.
verses.hindi: ।।2.57।। सब जगह आसक्तिरहित हुआ जो मनुष्य उस-उस शुभ-अशुभको प्राप्त करके न तो अभिनन्दित होता है और न द्वेष करता है, उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित है।
verses.wordMeaning: yaḥ—who; sarvatra—in all conditions; anabhisnehaḥ—unattached; tat—that; tat—that; prāpya—attaining; śhubha—good; aśhubham—evil; na—neither; abhinandati—delight in; na—nor; dveṣhṭi—dejected by; tasya—his; prajñā—knowledge; pratiṣhṭhitā—is fixed

verses.sanskrit:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.58।।
verses.transliteration:
yadā sanharate chāyaṁ kūrmo ’ṅgānīva sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
verses.translation: When one is able to draw their senses away from the objects of sense on all sides, like a tortoise draws in its limbs, then their wisdom is firmly established.
verses.hindi: ।।2.58।। जिस तरह कछुआ अपने अङ्गोंको सब ओरसे समेट लेता है, ऐसे ही जिस कालमें यह कर्मयोगी इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंसे इन्द्रियोंको सब प्रकारसे समेट लेता (हटा लेता) है, तब उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित हो जाती है।
verses.wordMeaning: yadā—when; sanharate—withdraw; cha—and; ayam—this; kūrmaḥ—tortoise; aṅgāni—limbs; iva—as; sarvaśhaḥ—fully; indriyāṇi—senses; indriya-arthebhyaḥ—from the sense objects; tasya—his; prajñā—divine wisdom; pratiṣhṭhitā—fixed in

verses.sanskrit:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।

रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते।।2.59।।
verses.transliteration:
viṣhayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ
rasa-varjaṁ raso ’pyasya paraṁ dṛiṣhṭvā nivartate
verses.translation: The objects of the senses, except for the pleasure they bring, turn away from the abstinent dweller in the body. Even the pleasure turns away from him when the Self, which is supreme over the senses, is seen.
verses.hindi: ।।2.59।। निराहारी (इन्द्रियोंको विषयोंसे हटानेवाले) मनुष्यके भी विषय तो निवृत्त हो जाते हैं, पर रस निवृत्त नहीं होता। परन्तु इस स्थितप्रज्ञ मनुष्यका तो रस भी परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव होनेसे निवृत्त हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: viṣhayāḥ—objects for senses; vinivartante—restrain; nirāhārasya—practicing self restraint; dehinaḥ—for the embodied; rasa-varjam—cessation of taste; rasaḥ—taste; api—however; asya—person’s; param—the Supreme; dṛiṣhṭvā—on realization; nivartate—ceases to be

verses.sanskrit:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः।

इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः।।2.60।।
verses.transliteration:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣhasya vipaśhchitaḥ
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṁ manaḥ
verses.translation: The turbulent senses, O Arjuna, can forcibly carry away the mind of even a wise man, though he is ever striving.
verses.hindi: ।।2.60।। हे कुन्तीनन्दन! (रसबुद्धि रहनेसे) यत्न करते हुए विद्वान् मनुष्यकी भी प्रमथनशील इन्द्रियाँ उसके मनको बलपूर्वक हर लेती हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: yatataḥ—while practicing self-control; hi—for; api—even; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; puruṣhasya—of a person; vipaśhchitaḥ—one endowed with discrimination; indriyāṇi—the senses; pramāthīni—turbulent; haranti—carry away; prasabham—forcibly; manaḥ—the mind

verses.sanskrit:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।

वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.61।।
verses.transliteration:
tāni sarvāṇi sanyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ
vaśhe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
verses.translation: Having controlled all the senses, let him remain in contemplation, regarding Me as supreme; for his knowledge is firmly established when his senses are under control.
verses.hindi: ।।2.61।। कर्मयोगी साधक उन सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके मेरे परायण होकर बैठे; क्योंकि जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ वशमें हैं, उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित है।
verses.wordMeaning: tāni—them; sarvāṇi—all; sanyamya—subduing; yuktaḥ—united; āsīta—seated; mat-paraḥ—toward me (Shree Krishna); vaśhe—control; hi—certainly; yasya—whose; indriyāṇi—senses; tasya—their; prajñā—perfect knowledge pratiṣhṭhitā

verses.sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।

सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते।।2.62।।
verses.transliteration:
dhyāyato viṣhayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣhūpajāyate
saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho ’bhijāyate
verses.translation: To one who is thinking about sense-objects, attachment to them arises; from attachment arises desire, and from desire arises anger.
verses.hindi: ।।2.62 -- 2.63।। विषयोंका चिन्तन करनेवाले मनुष्यकी उन विषयोंमें आसक्ति पैदा हो जाती है। आसक्तिसे कामना पैदा होती है। कामनासे क्रोध पैदा होता है। क्रोध होनेपर सम्मोह (मूढ़भाव) हो जाता है। सम्मोहसे स्मृति भ्रष्ट हो जाती है। स्मृति भ्रष्ट होनेपर बुद्धिका नाश हो जाता है। बुद्धिका नाश होनेपर मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: dhyāyataḥ—contemplating; viṣhayān—sense objects; puṁsaḥ—of a person; saṅgaḥ—attachment; teṣhu—to them (sense objects); upajāyate—arises; saṅgāt—from attachment; sañjāyate—develops; kāmaḥ—desire; kāmāt—from desire; krodhaḥ—anger; abhijāyate—arises

verses.sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।

स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति।।2.63।।
verses.transliteration:
krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛiti-vibhramaḥ
smṛiti-bhranśhād buddhi-nāśho buddhi-nāśhāt praṇaśhyati
verses.translation: Anger leads to delusion, which causes the loss of memory; the loss of memory leads to the destruction of discrimination, and with the destruction of discrimination, one is lost.
verses.hindi: ।।2.62 -- 2.63।। विषयोंका चिन्तन करनेवाले मनुष्यकी उन विषयोंमें आसक्ति पैदा हो जाती है। आसक्तिसे कामना पैदा होती है। कामनासे क्रोध पैदा होता है। क्रोध होनेपर सम्मोह (मूढ़भाव) हो जाता है। सम्मोहसे स्मृति भ्रष्ट हो जाती है। स्मृति भ्रष्ट होनेपर बुद्धिका नाश हो जाता है। बुद्धिका नाश होनेपर मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: krodhāt—from anger; bhavati—comes; sammohaḥ—clouding of judgement; sammohāt—from clouding of judgement; smṛiti—memory; vibhramaḥ—bewilderment; smṛiti-bhranśhāt—from bewilderment of memory; buddhi-nāśhaḥ—destruction of intellect; buddhi-nāśhāt—from destruction of intellect; praṇaśhyati—one is ruined

verses.sanskrit:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्।

आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति।।2.64।।
verses.transliteration:
rāga-dveṣha-viyuktais tu viṣhayān indriyaiśh charan
ātma-vaśhyair-vidheyātmā prasādam adhigachchhati
verses.translation: But he who goes through the sense-objects with the senses free from love and hate, disciplined and controlled, attains serenity.
verses.hindi: ।।2.64 -- 2.65।। वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाला कर्मयोगी साधक रागद्वेषसे रहित अपने वशमें की हुई इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता हुआ अन्तःकरणकी निर्मलता को प्राप्त हो जाता है। निर्मलता प्राप्त होनेपर साधकके सम्पूर्ण दुःखोंका नाश हो जाता है और ऐसे शुद्ध चित्तवाले साधककी बुद्धि निःसन्देह बहुत जल्दी परमात्मामें स्थिर हो जाती है।
verses.wordMeaning: rāga—attachment; dveṣha—aversion; viyuktaiḥ—free; tu—but; viṣhayān—objects of the senses; indriyaiḥ—by the senses; charan—while using; ātma-vaśhyaiḥ—controlling one’s mind; vidheya-ātmā—one who controls the mind; prasādam—the Grace of God; adhigachchhati—attains

verses.sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।

प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते।।2.65।।
verses.transliteration:
prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṁ hānir asyopajāyate
prasanna-chetaso hyāśhu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣhṭhate
verses.translation: In that serenity, all sorrow is lost; for in the case of the person with a serene mind, the Buddhi is quickly established.
verses.hindi: ।।2.64 -- 2.65।। वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाला कर्मयोगी साधक रागद्वेषसे रहित अपने वशमें की हुई इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता हुआ अन्तःकरणकी निर्मलता को प्राप्त हो जाता है। निर्मलता प्राप्त होनेपर साधकके सम्पूर्ण दुःखोंका नाश हो जाता है और ऐसे शुद्ध चित्तवाले साधककी बुद्धि निःसन्देह बहुत जल्दी परमात्मामें स्थिर हो जाती है।
verses.wordMeaning: prasāde—by divine grace; sarva—all; duḥkhānām—of sorrows; hāniḥ—destruction; asya—his; upajāyate—comes; prasanna-chetasaḥ—with a tranquil mind; hi—indeed; āśhu—soon; buddhiḥ—intellect; paryavatiṣhṭhate—becomes firmly established

verses.sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज | अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja | ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
verses.translation: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.
verses.hindi: सभी धर्मों (कर्तव्यों) को छोड़कर मेरी ही शरण में आओ। मैं तुम्हें सम्पूर्ण पापों से मुक्त कर दूँगा, तुम शोक न करो।
verses.wordMeaning: The culminating message of the entire Gita. Krishna asks for complete surrender (śaraṇāgati). He promises liberation from all sins to those who take refuge in Him alone.
verses.commentary: The culminating message of the entire Gita. Krishna asks for complete surrender (śaraṇāgati). He promises liberation from all sins to those who take refuge in Him alone.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।

तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।2.67।।
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇāṁ hi charatāṁ yan mano ’nuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi
verses.translation: For, when the mind follows the senses, experiencing their objects, his understanding is carried away by them, just as the wind carries away a ship on the waters.
verses.hindi: ।।2.67।। अपने-अपने विषयोंमें विचरती हुई इन्द्रियोंमेंसे एक ही इन्द्रिय जिस मनको अपना अनुगामी बना लेती है, वह अकेला मन जलमें नौकाको वायुकी तरह इसकी बुद्धिको हर लेता है।
verses.wordMeaning: indriyāṇām—of the senses; hi—indeed; charatām—roaming; yat—which; manaḥ—the mind; anuvidhīyate—becomes constantly engaged; tat—that; asya—of that; harati—carries away; prajñām—intellect; vāyuḥ—wind; nāvam—boat; iva—as; ambhasi—on the water

verses.sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.68।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛihītāni sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
verses.translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, he whose senses are restrained from going after their objects on all sides, his wisdom is firmly established.
verses.hindi: ।।2.68।। इसलिये हे महाबाहो ! जिस मनुष्यकी इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंसे सर्वथा निगृहीत (वशमें की हुई) हैं, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है।
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—therefore; yasya—whose; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed one; nigṛihītāni—restrained; sarvaśhaḥ—completely; indriyāṇi—senses; indriya-arthebhyaḥ—from sense objects; tasya—of that person; prajñā—transcendental knowledge; pratiṣhṭhitā—remains fixed

verses.sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।

यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।
verses.transliteration:
yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ
verses.translation: What is night for all beings, in it the one who is controlled is awake; when all beings are awake, that is the night for the sage who sees.
verses.hindi: ।।2.69।। सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों की जो रात (परमात्मासे विमुखता) है, उसमें संयमी मनुष्य जागता है, और जिसमें सब प्राणी जागते हैं (भोग और संग्रहमें लगे रहते हैं), वह तत्त्वको जाननेवाले मुनिकी दृष्टिमें रात है।
verses.wordMeaning: yā—which; niśhā—night; sarva-bhūtānām—of all living beings; tasyām—in that; jāgarti—is awake; sanyamī—self-controlled; yasyām—in which; jāgrati—are awake; bhūtāni—creatures; sā—that; niśhā—night; paśhyataḥ—see; muneḥ—sage

verses.sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं

समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।

तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे

स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।
verses.transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣhṭhaṁ
samudram āpaḥ praviśhanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśhanti sarve
sa śhāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī
verses.translation: He into whom all desires enter, just as the waters enter the full and undisturbed sea, attains peace, and not he who longs after objects of desire.
verses.hindi: ।।2.70।। जैसे सम्पूर्ण नदियोंका जल चारों ओरसे जलद्वारा परिपूर्ण समुद्रमें आकर मिलता है, पर समुद्र अपनी मर्यादामें अचल प्रतिष्ठित रहता है ऐसे ही सम्पूर्ण भोग-पदार्थ जिस संयमी मनुष्य को विकार उत्पन्न किये बिना ही उसको प्राप्त होते हैं, वही मनुष्य परमशान्तिको प्राप्त होता है, भोगोंकी कामनावाला नहीं।
verses.wordMeaning: āpūryamāṇam—filled from all sides; achala-pratiṣhṭham—undisturbed; samudram—ocean; āpaḥ—waters; praviśhanti—enter; yadvat—as; tadvat—likewise; kāmāḥ—desires; yam—whom; praviśhanti—enter; sarve—all; saḥ—that person; śhāntim—peace; āpnoti—attains; na—not; kāma-kāmī—one who strives to satisfy desires

verses.sanskrit:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।

निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।
verses.transliteration:
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānśh charati niḥspṛihaḥ
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sa śhāntim adhigachchhati
verses.translation: The one who, abandoning all desires, abides without longing, possession, and the sense of 'I' and 'mine', wins peace.
verses.hindi: ।।2.71।। जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका त्याग करके स्पृहारहित, ममतारहित और अहंकाररहित होकर आचरण करता है, वह शान्तिको प्राप्त होता है।
verses.wordMeaning: vihāya—giving up; kāmān—material desires; yaḥ—who; sarvān—all; pumān—a person; charati—lives; niḥspṛihaḥ—free from hankering; nirmamaḥ—without a sense of proprietorship; nirahankāraḥ—without egoism; saḥ—that person; śhāntim—perfect peace; adhigachchhati—attains

verses.sanskrit:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।

स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति।।2.72।।
verses.transliteration:
eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyām anta-kāle ’pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛichchhati
verses.translation: This is the Brahmic state, O Arjuna. No one attaining to this is deluded. By abiding in this state even at the hour of death, one will attain the Self.
verses.hindi: ।।2.72।। हे पृथानन्दन ! यह ब्राह्मी स्थिति है। इसको प्राप्त होकर कभी कोई मोहित नहीं होता। इस स्थितिमें यदि अन्तकालमें भी स्थित हो जाय, तो निर्वाण (शान्त) ब्रह्मकी प्राप्ति हो जाती है।
verses.wordMeaning: eṣhā—such; brāhmī sthitiḥ—state of God-realization; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; na—never; enām—this; prāpya—having attained; vimuhyati—is deluded; sthitvā—being established; asyām—in this; anta-kāle—at the hour of death; api—even; brahma-nirvāṇam—liberation from Maya; ṛichchhati—attains

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.transliteration: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
verses.hindi: अपने स्वधर्म में मरना भला है, चाहे वह अपूर्ण हो; परधर्म को अच्छी तरह से करना भयावह है।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.
verses.commentary: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.

verses.sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः | स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||
verses.transliteration: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||
verses.translation: Whatever a great man does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
verses.hindi: जो-जो आचरण श्रेष्ठ पुरुष करता है, अन्य लोग भी वही करते हैं। वह जो प्रमाण स्थापित करता है, संसार उसी का अनुसरण करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.
verses.commentary: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।

तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।3.9।।
verses.transliteration:
yajñārthāt karmaṇo ’nyatra loko ’yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ
tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samāchara
verses.translation: This world is held in the bondage of work only when work is not performed as a sacrifice. O Arjuna, you must perform work for this purpose, free from attachment.
verses.hindi: ।।3.9।। यज्ञ (कर्तव्यपालन) के लिये किये जानेवाले कर्मोंसे अन्यत्र (अपने लिये किये जानेवाले) कर्मोंमें लगा हुआ यह मनुष्य-समुदाय कर्मोंसे बँधता है, इसलिये हे कुन्तीनन्दन ! तू आसक्ति-रहित होकर उस यज्ञके लिये ही कर्तव्य-कर्म कर।
verses.wordMeaning: yajña-arthāt—for the sake of sacrifice; karmaṇaḥ—than action; anyatra—else; lokaḥ—material world; ayam—this; karma-bandhanaḥ—bondage through one’s work; tat—that; artham—for the sake of; karma—action; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; mukta-saṅgaḥ—free from attachment; samāchara—perform properly

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।

तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।3.12।।
verses.transliteration:
iṣhṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
verses.translation: The gods, pleased by the sacrifice, will bestow upon you the enjoyments you desire. He who enjoys the bounty of the gods without giving them anything in return is but a thief.
verses.hindi: ।।3.12।। यज्ञसे भावित (पुष्ट) हुए देवता भी तुमलोगोंको (बिना माँगे ही) कर्तव्य-पालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री देते रहेंगे। इस प्रकार उन देवताओंसे प्राप्त हुई सामग्रीको दूसरोंकी सेवामें लगाये बिना जो मनुष्य स्वयं ही उसका उपभोग करता है, वह चोर ही है।
verses.wordMeaning: iṣhṭān—desired; bhogān—necessities of life; hi—certainly; vaḥ—unto you; devāḥ—the celestial gods; dāsyante—will grant; yajña-bhāvitāḥ—satisfied by sacrifice; taiḥ—by them; dattān—things granted; apradāya—without offering; ebhyaḥ—to them; yaḥ—who; bhuṅkte—enjoys; stenaḥ—thieves; eva—verily; saḥ—they

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।

अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।3.16।।
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ pravartitaṁ chakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati
verses.translation: He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here, lives in sin, satisfying the senses, O Arjuna; he lives in vain.
verses.hindi: ।।3.16।। हे पार्थ! जो मनुष्य इस लोकमें इस प्रकार परम्परासे प्रचलित सृष्टिचक्रके अनुसार नहीं चलता, वह इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा भोगोंमें रमण करनेवाला अघायु (पापमय जीवन बितानेवाला) मनुष्य संसारमें व्यर्थ ही जीता है।
verses.wordMeaning: evam—thus; pravartitam—set into motion; chakram—cycle; na—not; anuvartayati—follow; iha—in this life; yaḥ—who; agha-āyuḥ—sinful living; indriya-ārāmaḥ—for the delight of their senses; mogham—vainly; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; saḥ—they; jīvati—live

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।

न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।3.18।।
verses.transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛitenārtho nākṛiteneha kaśhchana
na chāsya sarva-bhūteṣhu kaśhchid artha-vyapāśhrayaḥ
verses.translation: He has no purpose to gain from work done or left undone, nor does he have to rely on any end.
verses.hindi: ।।3.18।। उस (कर्मयोगसे सिद्ध हुए) महापुरुषका इस संसारमें न तो कर्म करनेसे कोई प्रयोजन रहता है, और न कर्म न करनेसे ही कोई प्रयोजन रहता है, तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें (किसी भी प्राणीके साथ) इसका किञ्चिन्मात्र भी स्वार्थका सम्बन्ध नहीं रहता।
verses.wordMeaning: na—not; eva—indeed; tasya—his; kṛitena—by discharge of duty; arthaḥ—gain; na—not; akṛitena—without discharge of duty; iha—here; kaśhchana—whatsoever; na—never; cha—and; asya—of that person; sarva-bhūteṣhu—among all living beings; kaśhchit—any; artha—necessity; vyapāśhrayaḥ—to depend upon

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।3.23।।
verses.transliteration:
yadi hyahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣhyāḥ pārtha sarvaśhaḥ
verses.translation: If I did not continue to work unweariedly, O Arjuna, people would follow my path.
verses.hindi: ।।3.23 -- 3.24।।  हे पार्थ! अगर मैं किसी समय सावधान होकर कर्तव्यकर्म न करूँ तो बड़ी हानि हो जाय; क्योंकि मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही मार्गका अनुसरण करते हैं। यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये सब मनुष्य नष्ट-भ्रष्ट हो जायँ और मैं वर्णसंकरताको करनेवाला होऊँ तथा इस समस्त प्रजाको नष्ट करनेवाला बनूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: yadi—if; hi—certainly; aham—I; na—not; varteyam—thus engage; jātu—ever; karmaṇi—in the performance of prescribed duties; atandritaḥ—carefully; mama—my; vartma—path; anuvartante—follow; manuṣhyāḥ—all men; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; sarvaśhaḥ—in all respects

verses.sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।

सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः।।3.24।।
verses.transliteration:
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ched aham
sankarasya cha kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
verses.translation: If I do not do the work, these people will be lost; and I will be causing chaos in life and thereby ruining all these people.
verses.hindi: ।।3.23 -- 3.24।।  हे पार्थ ! अगर मैं किसी समय सावधान होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म न करूँ (तो बड़ी हानि हो जाय; क्योंकि) मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही मार्गका अनुसरण करते हैं। यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये सब मनुष्य नष्ट-भ्रष्ट हो जायँ और मैं वर्णसंकरताको करनेवाला  तथा इस समस्त प्रजाको नष्ट करनेवाला बनूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: utsīdeyuḥ—would perish; ime—all these; lokāḥ—worlds; na—not; kuryām—I perform; karma—prescribed duties; chet—if; aham—I; sankarasya—of uncultured population; cha—and; kartā—responsible; syām—would be; upahanyām—would destroy; imāḥ—all these; prajāḥ—living entities

verses.sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।

कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्।।3.25।।
verses.transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvānso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryād vidvāns tathāsaktaśh chikīrṣhur loka-saṅgraham
verses.translation: Just as the ignorant, attached to their work, act, O Arjuna, so too the learned should act without any attachment, and only for the welfare of the world.
verses.hindi: ।।3.25 -- 3.26।। हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन! कर्ममें आसक्त हुए अज्ञानीजन जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं, आसक्तिरहित विद्वान भी लोकसंग्रह करना चाहता हुआ उसी प्रकार कर्म करे।  तत्त्वज्ञ महापुरुष कर्मोंमें आसक्तिवाले अज्ञानी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धिमें भ्रम उत्पन्न न करे, प्रत्युत स्वयं समस्त कर्मोंको अच्छी तरहसे करता हुआ उनसे भी वैसे ही करवाये।
verses.wordMeaning: saktāḥ—attached; karmaṇi—duties; avidvānsaḥ—the ignorant; yathā—as much as; kurvanti—act; bhārata—scion of Bharat (Arjun); kuryāt—should do; vidvān—the wise; tathā—thus; asaktaḥ—unattached; chikīrṣhuḥ—wishing; loka-saṅgraham—welfare of the world

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।

तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्।।3.29।।
verses.transliteration:
prakṛiter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu
tān akṛitsna-vido mandān kṛitsna-vin na vichālayet
verses.translation: Those who are deluded by the Gunas of Prakrti are attached to the works of the Gunas. But he who knows the whole truth should not disturb the ignorant who do not know the whole truth.
verses.hindi: ।।3.29।। प्रकृतिजन्य गुणोंसे अत्यन्त मोहित हुए अज्ञानी मनुष्य गुणों और कर्मोंमें आसक्त रहते हैं। उन पूर्णतया न समझनेवाले मन्दबुद्धि अज्ञानियोंको पूर्णतया जाननेवाला ज्ञानी मनुष्य विचलित न करे।
verses.wordMeaning: prakṛiteḥ—of material nature; guṇa—by the modes of material nature; sammūḍhāḥ—deluded; sajjante—become attached; guṇa-karmasu—to results of actions; tān—those; akṛitsna-vidaḥ—persons without knowledge; mandān—the ignorant; kṛitsna-vit—persons with knowledge; na vichālayet—should not unsettle

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One.
verses.hindi: आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूर्य उदय हों तो जो प्रकाश हो, वह उस महात्मा (विश्वरूप) के तेज के समान होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।

प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति।।3.33।।
verses.transliteration:
sadṛiśhaṁ cheṣhṭate svasyāḥ prakṛiter jñānavān api
prakṛitiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣhyati
verses.translation: Even the man of knowledge acts according to his nature; all beings follow their own nature. What will repression accomplish?
verses.hindi: ।।3.33।। सम्पूर्ण प्राणी प्रकृतिको प्राप्त होते हैं। ज्ञानी महापुरुष भी अपनी प्रकृतिके अनुसार चेष्टा करता है। फिर इसमें किसीका हठ क्या करेगा?
verses.wordMeaning: sadṛiśham—accordingly; cheṣhṭate—act; svasyāḥ—by their own; prakṛiteḥ—modes of nature; jñāna-vān—the wise; api—even; prakṛitim—nature; yānti—follow; bhūtāni—all living beings; nigrahaḥ—repression; kim—what; kariṣhyati—will do

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यतां गतं पार्थ मायया ते तदात्मकम् | यत्तु सत्यं सनातनं तदहं वदतः स्म ते ||
verses.transliteration: adṛśyatāṃ gataṃ pārtha māyayā te tadātmakam | yattu satyaṃ sanātanaṃ tadahaṃ vadataḥ sma te ||
verses.translation: O Partha, the cosmic form you saw was manifested by My Yoga-Maya. Now I shall reveal to you My eternal form.
verses.hindi: हे पार्थ! जो तुमने देखा वह मेरी योगमाया से प्रकट किया गया था। अब मैं तुम्हें अपना शाश्वत रूप बताता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.
verses.commentary: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।

अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः।।3.36।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
atha kena prayukto ’yaṁ pāpaṁ charati pūruṣhaḥ
anichchhann api vārṣhṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ
verses.translation: Arjuna said, "But, O Krsna, what impels one to commit sin, even against their own will, as if constrained by force?"
verses.hindi: ।।3.36।। अर्जुन बोले - हे वार्ष्णेय ! फिर यह मनुष्य न चाहता हुआ भी जबर्दस्ती लगाये हुएकी तरह किससे प्रेरित होकर पापका आचरण करता है?
verses.wordMeaning: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; atha—then; kena—by what; prayuktaḥ—impelled; ayam—one; pāpam—sins; charati—commit; pūruṣhaḥ—a person; anichchhan—unwillingly; api—even; vārṣhṇeya—he who belongs to the Vrishni clan, Shree Krishna; balāt—by force; iva—as if; niyojitaḥ—engaged

verses.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।

महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्।।3.37।।
verses.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
kāma eṣha krodha eṣha rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśhano mahā-pāpmā viddhyenam iha vairiṇam
verses.translation: The Lord said, "It is desire, it is wrath, born of the guna of rajas; it is a great devourer, an impeller of sin. Know this to be the enemy here."
verses.hindi: ।।3.37।। श्रीभगवान् बोले - रजोगुणसे उत्पन्न हुआ  यह काम ही क्रोध  है। यह बहुत खानेवाला और महापापी है। इस विषयमें तू इसको ही वैरी जान।
verses.wordMeaning: śhri-bhagavān uvācha—the Supreme Lord said; kāmaḥ—desire; eṣhaḥ—this; krodhaḥ—wrath; eṣhaḥ—this; rajaḥ-guṇa—the mode of passion; samudbhavaḥ—born of; mahā-aśhanaḥ—all-devouring; mahā-pāpmā—greatly sinful; viddhi—know; enam—this; iha—in the material world; vairiṇam—the enemy

verses.sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ | ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ||
verses.transliteration: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
verses.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same — then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.
verses.hindi: सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि और जय-पराजय को समान करके तब युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो। इस प्रकार तुम पाप नहीं प्राप्त करोगे।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).

verses.sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।

कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च।।3.39।।
verses.transliteration:
āvṛitaṁ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣhpūreṇānalena cha
verses.translation: The knowledge of the intelligent self is enveloped by this constant enemy, O Arjuna, which is of the nature of desire and is difficult to gratify and insatiable.
verses.hindi: ।।3.39।। और हे कुन्तीनन्दन ! इस अग्निके समान कभी तृप्त न होनेवाले और विवेकियोंके नित्य वैरी इस कामके द्वारा मनुष्यका विवेक ढका हुआ है।
verses.wordMeaning: āvṛitam—covered; jñānam—knowledge; etena—by this; jñāninaḥ—of the wise; nitya-vairiṇā—by the perpetual enemy; kāma-rūpeṇa—in the form of desires; kaunteya—Arjun the son of Kunti; duṣhpūreṇa—insatiable; analena—like fire; cha—and

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।

एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्।।3.40।।
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣhṭhānam uchyate
etair vimohayatyeṣha jñānam āvṛitya dehinam
verses.translation: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its instruments; by these, it overpowers the embodied self, enveloping its knowledge.
verses.hindi: ।।3.40।। इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि इस कामके वास-स्थान कहे गये हैं। यह काम इन- (इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि-) के द्वारा ज्ञानको ढककर देहाभिमानी मनुष्यको मोहित करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: indriyāṇi—the senses; manaḥ—the mind; buddhiḥ—the intellect; asya—of this; adhiṣhṭhānam—dwelling place; uchyate—are said to be; etaiḥ—by these; vimohayati—deludes; eṣhaḥ—this; jñānam—knowledge; āvṛitya—clouds; dehinam—the embodied soul

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।

पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्।।3.41।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣhabha
pāpmānaṁ prajahi hyenaṁ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśhanam
verses.translation: Therefore, O Arjuna, control your senses from the outset and slay this sinful thing that destroys both knowledge and discernment.
verses.hindi: ।।3.41।। इसलिये हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन ! तू सबसे पहले इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके इस ज्ञान और विज्ञानका नाश करनेवाले महान् पापी कामको अवश्य ही बलपूर्वक मार डाल।
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—therefore; tvam—you; indriyāṇi—senses; ādau—in the very beginning; niyamya—having controlled; bharata-ṛiṣhabha—Arjun, the best of the Bharatas; pāpmānam—the sinful; prajahi—slay; hi—certainly; enam—this; jñāna—knowledge; vijñāna—realization; nāśhanam—the destroyer

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।

जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्।।3.43।।
verses.transliteration:
evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā sanstabhyātmānam ātmanā
jahi śhatruṁ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṁ durāsadam
verses.translation: Thus, knowing that which is higher than the intellect and fixing the mind with the help of the intellect in Karma Yoga, O Arjuna, slay this enemy which takes the form of desire, and which is difficult to overcome.
verses.hindi: ।।3.42 -- 3.43।। इन्द्रियोंको (स्थूलशरीरसे) पर (श्रेष्ठ, सबल, प्रकाशक, व्यापक तथा सूक्ष्म) कहते हैं। इन्द्रियोंसे पर मन है, मनसे भी पर बुद्धि है औऱ जो बुद्धिसे भी पर है वह (काम) है। इस तरह बुद्धिसे पर - (काम-) को जानकर अपने द्वारा अपने-आपको वशमें करके हे महाबाहो ! तू इस कामरूप दुर्जय शत्रुको मार डाल।
verses.wordMeaning: evam—thus; buddheḥ—than the intellect; param—superior; buddhvā—knowing; sanstabhya—subdue; ātmānam—the lower self (senses, mind, and intellect); ātmanā—by higher self (soul); jahi—kill; śhatrum—the enemy; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed one; kāma-rūpam—in the form of desire; durāsadam—formidable

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, O Bharata, I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: हे भारत! जब-जब धर्म की हानि और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपने आपको प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna promises divine intervention whenever dharma weakens. This verse is the foundation of the doctrine of divine avataras.
verses.commentary: Krishna promises divine intervention whenever dharma weakens. This verse is the foundation of the doctrine of divine avataras.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत | श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ||
verses.transliteration: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhāḥ sa eva saḥ ||
verses.translation: The faith of each person, O Bharata, accords with their natural disposition. A person is made of their faith; what their faith is, that, verily, they are.
verses.hindi: हे भारत! प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की श्रद्धा उसके स्वभाव (सत्त्व) के अनुसार होती है। यह पुरुष श्रद्धामय है — जैसी श्रद्धा, वैसा पुरुष।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."
verses.commentary: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।

कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति।।4.4।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ
katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti
verses.translation: Arjuna said, "Your birth was later, and Vivasvan's birth was earlier. How then can I understand that you taught it in the beginning?"
verses.hindi: ।।4.4।। अर्जुन बोले - आपका जन्म तो अभीका है और सूर्यका जन्म बहुत पुराना है; अतः आपने ही सृष्टिके आदिमें सूर्यसे यह योग कहा था - यह बात मैं कैसे समझूँ?
verses.wordMeaning: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; aparam—later; bhavataḥ—your; janma—birth; param—prior; janma—birth; vivasvataḥ—Vivasvan, the sun-god; katham—how; etat—this; vijānīyām—am I to understand; tvam—you; ādau—in the beginning; proktavān—taught; iti—thus

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।

त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन।।4.9।।
verses.transliteration:
janma karma cha me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so ’rjuna
verses.translation: He who thus knows in truth My divine birth and actions does not get rebirth after leaving the body; he will come to Me, O Arjuna.
verses.hindi: ।।4.9।। हे अर्जुन ! मेरे जन्म और कर्म दिव्य हैं। इस प्रकार (मेरे जन्म और कर्मको) जो मनुष्य तत्त्वसे जान लेता अर्थात् दृढ़तापूर्वक मान लेता है, वह शरीरका त्याग करके पुनर्जन्मको प्राप्त नहीं होता, प्रत्युत मुझे प्राप्त होता है।
verses.wordMeaning: janma—birth; karma—activities; cha—and; me—of mine; divyam—divine; evam—thus; yaḥ—who; vetti—know; tattvataḥ—in truth; tyaktvā—having abandoned; deham—the body; punaḥ—again; janma—birth; na—never; eti—takes; mām—to me; eti—comes; saḥ—he; arjuna—Arjun

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः।

क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा।।4.12।।
verses.transliteration:
kāṅkṣhantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣhipraṁ hi mānuṣhe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā
verses.translation: Those who desire the fruits of their ritualistic acts, sacrifice to the gods here; for, success quickly accrues in the world of men.
verses.hindi: ।।4.12।। कर्मोंकी सिद्धि (फल) चाहनेवाले मनुष्य देवताओंकी उपासना किया करते हैं; क्योंकि इस मनुष्यलोकमें कर्मोंसे उत्पन्न होनेवाली सिद्धि जल्दी मिल जाती है।
verses.wordMeaning: kāṅkṣhantaḥ—desiring; karmaṇām—material activities; siddhim—success; yajante—worship; iha—in this world; devatāḥ—the celestial gods; kṣhipram—quickly; hi—certainly; mānuṣhe—in human society; loke—within this world; siddhiḥ—rewarding; bhavati—manifest; karma-jā—from material activities

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः।

तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।4.16।।
verses.transliteration:
kiṁ karma kim akarmeti kavayo ’pyatra mohitāḥ
tat te karma pravakṣhyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣhyase ’śhubhāt
verses.translation: What is action? What is non-action? Even the wise are puzzled in respect of these. I shall declare to you that kind of action, knowing which you will be freed from evil.
verses.hindi: ।।4.16।। कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है -- इस प्रकार इस विषयमें विद्वान् भी मोहित हो जाते हैं। अतः वह कर्म-तत्त्व मैं तुम्हें भलीभाँति कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर तू अशुभ- (संसार-बन्धन-) से मुक्त हो जायगा।
verses.wordMeaning: kim—what; karma—action; kim—what; akarma—inaction; iti—thus; kavayaḥ—the wise; api—even; atra—in this; mohitāḥ—are confused; tat—that; te—to you; karma—action; pravakṣhyāmi—I shall explain; yat—which; jñātvā—knowing; mokṣhyase—you may free yourself; aśhubhāt—from inauspiciousness

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।

स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्।।4.18।।
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśhyed akarmaṇi cha karma yaḥ
sa buddhimān manuṣhyeṣhu sa yuktaḥ kṛitsna-karma-kṛit
verses.translation: He who sees inaction in action and also action in inaction is wise among men. He is fit for release and has accomplished all actions.
verses.hindi: ।।4.18।। जो मनुष्य कर्ममें अकर्म देखता है और जो अकर्ममें कर्म देखता है, वह मनुष्योंमें बुद्धिमान् है,  योगी है और सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको करनेवाला  है।
verses.wordMeaning: karmaṇi—action; akarma—in inaction; yaḥ—who; paśhyet—see; akarmaṇi—inaction; cha—also; karma—action; yaḥ—who; saḥ—they; buddhi-mān—wise; manuṣhyeṣhu—amongst humans; saḥ—they; yuktaḥ—yogis; kṛitsna-karma-kṛit—performers all kinds of actions

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः।

यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते।।4.23।।
verses.transliteration:
gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-chetasaḥ
yajñāyācharataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate
verses.translation: One whose attachments have been relinquished, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who works only for sacrifices—their Karma is entirely dissolved.
verses.hindi: ।।4.23।। जिसकी आसक्ति सर्वथा मिट गयी है, जो मुक्त हो गया है, जिसकी बुद्धि स्वरूपके ज्ञानमें स्थित है, ऐसे केवल यज्ञके लिये कर्म करनेवाले मनुष्यके सम्पूर्ण कर्म विलीन हो जाते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: gata-saṅgasya—free from material attachments; muktasya—of the liberated; jñāna-avasthita—established in divine knowledge; chetasaḥ—whose intellect; yajñāya—as a sacrifice (to God); ācharataḥ—performing; karma—action; samagram—completely; pravilīyate—are freed

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।

ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना।।4.24।।
verses.transliteration:
brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahma-karma-samādhinā
verses.translation: Brahman is the instrument with which to offer; Brahman is the oblation. By Brahman is the oblation offered into the fire of Brahman; Brahman alone is to be attained by one who meditates on Him in their works.
verses.hindi: ।।4.24।। जिस यज्ञमें अर्पण भी ब्रह्म है, हवी भी ब्रह्म है और ब्रह्मरूप कर्ताके द्वारा ब्रह्मरूप अग्निमें आहुति देनारूप क्रिया भी ब्रह्म है, (ऐसे यज्ञको करनेवाले) जिस मनुष्यकी ब्रह्ममें ही कर्म-समाधि हो गयी है, उसके द्वारा प्राप्त करनेयोग्य फल भी ब्रह्म ही है।
verses.wordMeaning: brahma—Brahman; arpaṇam—the ladle and other offerings; brahma—Brahman; haviḥ—the oblation; brahma—Brahman; agnau—in the sacrificial fire; brahmaṇā—by that person; hutam—offered; brahma—Brahman; eva—certainly; tena—by that; gantavyam—to be attained; brahma—Brahman; karma—offering; samādhinā—those completely absorbed in God-consciousness

verses.sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते।

ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति।।4.25।।
verses.transliteration:
daivam evāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati
verses.translation: Some yogis resort only to the sacrifice relating to gods; others offer sacrifice into the fire of Brahman solely through sacrifice.
verses.hindi: ।।4.25।। अन्य योगीलोग भगवदर्पणरूप यज्ञका ही अनुष्ठान करते हैं और दूसरे योगीलोग ब्रह्मरूप अग्निमें विचाररूप यज्ञके द्वारा ही जीवात्मारूप यज्ञका हवन करते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: daivam—the celestial gods; eva—indeed; apare—others; yajñam—sacrifice; yoginaḥ—spiritual practioners; paryupāsate—worship; brahma—of the Supreme Truth; agnau—in the fire; apare—others; yajñam—sacrifice; yajñena—by sacrifice; eva—indeed; upajuhvati—offer

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे।

प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः।।4.29।।
verses.transliteration:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe ’pānaṁ tathāpare
prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ
 apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣhu juhvati
sarve ’pyete yajña-vido yajña-kṣhapita-kalmaṣhāḥ
verses.translation: Others, with restricted diets, are devoted to the control of breath. Some sacrifice the inward breath in the outward breath; similarly, others sacrifice the outward breath in the inward breath. Some others, stopping the flow of both the inward and outward breaths, sacrifice the inward and outward breaths.
verses.hindi: ।।4.29 -- 4.30।। दूसरे कितने ही प्राणायामके परायण हुए योगीलोग अपानमें प्राणका पूरक करके, प्राण और अपानकी गति रोककर फिर प्राणमें अपानका हवन करते हैं; तथा अन्य कितने ही नियमित आहार करनेवाले प्राणोंका प्राणोंमें हवन किया करते हैं। ये सभी साधक यज्ञोंद्वारा पापोंका नाश करनेवाले और यज्ञोंको जाननेवाले हैं।
verses.wordMeaning:
apāne—the incoming breath; juhvati—offer; prāṇam—the outgoing breath; prāṇe—in the outgoing breath; apānam—incoming breath; tathā—also; apare—others; prāṇa—of the outgoing breath; apāna—and the incoming breath; gatī—movement; ruddhvā—blocking; prāṇa-āyāma—control of breath; parāyaṇāḥ—wholly devoted
 apare—others; niyata—having controlled; āhārāḥ—food intake; prāṇān—life-breaths; prāṇeṣhu—life-energy; juhvati—sacrifice; sarve—all; api—also; ete—these; yajña-vidaḥ—knowers of sacrifices; yajña-kṣhapita—being cleansed by performances of sacrifices; kalmaṣhāḥ—of impurities

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
