What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."
verses.commentary: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः।

सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च।।10.4।।
verses.transliteration:
buddhir jñānam asammohaḥ kṣhamā satyaṁ damaḥ śhamaḥ
sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhavo ’bhāvo bhayaṁ chābhayameva cha
verses.translation: Intelligence, knowledge, non-delusion, forbearance, truth, restraint, self-control, pleasure, pain, exaltation, and depression, fear, and fearlessness;
verses.hindi: ।।10.4 -- 10.5।। बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश -- प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलग-अलग (बीस) भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: buddhiḥ—intellect; jñānam—knowledge; asammohaḥ—clarity of thought; kṣhamā—forgiveness; satyam—truthfulness; damaḥ—control over the senses; śhamaḥ—control of the mind; sukham—joy; duḥkham—sorrow; bhavaḥ—birth; abhāvaḥ—death; bhayam—fear; cha—and; abhayam—courage; eva—certainly; cha—and;

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit:
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम्।

कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च।।10.9।।
verses.transliteration:
mach-chittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam
kathayantaśh cha māṁ nityaṁ tuṣhyanti cha ramanti cha
verses.translation: With their minds focused on Me, their pranas centered in Me, inspiring one another and always speaking of Me, they live in contentment and bliss at all times.
verses.hindi: ।।10.9।।। मेरेमें चित्तवाले, मेरेमें प्राणोंको अर्पण करनेवाले भक्तजन आपसमें मेरे गुण, प्रभाव आदिको जानते हुए और उनका कथन करते हुए ही नित्य-निरन्तर सन्तुष्ट रहते हैं और मेरेमें प्रेम करते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: mat-chittāḥ—those with minds fixed on me; mat-gata-prāṇāḥ—those who have surrendered their lives to me; bodhayantaḥ—enlightening (with divine knowledge of God); parasparam—one another; kathayantaḥ—speaking; cha—and; mām—about me; nityam—continously; tuṣhyanti—satisfaction; cha—and; ramanti—(they) delight; cha—also

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान्।

पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम्।।10.12।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān
puruṣhaṁ śhāśhvataṁ divyam ādi-devam ajaṁ vibhum
verses.translation: Arjuna said, "You are the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Light, and the Supreme Sanctifier. All the seers proclaim You as the eternal, divine Person, the Primal Lord, the unborn, and all-pervading. So too do the divine sages Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa proclaim. You Yourself also proclaim this."
verses.hindi: ।।10.12 -- 10.12।। अर्जुन बोले -- परम ब्रह्म, परम धाम और महान् पवित्र आप ही हैं। आप शाश्वत, दिव्य पुरुष, आदिदेव, अजन्मा और विभु (व्यापक) हैं -- ऐसा सब-के-सब ऋषि, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल तथा व्यास कहते हैं और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति कहते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; param—Supreme; brahma—Brahman; param—Supreme; dhāma—Abode; pavitram—purifier; paramam—Supreme; bhavān—you; puruṣham—personality; śhāśhvatam—Eternal; divyam—Divine; ādi-devam—the Primal Being; ajam—the Unborn; vibhum—the Great;

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः।

याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि।।10.16।।
verses.transliteration:
vaktum arhasyaśheṣheṇa divyā hyātma-vibhūtayaḥ
yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṁs tvaṁ vyāpya tiṣhṭhasi
verses.translation: You should tell Me without reserve Your divine manifestations where You abide, pervading all these worlds.
verses.hindi: ।।10.16।।  जिन विभूतियोंसे आप इन सम्पूर्ण लोकोंको व्याप्त करके स्थित हैं, उन सभी अपनी दिव्य विभूतियोंका सम्पूर्णतासे वर्णन करनेमें आप ही समर्थ हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: vaktum—to describe; arhasi—please do; aśheṣheṇa—completely; divyāḥ—divine; hi—indeed; ātma—your own; vibhūtayaḥ—opulences; yābhiḥ—by which; vibhūtibhiḥ—opulences; lokān—all worlds; imān—these; tvam—you; vyāpya—pervade; tiṣhṭhasi—reside;

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन।

भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम्।।10.18।।
verses.transliteration:
vistareṇātmano yogaṁ vibhūtiṁ cha janārdana
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛiptir hi śhṛiṇvato nāsti me ’mṛitam
verses.translation: Speak to me again in full, O Krishna, about Your attributes and glories. For I am not sated by hearing Your ambrosial words.
verses.hindi: ।।10.18।। हे जनार्दन ! आप अपने योग (सामर्थ्य) को और विभूतियोंको विस्तारसे फिर कहिये; क्योंकि आपके अमृतमय वचन सुनते-सुनते मेरी तृप्ति नहीं हो रही है।
verses.wordMeaning: vistareṇa—in detail; ātmanaḥ—your; yogam—divine glories; vibhūtim—opulences; cha—also; janaārdana—Shree Krishna, he who looks after the public; bhūyaḥ—again; kathaya—describe; tṛiptiḥ—satisfaction; hi—because; śhṛiṇvataḥ—hearing; na—not; asti—is; me—my; amṛitam—nectar

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit:
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम्।

वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम्।।10.23।।
verses.transliteration:
rudrāṇāṁ śhaṅkaraśh chāsmi vitteśho yakṣha-rakṣhasām
vasūnāṁ pāvakaśh chāsmi meruḥ śhikhariṇām aham
verses.translation: Of the Rudras, I am Sankara. Of the Yaksas and Raksasas, I am the Lord of Wealth (Kubera). Of the Vasus, I am Agni; of the mountains, I am Meru.
verses.hindi: ।।10.23।। रुद्रोंमें शंकर और यक्ष-राक्षसोंमें कुबेर मैं हूँ।वसुओंमें पावक (अग्नि) और शिखरवाले पर्वतोंमें सुमेरु मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: rudrāṇām—amongst the Rudras; śhaṅkaraḥ—Lord Shiv; cha—and; asmi—I am; vitta-īśhaḥ—the god of wealth and the treasurer of the celestial gods; yakṣha—amongst the semi-divine demons; rakṣhasām—amongst the demons; vasūnām—amongst the Vasus; pāvakaḥ—Agni (fire); cha—and; asmi—I am; meruḥ—Mount Meru; śhikhariṇām—amongst the mountains; aham—I am

verses.sanskrit:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम्।

सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः।।10.24।।
verses.transliteration:
purodhasāṁ cha mukhyaṁ māṁ viddhi pārtha bṛihaspatim
senānīnām ahaṁ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ
verses.translation: Among family priests, O Arjuna, know Me to be the chief Brhaspati; of generals, I am Skanda; of reservoirs of water, I am the ocean.
verses.hindi: ।।10.24।। हे पार्थ ! पुरोहितोंमें मुख्य बृहस्पतिको मेरा स्वरूप समझो। सेनापतियोंमें स्कन्द और जलाशयोंमें समुद्र मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: purodhasām—amongst priests; cha—and; mukhyam—the chiefs; mām—me; viddhi—know; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; bṛihaspatim—Brihaspati; senānīnām—warrior chief; aham—I; skandaḥ—Kartikeya; sarasām—amongst reservoirs of water; asmi—I am; sāgaraḥ—the ocean

verses.sanskrit:
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम्।

यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः।।10.25।।
verses.transliteration:
maharṣhīṇāṁ bhṛigur ahaṁ girām asmyekam akṣharam
yajñānāṁ japa-yajño ’smi sthāvarāṇāṁ himālayaḥ
verses.translation: Of the great seers, I am Bhrgu; of words, I am the single-lettered word Om; of sacrifices, I am the sacrifice of Japa; of immovable things, I am the Himalayas.
verses.hindi: ।।10.25।। महर्षियोंमें भृगु और वाणियों-(शब्दों-) में एक अक्षर अर्थात् प्रणव मैं हूँ। सम्पूर्ण यज्ञोंमें जपयज्ञ और स्थिर रहनेवालोंमें हिमालय मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: mahā-ṛiṣhīṇām—among the great seers; bhṛiguḥ—Bhrigu; aham—I; girām—amongst chants; asmi—I am; ekam akṣharam—the syllable Om; yajñānām—of sacrifices; japa-yajñaḥ—sacrifice of the devotional repetition of the divine names of God; asmi—I am; sthāvarāṇām—amongst immovable things; himālayaḥ—the Himalayas

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम्।

पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम्।।10.29।।
verses.transliteration:
anantaśh chāsmi nāgānāṁ varuṇo yādasām aham
pitṝīṇām aryamā chāsmi yamaḥ sanyamatām aham
verses.translation: Of snakes, I am Ananta; of aquatic beings, I am Varuna; of manes, I am Aryama; of subduers, I am Yama.
verses.hindi: ।।10.29।। नागोंमें अनन्त (शेषनाग) और जल-जन्तुओंका अधिपति वरुण मैं हूँ। पितरोंमें अर्यमा और शासन करनेवालोंमें यमराज मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: anantaḥ—Anant; cha—and; asmi—I am; nāgānām—amongst snakes; varuṇaḥ—the celestial god of the ocean; yādasām—amongst aquatics; aham—I; pitṝīṇām—amongst the departed ancestors; aryamā—Aryama; cha—and; asmi—am; yamaḥ—the celestial god of death; sanyamatām—amongst dispensers of law; aham—I

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One.
verses.hindi: आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूर्य उदय हों तो जो प्रकाश हो, वह उस महात्मा (विश्वरूप) के तेज के समान होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.

verses.sanskrit:
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च।

अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः।।10.33।।
verses.transliteration:
अहमेवाक्षय: कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुख: || 33||

akṣharāṇām a-kāro ’smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya cha
aham evākṣhayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṁ viśhvato-mukhaḥ
verses.translation: Of letters, I am the alphabet 'A'; of compound words, I am the dvandva (copulative); I am myself imperishable time; I am the creator, facing all sides.
verses.hindi: ।।10.33।। अक्षरोंमें अकार और समासोंमें द्वन्द्व समास मैं हूँ। अक्षयकाल अर्थात् कालका भी महाकाल तथा सब ओर मुखवाला धाता भी मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: akṣharāṇām—amongst all letters; a-kāraḥ—the beginning letter “A”; asmi—I am; dvandvaḥ—the dual; sāmāsikasya—amongst grammatical compounds; cha—and; aham—I; eva—only; akṣhayaḥ—endless; kālaḥ—time; dhātā—amongst the creators; aham—I; viśhwataḥ-mukhaḥ—Brahma

verses.sanskrit: स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.transliteration: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
verses.hindi: अपने स्वधर्म में मरना भला है, चाहे वह अपूर्ण हो; परधर्म को अच्छी तरह से करना भयावह है।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.
verses.commentary: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.

verses.sanskrit:
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्।

जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम्।।10.36।।
verses.transliteration:
dyūtaṁ chhalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham
jayo ’smi vyavasāyo ’smi sattvaṁ sattvavatām aham
verses.translation: Of the fraudulent, I am gambling; I am the brilliance of the brilliant; I am victory, I am effort; I am the magnanimity of the magnanimous.
verses.hindi: ।।10.36।। छल करनेवालोंमें जूआ और तेजस्वियोंमें तेज मैं हूँ। जीतनेवालोंकी विजय, निश्चय करनेवालोंका निश्चय और सात्त्विक मनुष्योंका सात्त्विक भाव मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: dyūtam—gambling; chhalayatām—of all cheats; asmi—I am; tejaḥ—the splendor; tejasvinām—of the splendid; aham—I; jayaḥ—victory; asmi—I am; vyavasāyaḥ—firm resolve; asmi—I am; sattvam—virtue; sattva-vatām—of the virtuous; aham—I

verses.sanskrit:
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः।

मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः।।10.37।।
verses.transliteration:
vṛiṣhṇīnāṁ vāsudevo ’smi pāṇḍavānāṁ dhanañjayaḥ
munīnām apyahaṁ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśhanā kaviḥ
verses.translation: Of the Vrsnis, I am Vasudeva; of the Pandavas, I am Arjuna; of sages, I am Vyasa; and of seers, I am Usana (Sukra).
verses.hindi: ।।10.37।। वृष्णिवंशियोंमें वासुदेव और पाण्डवोंमें धनञ्जय मैं हूँ। मुनियोंमें वेदव्यास और कवियोंमें कवि शुक्राचार्य भी मैं हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: vṛiṣhṇīnām—amongst the descendants of Vrishni; vāsudevaḥ—Krishna, the son of Vasudev; asmi—I am; pāṇḍavānām—amongst the Pandavas; dhanañjayaḥ—Arjun, the conqueror of wealth; munīnām—amongst the sages; api—also; aham—I; vyāsaḥ—Ved Vyas; kavīnām—amongst the great thinkers; uśhanā—Shukracharya; kaviḥ—the thinker

verses.sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ | ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ||
verses.transliteration: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
verses.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same — then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.
verses.hindi: सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि और जय-पराजय को समान करके तब युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो। इस प्रकार तुम पाप नहीं प्राप्त करोगे।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).

verses.sanskrit:
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन।

न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्।।10.39।।
verses.transliteration:
yach chāpi sarva-bhūtānāṁ bījaṁ tad aham arjuna
na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṁ charācharam
verses.translation: I am also that which is the seed of all beings, O Arjuna. Nothing that moves or does not move exists without Me.
verses.hindi: ।।10.39।। हे अर्जुन! सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका जो बीज है, वह बीज मैं ही हूँ; क्योंकि मेरे बिना कोई भी चर-अचर प्राणी नहीं है अर्थात् चर-अचर सब कुछ मैं ही हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: yat—which; cha—and; api—also; sarva-bhūtānām—of all living beings; bījam—generating seed; tat—that; aham—I; arjuna—Arjun; na—not; tat—that; asti—is; vinā—without; yat—which; syāt—may exist; mayā—me; bhūtam—creature; chara-acharam—moving and nonmoving

verses.sanskrit:
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप।

एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया।।10.40।।
verses.transliteration:
nānto ’sti mama divyānāṁ vibhūtīnāṁ parantapa
eṣha tūddeśhataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā
verses.translation: There is no limit to My divine manifestations. Here, I have briefly described the extent of such manifestations.
verses.hindi: ।।10.40।। हे परंतप अर्जुन ! मेरी दिव्य विभूतियोंका अन्त नहीं है। मैंने तुम्हारे सामने अपनी विभूतियोंका जो विस्तार कहा है, यह तो केवल संक्षेपसे कहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: na—not; antaḥ—end; asti—is; mama—my; divyānām—divine; vibhūtīnām—manifestations; parantapa—Arjun, the conqueror of the enemies; eṣhaḥ—this; tu—but; uddeśhataḥ—just one portion; proktaḥ—declared; vibhūteḥ—of (my) glories; vistaraḥ—the breath of the topic; mayā—by me

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा।

तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम्।।10.41।।
verses.transliteration:
yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śhrīmad ūrjitam eva vā
tat tad evāvagachchha tvaṁ mama tejo ’nśha-sambhavam
verses.translation: Whatever being is possessed of power, or splendour, or energy, know that as coming from a fragment of My power.
verses.hindi: ।।10.41।। जो-जो ऐश्वर्ययुक्त, शोभायुक्त और बलयुक्त प्राणी तथा वस्तु है, उस-उसको तुम मेरे ही तेज-(योग-) के अंशसे उत्पन्न हुई समझो।
verses.wordMeaning: yat yat—whatever; vibhūtimat—opulent; sattvam—being; śhrī-mat—beautiful; ūrjitam—glorious; eva—also; vā—or; tat tat—all that; eva—only; avagachchha—know; tvam—you; mama—my; tejaḥ-anśha-sambhavam—splendor; anśha—a part; sambhavam—born of

verses.sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः | स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||
verses.transliteration: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||
verses.translation: Whatever a great man does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
verses.hindi: जो-जो आचरण श्रेष्ठ पुरुष करता है, अन्य लोग भी वही करते हैं। वह जो प्रमाण स्थापित करता है, संसार उसी का अनुसरण करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.
verses.commentary: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One.
verses.hindi: आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूर्य उदय हों तो जो प्रकाश हो, वह उस महात्मा (विश्वरूप) के तेज के समान होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत | क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ||
verses.transliteration: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata | kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama ||
verses.translation: And also know Me to be the knower of the field in all fields, O Bharata. I consider true knowledge to be the understanding of the field and the knower of the field.
verses.hindi: और हे भारत! सभी क्षेत्रों में क्षेत्रज्ञ (क्षेत्र को जानने वाला) भी मुझे ही जानो। क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ का यह ज्ञान ही मेरे मत में सच्चा ज्ञान है।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the fundamental metaphysical distinction: the "field" (body, mind, senses, and all their modifications) and the "knower of the field" (pure consciousness). The body is the field — it changes, ages, dies. The knower of the field is the eternal witness. Identifying with the field is ignorance; recognizing oneself as the knower is wisdom.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the fundamental metaphysical distinction: the "field" (body, mind, senses, and all their modifications) and the "knower of the field" (pure consciousness). The body is the field — it changes, ages, dies. The knower of the field is the eternal witness. Identifying with the field is ignorance; recognizing oneself as the knower is wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत | श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ||
verses.transliteration: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhāḥ sa eva saḥ ||
verses.translation: The faith of each person, O Bharata, accords with their natural disposition. A person is made of their faith; what their faith is, that, verily, they are.
verses.hindi: हे भारत! प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की श्रद्धा उसके स्वभाव (सत्त्व) के अनुसार होती है। यह पुरुष श्रद्धामय है — जैसी श्रद्धा, वैसा पुरुष।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."
verses.commentary: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."

verses.sanskrit:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो।

योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम्।।11.4।।
verses.transliteration:
manyase yadi tach chhakyaṁ mayā draṣhṭum iti prabho
yogeśhvara tato me tvaṁ darśhayātmānam avyayam
verses.translation: If you think, O Lord, that it can be seen by me, then, O Lord of Yoga, reveal Yourself fully to me.
verses.hindi: ।।11.4।। हे प्रभो ! मेरे द्वारा आपका वह परम ऐश्वर रूप देखा जा सकता है -- ऐसा अगर आप मानते हैं, तो हे योगेश्वर ! आप अपने उस अविनाशी स्वरूपको मुझे दिखा दीजिये।
verses.wordMeaning: manyase—you think; yadi—if; tat—that; śhakyam—possible; mayā—by me; draṣhṭum—to behold; iti—thus; prabho—Lord; yoga-īśhvara—Lord of all mystic powers; tataḥ—then; me—to me; tvam—you; darśhaya—reveal; ātmānam—yourself; avyayam—imperishable

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः।

दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्।।11.9।।
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvā tato rājan mahā-yogeśhvaro hariḥ
darśhayām āsa pārthāya paramaṁ rūpam aiśhwaram
verses.translation: Sanjaya said, "O King, having spoken, Sri Krishna, the great Lord of Yoga, then revealed to Arjuna the supreme, lordly form."
verses.hindi: ।।11.9।। सञ्जय बोले -- हे राजन् ! ऐसा कहकर फिर महायोगेश्वर भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने अर्जुनको परम ऐश्वर-रूप दिखाया।
verses.wordMeaning: sañjayaḥ uvācha—Sanjay said; evam—thus; uktvā—having spoken; tataḥ—then; rājan—King; mahā-yoga-īśhvaraḥ—the Supreme Lord of Yog; hariḥ—Shree Krishna; darśhayām āsa—displayed; pārthāya—to Arjun; paramam—divine; rūpam aiśhwaram—opulence

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं

पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम्।

नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं

पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप।।11.16।।
verses.transliteration:
aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netraṁ
paśhyāmi tvāṁ sarvato ’nanta-rūpam
nāntaṁ na madhyaṁ na punas tavādiṁ
paśhyāmi viśhveśhvara viśhva-rūpa
verses.translation: With manifold arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes, I behold Your infinite form on all sides. I see no end, no middle, nor the beginning of You, O Lord of the universe, O You of Universal Form.
verses.hindi: ।।11.16।। हे विश्वरूप ! हे विश्वेश्वरव ! आपको मैं अनेक हाथों, पेटों, मुखों और नेत्रोंवाला तथा सब ओरसे अनन्त रूपोंवाला देख रहा हूँ। मैं आपके न आदिको, न मध्यको और न अन्तको ही देख रहा हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: aneka—infinite; bāhu—arms; udara—stomachs; vaktra—faces; netram—eyes; paśhyāmi—I see; tvām—you; sarvataḥ—in every direction; ananta-rūpam—inifinite forms; na antam—without end; na—not; madhyam—middle; na—no; punaḥ—again; tava—your; ādim—beginning; paśhyāmi—I see; viśhwa-īśhwara—The Lord of the universe; viśhwa-rūpa—universal form

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं

त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्।

त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता

सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे।।11.18।।
verses.transliteration:
tvam akṣharaṁ paramaṁ veditavyaṁ
tvam asya viśhvasya paraṁ nidhānam
tvam avyayaḥ śhāśhvata-dharma-goptā
sanātanas tvaṁ puruṣho mato me
verses.translation: You are the Imperishable, Supreme One to be realized. You are the Supreme Substratum of this universe. You are immutable, the guardian of the eternal law; I know You are the Supreme Person who is everlasting.
verses.hindi: ।।11.18।। आप ही जाननेयोग्य परम अक्षर (अक्षरब्रह्म) हैं, आप ही इस सम्पूर्ण विश्वके परम आश्रय हैं, आप ही सनातनधर्मके रक्षक हैं और आप ही अविनाशी सनातन पुरुष हैं -- ऐसा मैं मानता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: tvam—you; akṣharam—the imperishable; paramam—the supreme being; veditavyam—worthy of being known; tvam—you; asya—of this; viśhwasya—of the creation; param—supreme; nidhānam—support; tvam—you; avyayaḥ—eternal; śhāśhvata-dharma-goptā—protector of the eternal religion; sanātanaḥ—everlasting; tvam—you; puruṣhaḥ—the Supreme Divine Person; mataḥ me—my opinion

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit:
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं

महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम्।

बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं

दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम्।।11.23।।
verses.transliteration:
rūpaṁ mahat te bahu-vaktra-netraṁ
mahā-bāho bahu-bāhūru-pādam
bahūdaraṁ bahu-danṣhṭrā-karālaṁ
dṛiṣhṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitās tathāham
verses.translation: Beholding Your great form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many stomachs, and terrible with many teeth, the worlds tremble, and I too quake, O mighty-armed one.
verses.hindi: ।।11.23।। हे महाबाहो! आपके बहुत मुखों और नेत्रोंवाले, बहुत भुजाओं, जंघाओं और चरणोंवाले, बहुत उदरोंवाले, बहुत विकराल दाढ़ोंवाले महान् रूपको देखकर सब प्राणी व्यथित हो रहे हैं तथा मैं भी व्यथित हो रहा हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: rūpam—form; mahat—magnificent; te—your; bahu—many; vaktra—mouths; netram—eyes; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed Lord; bahu—many; bāhu—arms; ūru—thighs; pādam—legs; bahu-udaram—many stomachs; bahu-danṣhṭrā—many teeth; karālam—terrifying; dṛiṣhṭvā—seeing; lokāḥ—all the worlds; pravyathitāḥ—terror-stricken; tathā—so also; aham—I

verses.sanskrit:
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं

व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम्।

दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा

धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो।।11.24।।
verses.transliteration:
nabhaḥ-spṛiśhaṁ dīptam aneka-varṇaṁ
vyāttānanaṁ dīpta-viśhāla-netram
dṛiṣhṭvā hi tvāṁ pravyathitāntar-ātmā
dhṛitiṁ na vindāmi śhamaṁ cha viṣhṇo
verses.translation: When I behold You touching the Supreme Heaven, shining, multicolored, with yawning mouths and large, resplendent eyes, my inner being trembles in fear. I am unable to find support or peace, O Vishnu.
verses.hindi: ।।11.24।। हे विष्णो ! आपके अनेक देदीप्यमान वर्ण हैं, आप आकाशको स्पर्श कर रहे हैं, आपका मुख फैला हुआ है आपके नेत्र प्रदीप्त और विशाल हैं। ऐसे आपको देखकर भयभीत अन्तःकरणवाला मैं धैर्य और शान्तिको प्राप्त नहीं हो रहा हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: nabhaḥ-spṛiśham—touching the sky; dīptam—effulgent; aneka—many; varṇam—colors; vyātta—open; ānanam—mouths; dīpta—blazing; viśhāla—enormous; netram—eyes; dṛiṣhṭvā—seeing; hi—indeed; tvām—you; pravyathitāntar-ātmā—my heart is trembling with fear; dhṛitim—firmness; na—not; vindāmi—I find; śhamam—mental peace; cha—and; viṣhṇo—Lord Vishnu

verses.sanskrit:
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि

दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि।

दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म

प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास।।11.25।।
verses.transliteration:
danṣhṭrā-karālāni cha te mukhāni
dṛiṣhṭvaiva kālānala-sannibhāni
diśho na jāne na labhe cha śharma
prasīda deveśha jagan-nivāsa
verses.translation: Viewing Your mouths, presenting awe-generating fangs and looking like the consuming fire of final destruction, I know not the quarters of the globe nor do I find repose. Be gracious, O Lord of the Devas! O Abode of the universe!
verses.hindi: ।।11.25।। आपके प्रलयकालकी अग्निके समान प्रज्वलित और दाढ़ोंके कारण विकराल (भयानक) मुखोंको देखकर मुझे न तो दिशाओंका ज्ञान हो रहा है और न शान्ति ही मिल रही है। इसलिये हे देवेश ! हे जगन्निवास ! आप प्रसन्न होइये।
verses.wordMeaning: danṣhṭrā—teeth; karālāni—terrible; cha—and; te—your; mukhāni—mouths; dṛiṣhṭvā—having seen; eva—indeed; kāla-anala—the fire of annihilation; sannibhāni—resembling; diśhaḥ—the directions; na—not; jāne—know; na—not; labhe—I obtain; cha—and; śharma—peace; prasīda—have mercy; deva-īśha—The Lord of lords; jagat-nivāsa—The shelter of the universe

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा

विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः।

तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका

स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः।।11.29।।
verses.transliteration:
yathā pradīptaṁ jvalanaṁ pataṅgā
viśhanti nāśhāya samṛiddha-vegāḥ
tathaiva nāśhāya viśhanti lokās
tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛiddha-vegāḥ
verses.translation: As moths rush swiftly into a blazing fire, leading to their destruction, so do these men swiftly rush into Your mouths, leading to their destruction.
verses.hindi: ।।11.29।। जैसे पतंगे मोहवश अपना नाश करनेके लिये बड़े वेगसे दौड़ते हुए प्रज्वलित अग्निमें प्रविष्ट होते हैं, ऐसे ही ये सब लोग भी मोहवश अपना नाश करनेके लिये बड़े वेगसे दौड़ते हुए आपके मुखोंमें प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: yathā—as; pradīptam—blazing; jvalanam—fire; pataṅgāḥ—moths; viśhanti—enter; nāśhāya—to be perished; samṛiddha vegāḥ—with great speed; tathā eva—similarly; nāśhāya—to be perished; viśhanti—enter; lokāḥ—these people; tava—your; api—also; vaktrāṇi—mouths; samṛiddha-vegāḥ—with great speed

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व

जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम्।

मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव

निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्।।11.33।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmāt tvam uttiṣhṭha yaśho labhasva
jitvā śhatrūn bhuṅkṣhva rājyaṁ samṛiddham
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sāchin
verses.translation: Therefore, arise, win glory. Conquering your foes, enjoy a prosperous kingdom. By Me they have already been slain. You be merely an instrument, O Arjuna, you great archer!
verses.hindi: ।।11.33।। इसलिये तुम युद्धके लिये खड़े हो जाओ और यशको प्राप्त करो तथा शत्रुओंको जीतकर धन-धान्यसे सम्पन्न राज्यको भोगो। ये सभी मेरे द्वारा पहलेसे ही मारे हुए हैं। हे सव्यसाचिन् !  तुम निमित्तमात्र बन जाओ।
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—therefore; tvam—you; uttiṣhṭha—arise; yaśhaḥ—honor; labhasva—attain; jitvā—conquer; śhatrūn—foes; bhuṅkṣhva—enjoy; rājyam—kingdom; samṛiddham—prosperous; mayā—by me; eva—indeed; ete—these; nihatāḥ—slain; pūrvam—already; eva nimitta-mātram—only an instrument; bhava—become; savya-sāchin—Arjun, the one who can shoot arrows with both hands

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यतां गतं पार्थ मायया ते तदात्मकम् | यत्तु सत्यं सनातनं तदहं वदतः स्म ते ||
verses.transliteration: adṛśyatāṃ gataṃ pārtha māyayā te tadātmakam | yattu satyaṃ sanātanaṃ tadahaṃ vadataḥ sma te ||
verses.translation: O Partha, the cosmic form you saw was manifested by My Yoga-Maya. Now I shall reveal to you My eternal form.
verses.hindi: हे पार्थ! जो तुमने देखा वह मेरी योगमाया से प्रकट किया गया था। अब मैं तुम्हें अपना शाश्वत रूप बताता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.
verses.commentary: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.transliteration: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
verses.hindi: अपने स्वधर्म में मरना भला है, चाहे वह अपूर्ण हो; परधर्म को अच्छी तरह से करना भयावह है।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.
verses.commentary: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या

जगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च।

रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति

सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः।।11.36।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sthāne hṛiṣhīkeśha tava prakīrtyā
jagat prahṛiṣhyaty anurajyate cha
rakṣhānsi bhītāni diśho dravanti
sarve namasyanti cha siddha-saṅghāḥ
verses.translation: Arjuna said, Rightly it is, O Krsna, that Your praise should move the world to joy and love. The rakshasas flee in fear on all sides, and all the hosts of siddhas bow down to You.
verses.hindi: ।।11.36।। अर्जुन बोले -- हे अन्तर्यामी भगवन् ! आपके नाम, गुण, लीलाका कीर्तन करनेसे यह सम्पूर्ण जगत् हर्षित हो रहा है और अनुराग(-प्रेम-) को प्राप्त हो रहा है। आपके नाम, गुण आदिके कीर्तनसे भयभीत होकर राक्षसलोग दसों दिशाओंमें भागते हुए जा रहे हैं और सम्पूर्ण सिद्धगण आपको नमस्कार कर रहे हैं। यह सब होना उचित ही है।
verses.wordMeaning: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; sthāne—it is but apt; hṛiṣhīka-īśha—Shree Krishna, the master of the senses; tava—your; prakīrtyā—in praise; jagat—the universe; prahṛiṣhyati—rejoices; anurajyate—be enamored; cha—and; rakṣhānsi—the demons; bhītāni—fearfully; diśhaḥ—in all directions; dravanti—flee; sarve—all; namasyanti—bow down; cha—and; siddha-saṅghāḥ—hosts of perfected saints

verses.sanskrit:
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्

गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे।

अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास

त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत्।।11.37।।
verses.transliteration:
kasmāch cha te na nameran mahātman
garīyase brahmaṇo ’py ādi-kartre
ananta deveśha jagan-nivāsa
tvam akṣharaṁ sad-asat tat paraṁ yat
verses.translation:
(a) And why should they not, O Mahatma, bow down to You who are great, being the first Creator, even of Brahma?
(b) O Infinite, Lord of gods, O You who have the universe as Your abode! You are the imperishable individual self, the existent and the non-existent, and that which is beyond both.
verses.hindi: ।।11.37।। हे महात्मन् ! गुरुओंके भी गुरु और ब्रह्माके भी आदिकर्ता आपके लिये (वे सिद्धगण) नमस्कार क्यों नहीं करें? क्योंकि हे अनन्त ! हे देवेश ! हे जगन्निवास ! आप अक्षरस्वरूप हैं; आप सत् भी हैं, असत् भी हैं, और सत्-असत् से पर भी जो कुछ है, वह भी आप ही हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: kasmāt—why; cha—and; te—you; na nameran—should they not bow down; mahā-ātman—The Great one; garīyase—who are greater; brahmaṇaḥ—than Brahma; api—even; ādi-kartre—to the original creator; ananta—The limitless One; deva-īśha—Lord of the devatās; jagat-nivāsa—Refuge of the universe; tvam—you; akṣharam—the imperishable; sat-asat—manifest and non-manifest; tat—that; param—beyond; yat—which

verses.sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ | ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ||
verses.transliteration: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau | tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
verses.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same — then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.
verses.hindi: सुख-दुःख, लाभ-हानि और जय-पराजय को समान करके तब युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो। इस प्रकार तुम पाप नहीं प्राप्त करोगे।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the yoga of equanimity (samatva). The key to action without attachment is treating opposites as equal — not by suppressing feelings but by maintaining inner balance regardless of external outcomes. When action is performed without the fever of craving or aversion, it becomes pure (without sin/papa).

verses.sanskrit:
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः

प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च।

नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः

पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते।।11.39।।
verses.transliteration:
vāyur yamo ’gnir varuṇaḥ śhaśhāṅkaḥ
prajāpatis tvaṁ prapitāmahaśh cha
namo namas te ’stu sahasra-kṛitvaḥ
punaśh cha bhūyo ’pi namo namas te
verses.translation:
(a) You are Yayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, Sashanka, Prajapati, and the great-grandsire.
(b) Hail to You a thousand times! Hail to You again and yet again!
verses.hindi: ।।11.39।। आप ही वायु, यमराज, अग्नि, वरुण, चन्द्रमा, दक्ष आदि प्रजापति और प्रपितामह (ब्रह्माजीके भी पिता) हैं। आपको हजारों बार नमस्कार हो! नमस्कार हो ! ! और फिर भी आपको बार-बार नमस्कार हो ! नमस्कार हो !
verses.wordMeaning: vāyuḥ—the god of wind; yamaḥ—the god of death; agniḥ—the god of fire; varuṇaḥ—the god of water; śhaśha-aṅkaḥ—the moon-God; prajāpatiḥ—Brahma; tvam—you; prapitāmahaḥ—the great-grandfather; cha—and; namaḥ—my salutations; namaḥ—my salutations; te—unto you; astu—let there be; sahasra-kṛitvaḥ—a thousand times; punaḥ cha—and again; bhūyaḥ—again; api—also; namaḥ—(offering) my salutations; namaḥ te—offering my salutations unto you

verses.sanskrit:
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते

नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व।

अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं

सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः।।11.40।।
verses.transliteration:
namaḥ purastād atha pṛiṣhṭhatas te
namo ’stu te sarvata eva sarva
ananta-vīryāmita-vikramas tvaṁ
sarvaṁ samāpnoṣhi tato ’si sarvaḥ
verses.translation:
(a) Salutations to You from before and behind! Salutations to You from all sides, O All!৷৷.

(b) ৷৷. O You of infinite prowess and heroic action, which are measureless! You pervade all beings, and therefore, You are all.
verses.hindi: ।।11.40।। हे सर्व ! आपको आगेसे भी नमस्कार हो !  पीछेसे भी नमस्कार हो ! सब ओरसे ही नमस्कार हो ! हे अनन्तवीर्य ! अमित विक्रमवाले आपने सबको समावृत कर रखा है; अतः सब कुछ आप ही हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: namaḥ—offering salutations; purastāt—from the front; atha—and; pṛiṣhṭhataḥ—the rear; te—to you; namaḥ astu—I offer my salutations; te—to you; sarvataḥ—from all sides; eva—indeed; sarva—all; ananta-vīrya—infinite power; amita-vikramaḥ—infinite valor and might; tvam—you; sarvam—everything; samāpnoṣhi—pervade; tataḥ—thus; asi—(you) are; sarvaḥ—everything

verses.sanskrit:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं

हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति।

अजानता महिमानं तवेदं

मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि।।11.41।।
verses.transliteration:
sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yad uktaṁ
he kṛiṣhṇa he yādava he sakheti
ajānatā mahimānaṁ tavedaṁ
mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi
verses.translation: Unaware of Your majesty, and either out of negligence or love, or considering You to be a friend, whatever I have said rudely, such as 'O Krsna, O Yadava, O Comrade,'
verses.hindi: ।।11.41 -- 11.42।। आपकी महिमा और स्वरूपको न जानते हुए 'मेरे सखा हैं' ऐसा मानकर मैंने प्रमादसे अथवा प्रेमसे हठपूर्वक (बिना सोचे-समझे) 'हे कृष्ण ! हे यादव ! हे सखे !' इस प्रकार जो कुछ कहा है; और हे अच्युत ! हँसी-दिल्लगीमें, चलते-फिरते, सोते-जागते, उठते-बैठते, खाते-पीते समयमें अकेले अथवा उन सखाओं, कुटुम्बियों आदिके सामने मेरे द्वारा आपका जो कुछ तिरस्कार किया गया है;  वह सब अप्रमेयस्वरुप आपसे मैं क्षमा माँगता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: sakhā—friend; iti—as; matvā—thinking; prasabham—presumptuously; yat—whatever; uktam—addressed; he kṛiṣhṇa—O Shree Krishna; he yādava—O Shree Krishna, who was born in the Yadu clan; he sakhe—O my dear mate; iti—thus; ajānatā—in ignorance; mahimānam—majesty; tava—your; idam—this; mayā—by me; pramādāt—out of negligence; praṇayena—out of affection; vā api—or else;

verses.sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः | स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||
verses.transliteration: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||
verses.translation: Whatever a great man does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
verses.hindi: जो-जो आचरण श्रेष्ठ पुरुष करता है, अन्य लोग भी वही करते हैं। वह जो प्रमाण स्थापित करता है, संसार उसी का अनुसरण करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.
verses.commentary: Leaders have a duty to set the highest example. Arjuna, as a kshatriya prince, must uphold dharma through action.

verses.sanskrit:
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य

त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान्।

न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो

लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव।।11.43।।
verses.transliteration:
pitāsi lokasya charācharasya
tvam asya pūjyaśh cha gurur garīyān
na tvat-samo ’sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto ’nyo
loka-traye ’py apratima-prabhāva
verses.translation: You are the father of this world, of all that moves and does not move. You are its teacher and the one most worthy of reverence. There is none equal to You. How then could there be in the three worlds another greater than You, O Being of matchless greatness?
verses.hindi: ।।11.43।। आप ही इस चराचर संसारके पिता हैं, आप ही पूजनीय हैं और आप ही गुरुओंके महान् गुरु हैं। हे अनन्त प्रभावशाली भगवन् ! इस त्रिलोकीमें आपके समान भी दूसरा कोई नहीं है, फिर अधिक तो हो ही कैसे सकता है !
verses.wordMeaning: pitā—the father; asi—you are; lokasya—of the entire universe; chara—moving; acharasya—nonmoving; tvam—you; asya—of this; pūjyaḥ—worshipable; cha—and; guruḥ—spiritual master; garīyān—glorious; na—not; tvat-samaḥ—equal to you; asti—is; abhyadhikaḥ—greater; kutaḥ—who is?; anyaḥ—other; loka-traye—in the three worlds; api—even; apratima-prabhāva—possessor of incomparable power

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं

प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम्।

पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः

प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम्।।11.44।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṁ
prasādaye tvām aham īśham īḍyam
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum
verses.translation: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I implore Your mercy, O adorable Lord. As a father listens to his son or a friend to his friend, it is fitting, O Lord, that You, who are dear to me, should bear with me who am dear to You.
verses.hindi: ।।11.44।। इसलिये शरीरसे लम्बा पड़कर स्तुति करनेयोग्य आप ईश्वरको मैं प्रणाम करके प्रसन्न करना चाहता हूँ। जैसे पिता पुत्रके, मित्र मित्रके और पति पत्नीके अपमानको सह लेता है, ऐसे ही हे देव ! आप मेरे द्वारा किया गया अपमान सहनेमें समर्थ हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—therefore; praṇamya—bowing down; praṇidhāya—prostrating; kāyam—the body; prasādaye—to implore grace; tvām—your; aham—I; īśham—the Supreme Lord; īḍyam—adorable; pitā—father; iva—as; putrasya—with a son; sakhā—friend; iva—as; sakhyuḥ—with a friend; priyaḥ—a lover; priyāyāḥ—with the beloved; arhasi—you should; deva—Lord; soḍhum—forgive

verses.sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा

भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे।

तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं

प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास।।11.45।।
verses.transliteration:
adṛiṣhṭa-pūrvaṁ hṛiṣhito ’smi dṛiṣhṭvā
bhayena cha pravyathitaṁ mano me
tad eva me darśhaya deva rūpaṁ
prasīda deveśha jagan-nivāsa
verses.translation: Seeing something never seen before, I am delighted. But my mind is also filled with awe. Show me, O Lord! Your other form. O Lord of the gods! Be gracious, O Abode of the universe!
verses.hindi: ।।11.45।। मैंने ऐसा रुप पहले कभी नहीं देखा। इस रूपको देखकर मैं हर्षित हो रहा हूँ और (साथ-ही-साथ) भयसे मेरा मन अत्यन्त व्यथित हो रहा है। अतः आप मुझे अपने उसी देवरूपको (सौम्य विष्णुरूपको)  दिखाइये। हे देवेश ! हे जगन्निवास ! आप प्रसन्न होइये।
verses.wordMeaning: adṛiṣhṭa-pūrvam—that which has not been seen before; hṛiṣhitaḥ—great joy; asmi—I am; dṛiṣhṭvā—having seen; bhayena—with fear; cha—yet; pravyathitam—trembles; manaḥ—mind; me—my; tat—that; eva—certainly; me—to me; darśhaya—show; deva—Lord; rūpam—form; prasīda—please have mercy; deva-īśha—God of gods; jagat-nivāsa—abode of the universe

verses.sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः | धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ||
verses.transliteration: yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||
verses.translation: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, slay me in battle while I am unarmed and unresisting, that would be better for me.
verses.hindi: यदि धार्तराष्ट्र शस्त्र-पाणि होकर युद्ध में मुझ अप्रतिकार करने वाले को मार दें, तो यह मेरे लिए अधिक कल्याणकारक होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna reaches the nadir of despondency. He confuses non-violence with cowardice. True non-violence is acting without hatred, not paralysis from attachment.
verses.commentary: Arjuna reaches the nadir of despondency. He confuses non-violence with cowardice. True non-violence is acting without hatred, not paralysis from attachment.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच | एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् | विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ||
verses.transliteration: sañjaya uvāca | evamuktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat | visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ ||
verses.translation: Having spoken thus, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows, and sat down on the chariot, his mind distressed with grief.
verses.hindi: संजय बोले — इस प्रकार कहकर, शोक से व्याकुल मन वाले अर्जुन ने रणभूमि में अपने बाण और धनुष छोड़कर रथ के पिछले भाग में बैठ गए।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna casts aside his weapons — the tools of his kshatriya dharma. His sitting posture signals defeat. This sets the stage for Krishna's entire teaching.
verses.commentary: Arjuna casts aside his weapons — the tools of his kshatriya dharma. His sitting posture signals defeat. This sets the stage for Krishna's entire teaching.

verses.sanskrit:
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै

र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः।

एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके

द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर।।11.48।।
verses.transliteration:
na veda-yajñādhyayanair na dānair
na cha kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ
evaṁ-rūpaḥ śhakya ahaṁ nṛi-loke
draṣhṭuṁ tvad anyena kuru-pravīra
verses.translation: Neither through the study of the Vedas, nor by sacrifices, nor by recitations of the scriptures, nor by gifts, nor by rituals, nor by strict austerities can I be realized in a form like this in the world of men by anyone else but you. O Arjuna!
verses.hindi: ।।11.48।। हे कुरुप्रवीर! मनुष्यलोकमें इस प्रकारके विश्वरूपवाला मैं न वेदोंके पढ़नेसे, न यज्ञोंके अनुष्ठानसे, न दानसे, न उग्र तपोंसे और न मात्र क्रियाओंसे तेरे (कृपापात्रके) सिवाय और किसीके द्वारा देखा जाना शक्य हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: na—not; veda-yajña—by performance of sacrifice; adhyayanaiḥ—by study of the Vedas; na—nor; dānaiḥ—by charity; na—nor; cha—and; kriyābhiḥ—by rituals; na—not; tapobhiḥ—by austerities; ugraiḥ—severe; evam-rūpaḥ—in this form; śhakyaḥ—possible; aham—I; nṛi-loke—in the world of the mortals; draṣhṭum—to be seen; tvat—than you; anyena—by another; kuru-pravīra—the best of the Kuru warriors

verses.sanskrit:
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो

दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम्।

व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं

तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य।।11.49।।
verses.transliteration:
mā te vyathā mā cha vimūḍha-bhāvo
dṛiṣhṭvā rūpaṁ ghoram īdṛiṅ mamedam
vyapeta-bhīḥ prīta-manāḥ punas tvaṁ
tad eva me rūpam idaṁ prapaśhya
verses.translation: You need not fear any longer, nor be perplexed, looking upon this awe-inspiring form of Mine. Free from fear and with a gladdened heart, behold once again that other form of Mine.
