verses.hindi: ।।11.49।। यह इस प्रकारका मेरा घोररूप देखकर तेरेको व्यथा नहीं होनी चाहिये और मूढ़भाव भी नहीं होना चाहिये। अब निर्भय और प्रसन्न मनवाला होकर तू फिर उसी मेरे इस (चतुर्भुज) रूपको अच्छी तरह देख ले।
verses.wordMeaning: mā te—you shout not be; vyathā—afraid; mā—not; cha—and; vimūḍha-bhāvaḥ—bewildered state; dṛiṣhṭvā—on seeing; rūpam—form; ghoram—terrible; īdṛik—such; mama—of mine; idam—this; vyapeta-bhīḥ—free from fear; prīta-manāḥ—cheerful mind; punaḥ—again; tvam—you; tat eva—that very; me—my; rūpam—form; idam—this; prapaśhya—behold

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच

इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा

स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः।

आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं

भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा।।11.50।।
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
ity arjunaṁ vāsudevas tathoktvā
svakaṁ rūpaṁ darśhayām āsa bhūyaḥ
āśhvāsayām āsa cha bhītam enaṁ
bhūtvā punaḥ saumya-vapur mahātmā
verses.translation: Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Sri Krsna once more revealed His own form. The Mahatman, assuming a benign form again, reassured him who had been struck with awe.
verses.hindi: ।।11.50।। सञ्जय बोले -- वासुदेवभगवान् ने अर्जुनसे ऐसा कहकर फिर उसी प्रकारसे अपना रूप (देवरूप) दिखाया और महात्मा श्रीकृष्णने पुनः सौम्यवपु (द्विभुजरूप) होकर इस भयभीत अर्जुनको आश्वासन दिया।
verses.wordMeaning: sañjayaḥ uvācha—Sanjay said; iti—thus; arjunam—to Arjun; vāsudevaḥ—Krishna, the son of Vasudev; tathā—in that way; uktvā—having spoken; svakam—his personal; rūpam—form; darśhayām āsa—displayed; bhūyaḥ—again; āśhvāsayām āsa—consoled; cha—and; bhītam—frightened; enam—him; bhūtvā—becoming; punaḥ—again; saumya-vapuḥ—the gentle (two-armed) form; mahā-ātmā—the compassionate

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन।

इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः।।11.51।।
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
dṛiṣhṭvedaṁ mānuṣhaṁ rūpaṁ tava saumyaṁ janārdana
idānīm asmi saṁvṛittaḥ sa-chetāḥ prakṛitiṁ gataḥ
verses.translation: Arjuna said, "Having beheld Your human and pleasing form, O Krsna, I am now composed in mind and have been restored to my normal nature."
verses.hindi: ।।11.51।। अर्जुन बोले -- हे जनार्दन ! आपके इस सौम्य मनुष्यरूपको देखकर मैं इस समय स्थिरचित्त हो गया हूँ और अपनी स्वाभाविक स्थितिको प्राप्त हो गया हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; dṛiṣhṭvā—seeing; idam—this; mānuṣham—human; rūpam—form; tava—your; saumyam—gentle; janārdana—he who looks after the public, Krishna; idānīm—now; asmi—I am; saṁvṛittaḥ—composed; sa-chetāḥ—in my mind; prakṛitim—to normality; gataḥ—have become

verses.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम।

देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः।।11.52।।
verses.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
su-durdarśham idaṁ rūpaṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi yan mama
devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṁ darśhana-kāṅkṣhiṇaḥ
verses.translation: The Lord said, "It is very hard to behold this form of Mine which you have seen. Even the gods everlong to behold this form."
verses.hindi: ।।11.52।। श्रीभगवान् बोले -- मेरा यह जो रूप तुमने देखा है, इसके दर्शन अत्यन्त ही दुर्लभ हैं। इस रूपको देखनेके लिये देवता भी नित्य लालायित रहते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha—the Supreme Lord said; su-durdarśham—exceedingly difficult to behold; idam—this; rūpam—form; dṛiṣhṭavān asi—that you are seeing; yat—which; mama—of mine; devāḥ—the celestial gods; api—even; asya—this; rūpasya—form; nityam—eternally; darśhana-kāṅkṣhiṇaḥ—aspiring to see;

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया।

शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा।।11.53।।
verses.transliteration:
nāhaṁ vedair na tapasā na dānena na chejyayā
śhakya evaṁ-vidho draṣhṭuṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi māṁ yathā
verses.translation: Sri Krishna says, "I cannot be seen in such a form as You have seen Me, not by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by gifts, nor by sacrifice."
verses.hindi: ।।11.53।। जिस प्रकार तुमने मुझे देखा है, इस प्रकारका (चतुर्भुजरूपवाला) मैं न तो वेदोंसे, न तपसे, न दानसे और न यज्ञसे ही देखा जा सकता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: na—never; aham—I; vedaiḥ—by study of the Vedas; na—never; tapasā—by serious penances; na—never; dānena—by charity; na—never; cha—also; ijyayā—by worship; śhakyaḥ—it is possible; evam-vidhaḥ—like this; draṣhṭum—to see; dṛiṣhṭavān—seeing; asi—you are; mām—me; yathā—as

verses.sanskrit:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन।

ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप।।11.54।।
verses.transliteration:
bhaktyā tv ananyayā śhakya aham evaṁ-vidho ’rjuna
jñātuṁ draṣhṭuṁ cha tattvena praveṣhṭuṁ cha parantapa
verses.translation: But by single-minded devotion, O Arjuna, it is possible to truly know, to see, and to enter into Me, who am of this form, O harasser of foes.
verses.hindi: ।।11.54।। परन्तु हे शत्रुतापन अर्जुन ! इस प्रकार (चतुर्भुजरूपवाला) मैं अनन्यभक्तिसे ही तत्त्वसे जाननेमें, सगुणरूपसे देखनेमें और प्राप्त करनेमें शक्य हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: bhaktyā—by devotion; tu—alone; ananyayā—unalloyed; śhakyaḥ—possible; aham—I; evam-vidhaḥ—like this; arjuna—Arjun; jñātum—to be known; draṣhṭum—to be seen; cha—and; tattvena—truly; praveṣhṭum—to enter into (union with me); cha—and; parantapa—scorcher of foes

verses.sanskrit:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः।

निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव।।11.55।।
verses.transliteration:
mat-karma-kṛin mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ
nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣhu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava
verses.translation: Whoever works for Me, regards Me as the highest and is devoted to Me, free from attachment and without animosity towards any creature, they come to Me, O Arjuna.
verses.hindi: ।।11.55।। हे पाण्डवन ! जो मेरे लिये ही कर्म करनेवाला, मेरे ही परायण और मेरा ही भक्त है तथा सर्वथा आसक्तिरहित और प्राणिमात्रके साथ निर्वैर है, वह भक्त मेरेको प्राप्त होता है।
verses.wordMeaning: mat-karma-kṛit—perform duties for my sake; mat-paramaḥ—considering me the Supreme; mat-bhaktaḥ—devoted to me; saṅga-varjitaḥ—free from attachment; nirvairaḥ—without malice; sarva-bhūteṣhu—toward all entities; yaḥ—who; saḥ—he; mām—to me; eti—comes; pāṇḍava—Arjun, the son of Pandu

verses.sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः | शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ||
verses.transliteration: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ | śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ ||
verses.translation: One who is equal to friends and enemies, honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment...
verses.hindi: जो शत्रु और मित्र में, मान और अपमान में, सर्दी-गर्मी और सुख-दुःख में समद्र्शी हो, और आसक्ति से रहित हो — वह भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: A true devotee is equipoised under all conditions. Such a person is dear to Krishna.
verses.commentary: A true devotee is equipoised under all conditions. Such a person is dear to Krishna.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते | सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ||
verses.transliteration: ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate | sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam ||
verses.translation: Others, who worship the imperishable, indefinable, unmanifest, omnipresent, unthinkable, unchangeable, immovable, and eternal...
verses.hindi: जो अक्षर, अनिर्देश्य, अव्यक्त, सर्वव्यापी, अचिंत्य, अचल और ध्रुव की उपासना करते हैं...
verses.wordMeaning: Devotion to the unmanifest (nirguna Brahman) is harder but also leads to liberation. The path of saguna (with form) is easier for embodied beings.
verses.commentary: Devotion to the unmanifest (nirguna Brahman) is harder but also leads to liberation. The path of saguna (with form) is easier for embodied beings.

verses.sanskrit: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः।ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः।।12.4।।
verses.transliteration: sanniyamyendriya-grāmaṁ  sarvatra    sama-buddhayaḥ  te  prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite    ratāḥ
verses.translation: Having subdued all the senses, being even-minded, and engaged in the welfare of all beings, they too come to Me only.
verses.hindi: ।।12.4।।जो अपनी इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके अचिन्त्य, सब जगह परिपूर्ण, अनिर्देश्य, कूटस्थ, अचल, ध्रुव, अक्षर और अव्यक्तकी उपासना करते हैं, वे प्राणिमात्रके हितमें रत और सब जगह समबुद्धिवाले मनुष्य मुझे ही प्राप्त होते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: sanniyamya-controlling;    indriya-grāmam—all  the senses; sarvatra—everywhere;     sama-buddayaḥ—equally  disposed;   te-they;    prāpnuvanti—achieve;    mām—unto    Me; eva—certainly;  sarva-bhūtahite—all living  entities'   welfare;    ratāḥ—engaged.

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय।।12.9।।
verses.transliteration:
atha chittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śhaknoṣhi mayi sthiram
abhyāsa-yogena tato mām ichchhāptuṁ dhanañjaya
verses.translation: If now you are unable to focus your mind on Me, then seek to reach Me, O Arjuna, through the practice of repetition.
verses.hindi: ।।12.9।।अगर तू मनको मेरेमें अचलभावसे स्थिर (अर्पण) करनेमें समर्थ नहीं है, तो हे धनञ्जय ! अभ्यासयोगके द्वारा तू मेरी प्राप्तिकी इच्छा कर।
verses.wordMeaning: atha—if; chittam—mind; samādhātum—to fix; na śhaknoṣhi—(you) are unable; mayi—on me; sthiram—steadily; abhyāsa-yogena—by uniting with God through repeated practice; tataḥ—then; mām—me; ichchhā—desire; āptum—to attain; dhanañjaya—Arjun, the conqueror of wealth

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते।ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम्।।12.12।।
verses.transliteration:
śhreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṁ viśhiṣhyate
dhyānāt karma-phala-tyāgas tyāgāch chhāntir anantaram
verses.translation: Far better is knowledge of the Self than the repeated practice (of remembrance of the Lord). Better is meditation than this knowledge; better is renunciation of the fruits of action than meditation. From such renunciation, peace ensues.
verses.hindi: ।।12.12।।अभ्याससे शास्त्रज्ञान श्रेष्ठ है, शास्त्रज्ञानसे ध्यान श्रेष्ठ है और ध्यानसे भी सब कर्मोंके फलका त्याग श्रेष्ठ है। कर्मफलत्यागसे तत्काल ही परमशान्ति प्राप्त हो जाती है।
verses.wordMeaning: śhreyaḥ—better; hi—for; jñānam—knowledge; abhyāsāt—than (mechanical) practice; jñānāt—than knowledge; dhyānam—meditation; viśhiṣhyate—better; dhyānāt—than meditation; karma-phala-tyāgaḥ—renunciation of the fruits of actions; tyāgāt—renunciation; śhāntiḥ—peace; anantaram—immediately

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः।।12.16।।
verses.transliteration:
anapekṣhaḥ śhuchir dakṣha udāsīno gata-vyathaḥ
sarvārambha-parityāgī yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
verses.translation: He who is free from desires, who is pure, expert, indifferent, and free from agony, who has renounced every undertaking—he is dear to me.
verses.hindi: ।।12.16।।जो आकाङ्क्षासे रहित, बाहर-भीतरसे पवित्र, दक्ष, उदासीन, व्यथासे रहित और सभी आरम्भोंका अर्थात् नये-नये कर्मोंके आरम्भका सर्वथा त्यागी है, वह मेरा भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: anapekṣhaḥ—indifferent to worldly gain; śhuchiḥ—pure; dakṣhaḥ—skillful; udāsīnaḥ—without cares; gata-vyathaḥ—untroubled; sarva-ārambha—of all undertakings; parityāgī—renouncer; saḥ—who; mat-bhaktaḥ—my devotee; saḥ—he; me—to ne; priyaḥ—very dear

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत | क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ||
verses.transliteration: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata | kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama ||
verses.translation: And also know Me to be the knower of the field in all fields, O Bharata. I consider true knowledge to be the understanding of the field and the knower of the field.
verses.hindi: और हे भारत! सभी क्षेत्रों में क्षेत्रज्ञ (क्षेत्र को जानने वाला) भी मुझे ही जानो। क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ का यह ज्ञान ही मेरे मत में सच्चा ज्ञान है।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the fundamental metaphysical distinction: the "field" (body, mind, senses, and all their modifications) and the "knower of the field" (pure consciousness). The body is the field — it changes, ages, dies. The knower of the field is the eternal witness. Identifying with the field is ignorance; recognizing oneself as the knower is wisdom.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the fundamental metaphysical distinction: the "field" (body, mind, senses, and all their modifications) and the "knower of the field" (pure consciousness). The body is the field — it changes, ages, dies. The knower of the field is the eternal witness. Identifying with the field is ignorance; recognizing oneself as the knower is wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् | विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: samaṃ sarvebhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram | vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||
verses.translation: He who sees the Supreme Lord dwelling equally in all beings — not perishing when they perish — he truly sees.
verses.hindi: जो सभी प्राणियों में समान रूप से स्थित परमेश्वर को देखता है, नाशवान में अविनाशी को देखता है — वही वास्तव में देखता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of true sight: seeing the eternal, unchanging consciousness in all temporary forms. Most people see only the forms — the differences, the distinctions, the personalities. The wise see the one consciousness that animates all forms equally.
verses.commentary: The definition of true sight: seeing the eternal, unchanging consciousness in all temporary forms. Most people see only the forms — the differences, the distinctions, the personalities. The wise see the one consciousness that animates all forms equally.

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च।जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्।।13.9।।
verses.transliteration:
indriyārtheṣhu vairāgyam anahankāra eva cha
janma-mṛityu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣhānudarśhanam
verses.translation: Absence of desire for sense-objects, and also absence of egotism, the recognition of evil in birth, death, old age, disease, and sorrow;
verses.hindi: ।।13.9।।इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें वैराग्यका होना, अहंकारका भी न होना और जन्म, मृत्यु, वृद्धावस्था तथा व्याधियोंमें दुःखरूप दोषोंको बार-बार देखना।
verses.wordMeaning: indriya-artheṣhu—toward objects of the senses; vairāgyam—dispassion; anahankāraḥ—absence of egotism; eva cha—and also; janma—of birth; mṛityu—death; jarā—old age; vyādhi—disease; duḥkha—evils; doṣha—faults; anudarśhanam—perception;

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्।एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोन्यथा।।13.12।।
verses.transliteration:
adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvaṁ tattva-jñānārtha-darśhanam
etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṁ yad ato ’nyathā
verses.translation: Constant contemplation on the knowledge pertaining to the self, reflection for the attainment of knowledge of the truth—this is declared to be knowledge, and what is contrary to it is ignorance.
verses.hindi: ।।13.12।।अध्यात्मज्ञानमें नित्य-निरन्तर रहना, तत्त्वज्ञानके अर्थरूप परमात्माको सब जगह देखना -- यह (पूर्वोक्त साधन-समुदाय) तो ज्ञान है; और जो इसके विपरीत है वह अज्ञान है -- ऐसा कहा गया है।
verses.wordMeaning: adhyātma—spiritual; jñāna—knowledge; nityatvam—constancy; tattva-jñāna—knowledge of spiritual principles; artha—for; darśhanam—philosophy; etat—all this; jñānam—knowledge; iti—thus; proktam—declared; ajñānam—ignorance; yat—what; ataḥ—to this; anyathā—contrary

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्।।13.16।।
verses.transliteration:
bahir antaśh cha bhūtānām acharaṁ charam eva cha
sūkṣhmatvāt tad avijñeyaṁ dūra-sthaṁ chāntike cha tat
verses.translation: It is within and without all beings; It is unmoving yet moving; It is so subtle that none can comprehend it; It is far away yet very near.
verses.hindi: ।।13.16।।वे परमात्मा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके बाहर-भीतर परिपूर्ण हैं और चर-अचर प्राणियोंके रूपमें भी वे ही हैं एवं दूर-से-दूर तथा नजदीक-से-नजदीक भी वे ही हैं। वे अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म होनेसे जाननेका विषय नहीं हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: bahiḥ—outside; antaḥ—inside; cha—and; bhūtānām—all living beings; acharam—not moving; charam—moving; eva—indeed; cha—and; sūkṣhmatvāt—due to subtlety; tat—he; avijñeyam—incomprehensible; dūra-stham—very far away; cha—and; antike—very near; cha—also; tat—he

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्।।13.18।।
verses.transliteration:
jyotiṣhām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param uchyate
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ jñāna-gamyaṁ hṛidi sarvasya viṣhṭhitam
verses.translation: The light of all lights is said to be beyond Tamas (darkness); it is known to be knowledge, to be attained through knowledge, and to be present in the hearts of all.
verses.hindi: ।।13.18।।वह परमात्मा सम्पूर्ण ज्योतियोंका भी ज्योति और अज्ञानसे अत्यन्त परे कहा गया है। वह ज्ञानस्वरूप, जाननेयोग्य, ज्ञान(साधन-समुदाय) से प्राप्त करनेयोग्य और सबके हृदयमें विराजमान है।
verses.wordMeaning: jyotiṣhām—in all luminarie; api—and; tat—that; jyotiḥ—the source of light; tamasaḥ—the darkness; param—beyond; uchyate—is said (to be); jñānam—knowledge; jñeyam—the object of knowledge; jñāna-gamyam—the goal of knowledge; hṛidi—within the heart; sarvasya—of all living beings; viṣhṭhitam—dwells

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः।।13.23।।
verses.transliteration:
upadraṣhṭānumantā cha bhartā bhoktā maheśhvaraḥ
paramātmeti chāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣhaḥ paraḥ
verses.translation: The self in the body is called the spectator, approver, supporter, experiencer, great lord, and supreme self.
verses.hindi: ।।13.23।।यह पुरुष प्रकृति-(शरीर-) के साथ सम्बन्ध रखनेसे 'उपद्रष्टा', उसके साथ मिलकर सम्मति, अनुमति देनेसे 'अनुमन्ता', अपनेको उसका भरणपोषण करनेवाला माननेसे 'भर्ता', उसके सङ्गसे सुखदुःख भोगनेसे 'भोक्ता', और अपनेको उसका स्वामी माननेसे 'महेश्वर' बन जाता है। परन्तु स्वरूपसे यह पुरुष 'परमात्मा' कहा जाता है। यह देहमें रहता हुआ भी देहसे पर (सम्बन्ध-रहित) ही है।
verses.wordMeaning: upadraṣhṭā—the witness; anumantā—the permitter; cha—and; bhartā—the supporter; bhoktā—the transcendental enjoyer; mahā-īśhvaraḥ—the ultimate controller; parama-ātmā—Superme Soul; iti—that; cha api—and also; uktaḥ—is said; dehe—within the body; asmin—this; puruṣhaḥ paraḥ—the Supreme Lord

verses.sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह।सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते।।13.24।।
verses.transliteration:
ya evaṁ vetti puruṣhaṁ prakṛitiṁ cha guṇaiḥ saha
sarvathā vartamāno ’pi na sa bhūyo ’bhijāyate
verses.translation: He who understands the Self and Prakriti, along with the Gunas, will not be born again, no matter what state he may be in.
verses.hindi: ।।13.24।।इस प्रकार पुरुषको और गुणोंके सहित प्रकृतिको जो मनुष्य अलग-अलग जानता है, वह सब तरहका बर्ताव करता हुआ भी फिर जन्म नहीं लेता।
verses.wordMeaning: yaḥ—who; evam—thus; vetti—understand; puruṣham—Puruṣh; prakṛitim—the material nature; cha—and; guṇaiḥ—the three modes of nature; saha—with; sarvathā—in every way; vartamānaḥ—situated; api—although; na—not; saḥ—they; bhūyaḥ—again; abhijāyate—take birth

verses.sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे।।13.25।।
verses.transliteration:
dhyānenātmani paśhyanti kechid ātmānam ātmanā
anye sānkhyena yogena karma-yogena chāpare
verses.translation: Some perceive the Self within the self (body) through meditation of the mind, others through Sankhya Yoga, and still others through Karma Yoga.
verses.hindi: ।।13.25।।कई मनुष्य ध्यानयोगके द्वारा, कई सांख्ययोगके द्वारा और कई कर्मयोगके द्वारा अपने-आपसे अपने-आपमें परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव करते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: dhyānena—through meditation; ātmani—within one’s heart; paśhyanti—percieve; kechit—some; ātmānam—the Supreme soul; ātmanā—by the mind; anye—others; sānkhyena—through cultivation of knowledge; yogena—the yog system; karma-yogena—union with God with through path of action; cha—and; apare—others

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्।।13.29।।
verses.transliteration:
samaṁ paśhyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśhvaram
na hinasty ātmanātmānaṁ tato yāti parāṁ gatim
verses.translation: For, seeing the ruler abiding alike in every place, he does not injure himself with his own mind and therefore reaches the highest goal.
verses.hindi: ।।13.29।।क्योंकि सब जगह समरूपसे स्थित ईश्वरको समरूपसे देखनेवाला मनुष्य अपने-आपसे अपनी हिंसा नहीं करता, इसलिये वह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: samam—equally; paśhyan—see; hi—indeed; sarvatra—everywhere; samavasthitam—equally present; īśhvaram—God as the Supreme soul; na—do not; hinasti—degrade; ātmanā—by one’s mind; ātmānam—the self; tataḥ—thereby; yāti—reach; parām—the supreme; gatim—destination

verses.sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव | न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ||
verses.transliteration: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava | na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave ||
verses.translation: O Keshava (Krishna), I see only inauspicious omens. I do not see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.
verses.hindi: हे केशव! मैं अपशकुन ही देख रहा हूँ। युद्ध में स्वजनों को मारने में मुझे कोई कल्याण नहीं दिखता।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees inauspicious omens because his perception is clouded by attachment. What is actually his dharma appears inauspicious because he identifies with bodily relations rather than the soul.

verses.sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता | यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst forth at once in the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One.
verses.hindi: आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूर्य उदय हों तो जो प्रकाश हो, वह उस महात्मा (विश्वरूप) के तेज के समान होगा।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.
verses.commentary: Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form (Vishwarupa) — infinite, terrifying, and magnificent. The comparison to a thousand suns conveys its overwhelming brilliance.

verses.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते।।13.33।।
verses.transliteration:
yathā sarva-gataṁ saukṣhmyād ākāśhaṁ nopalipyate
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate
verses.translation: As the all-pervading ether is not tainted due to its subtlety, even so, the self abiding in the body is not tainted everywhere.
verses.hindi: ।।13.33।।जैसे सब जगह व्याप्त आकाश अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म होनेसे कहीं भी लिप्त नहीं होता, ऐसे ही सब जगह परिपूर्ण आत्मा किसी भी देहमें लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: yathā—as; sarva-gatam—all-pervading; saukṣhmyāt—due to subtlety; ākāśham—the space; na—not; upalipyate—is contaminated; sarvatra—everywhere; avasthitaḥ—situated; dehe—the body; tathā—similarly; ātmā—the soul; na—not; upalipyate—is contaminated

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यतां गतं पार्थ मायया ते तदात्मकम् | यत्तु सत्यं सनातनं तदहं वदतः स्म ते ||
verses.transliteration: adṛśyatāṃ gataṃ pārtha māyayā te tadātmakam | yattu satyaṃ sanātanaṃ tadahaṃ vadataḥ sma te ||
verses.translation: O Partha, the cosmic form you saw was manifested by My Yoga-Maya. Now I shall reveal to you My eternal form.
verses.hindi: हे पार्थ! जो तुमने देखा वह मेरी योगमाया से प्रकट किया गया था। अब मैं तुम्हें अपना शाश्वत रूप बताता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.
verses.commentary: The cosmic form (Vishwarupa) is a temporary manifestation. Krishna's true form is eternal and personal — the beautiful two-armed form.

verses.sanskrit: स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.transliteration: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
verses.translation: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
verses.hindi: अपने स्वधर्म में मरना भला है, चाहे वह अपूर्ण हो; परधर्म को अच्छी तरह से करना भयावह है।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.
verses.commentary: One of the most practical verses. Following another's path, even if done perfectly, is dangerous because it is not aligned with your nature. Your own dharma, even if imperfectly practiced, leads to genuine growth.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसम्भवाः | निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ||
verses.transliteration: sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisambhavāḥ | nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam ||
verses.translation: Sattva, rajas, and tamas — these three qualities born of nature bind the embodied, eternal soul to the body.
verses.hindi: हे महाबाहो! सत्त्व, रज और तम — ये प्रकृति से उत्पन्न तीन गुण अव्यय देही (आत्मा) को शरीर में बाँधते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: The three gunas are the fundamental operating modes of all matter and mind. Sattva = clarity, light, harmony. Rajas = energy, passion, restlessness, ambition. Tamas = inertia, heaviness, delusion, lethargy. Every thought, food, action, and environment pushes us toward one of these three states.
verses.commentary: The three gunas are the fundamental operating modes of all matter and mind. Sattva = clarity, light, harmony. Rajas = energy, passion, restlessness, ambition. Tamas = inertia, heaviness, delusion, lethargy. Every thought, food, action, and environment pushes us toward one of these three states.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता।।14.4।।
verses.transliteration:
sarva-yoniṣhu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ
tāsāṁ brahma mahad yonir ahaṁ bīja-pradaḥ pitā
verses.translation: Whatever forms are produced in any womb, O Arjuna, the Prakṛti is their great womb, and I am the sowing father.
verses.hindi: ।।14.4।।हे कुन्तीनन्दन ! सम्पूर्ण योनियोंमें प्राणियोंके जितने शरीर पैदा होते हैं, उन सबकी मूल प्रकृति तो माता है और मैं बीज-स्थापन करनेवाला पिता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: sarva—all; yoniṣhu—species of life; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; mūrtayaḥ—forms; sambhavanti—are produced; yāḥ—which; tāsām—of all of them; brahma-mahat—great material nature; yoniḥ—womb; aham—I; bīja-pradaḥ—seed-giving; pitā—Father

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत।ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत।।14.9।।
verses.transliteration:
sattvaṁ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata
jñānam āvṛitya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta
verses.translation: Sattva generates attachment to pleasure, Rajas to action, O Arjuna. But Tamas, obscuring knowledge, generates attachment to negligence.
verses.hindi: ।।14.9।।हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन ! सत्त्वगुण सुखमें और रजोगुण कर्ममें लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजय करता है तथा तमोगुण ज्ञानको ढककर एवं प्रमादमें भी लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजंय करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: sattvam—mode of goodness; sukhe—to happiness; sañjayati—binds; rajaḥ—mode of passion; karmaṇi—toward actions; bhārata—Arjun, the son of Bharat; jñānam—wisdom; āvṛitya—clouds; tu—but; tamaḥ—mode of ignorance; pramāde—to delusion; sañjayati—binds; uta—indeed

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा।रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ।।14.12।।
verses.transliteration:
lobhaḥ pravṛittir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśhamaḥ spṛihā
rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛiddhe bharatarṣhabha
verses.translation: Greed, activity, undertaking of work, restlessness, and longing—these arise, O Arjuna, when Rajas predominates.
verses.hindi: ।।14.12।।हे भरतवंशमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन ! रजोगुणके बढ़नेपर लोभ, प्रवृत्ति, कर्मोंका आरम्भ, अशान्ति और स्पृहा -- ये वृत्तियाँ पैदा होती हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: lobhaḥ—greed; pravṛittiḥ—activity; ārambhaḥ—exertion; karmaṇām—for fruitive actions; aśhamaḥ—restlessness; spṛihā—craving; rajasi—of the mode of passion; etāni—these; jāyante—develop; vivṛiddhe—when predominates; bharata-ṛiṣhabha—the best of the Bharatas, Arjun;

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम्।रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्।।14.16।।
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇaḥ sukṛitasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṁ nirmalaṁ phalam
rajasas tu phalaṁ duḥkham ajñānaṁ tamasaḥ phalam
verses.translation: It is said that the fruit of a good deed is pure and of the nature of Sattva; the fruit of Rajas is pain; and the fruit of Tamas is ignorance.
verses.hindi: ।।14.16।।(विवेकी पुरुषोंने) शुभ-कर्मका तो सात्त्विक निर्मल फल कहा है, राजस कर्मका फल दुःख कहा है और तामस कर्मका फल अज्ञान (मूढ़ता) कहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: karmaṇaḥ—of action; su-kṛitasya—pure; āhuḥ—is said; sāttvikam—mode of goodness; nirmalam—pure; phalam—result; rajasaḥ—mode of passion; tu—indeed; phalam—result; duḥkham—pain; ajñānam—ignorance; tamasaḥ—mode of ignorance; phalam—result

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः।जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः।।14.18।।
verses.transliteration:
ūrdhvaṁ gachchhanti sattva-sthā madhye tiṣhṭhanti rājasāḥ
jaghanya-guṇa-vṛitti-sthā adho gachchhanti tāmasāḥ
verses.translation: Those who rest in Sattva ascend upwards; those who abide in Rajas stay in the middle; and those, abiding in the tendencies of Tamas descend downwards.
verses.hindi: ।।14.18।।सत्त्वगुणमें स्थित मनुष्य ऊर्ध्वलोकोंमें जाते हैं, रजोगुणमें स्थित मनुष्य मृत्युलोकमें जन्म लेते हैं और निन्दनीय तमोगुणकी वृत्तिमें स्थित मनुष्य अधोगतिमें जाते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: ūrdhvam—upward; gachchhanti—rise; sattva-sthāḥ—those situated in the mode of goodness; madhye—in the middle; tiṣhṭhanti—stay; rājasāḥ—those in the mode of passion; jaghanya—abominable; guṇa—quality; vṛitti-sthāḥ—engaged in activities; adhaḥ—down; gachchhanti—go; tāmasāḥ—those in the mode of ignorance

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते।।14.23।।
verses.transliteration:
udāsīna-vad āsīno guṇair yo na vichālyate
guṇā vartanta ity evaṁ yo ’vatiṣhṭhati neṅgate
verses.translation: He who sits like one unconcerned, undisturbed by the Gunas; who knows, 'It is the Gunas that are in motion,' and so remains unshaken;
verses.hindi: ।।14.23।।जो उदासीनकी तरह स्थित है और जो गुणोंके द्वारा विचलित नहीं किया जा सकता तथा गुण ही (गुणोंमें) बरत रहे हैं -- इस भावसे जो अपने स्वरूपमें ही स्थित रहता है और स्वयं कोई भी चेष्टा नहीं करता।
verses.wordMeaning: udāsīna-vat—neutral; āsīnaḥ—situated; guṇaiḥ—to the modes of material nature; yaḥ—who; na—not; vichālyate—are disturbed; guṇāḥ—modes of material nature; vartante—act; iti-evam—knowing it in this way; yaḥ—who; avatiṣhṭhati—established in the self; na—not; iṅgate—wavering

verses.sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः।।14.24।।
verses.transliteration:
sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sva-sthaḥ sama-loṣhṭāśhma-kāñchanaḥ
tulya-priyāpriyo dhīras tulya-nindātma-sanstutiḥ
verses.translation: He who is alike in pleasure and pain, who dwells in his Self, who looks upon a clod, a stone, and a piece of gold as of equal value, who remains the same towards things dear and hateful, and who is intelligent, who regards both blame and praise of himself as equal.
verses.hindi: ।।14.24।।जो धीर मनुष्य सुख-दुःखमें सम तथा अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है; जो मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर और सोनेमें सम रहता है जो प्रिय-अप्रियमें तथा अपनी निन्दा-स्तुतिमें सम रहता है; जो मान-अपमानमें तथा मित्र-शत्रुके पक्षमें सम रहता है जो सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भका त्यागी है, वह मनुष्य गुणातीत कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: sama—alike; duḥkha—distress; sukhaḥ—happiness; sva-sthaḥ—established in the self; sama—equally; loṣhṭa—a clod; aśhma—stone; kāñchanaḥ—gold; tulya—of equal value; priya—pleasant; apriyaḥ—unpleasant; dhīraḥ—steady; tulya—the same; nindā—blame; ātma-sanstutiḥ—praise;

verses.sanskrit: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते।।14.25।।
verses.transliteration:
mānāpamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāri-pakṣhayoḥ
sarvārambha-parityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa uchyate
verses.translation: He who is the same in honor and dishonor, and the same to friend and foe, and who has abandoned all enterprises—he is said to have risen above the Gunas.
verses.hindi: ।।14.25।।जो धीर मनुष्य सुख-दुःखमें सम तथा अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है; जो मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर और सोनेमें सम रहता है जो प्रिय-अप्रियमें तथा अपनी निन्दा-स्तुतिमें सम रहता है जो मान-अपमानमें तथा मित्र-शत्रुके पक्षमें सम रहता है; जो सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भका त्यागी है, वह मनुष्य गुणातीत कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: māna—honor; apamānayoḥ—dishonor; tulyaḥ—equal; tulyaḥ—equal; mitra—friend; ari—foe; pakṣhayoḥ—to the parties; sarva—all; ārambha—enterprises; parityāgī—renouncer; guṇa-atītaḥ—risen above the three modes of material nature; saḥ—they; uchyate—are said to have

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् | छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ||
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam | chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit ||
verses.translation: They speak of an imperishable Ashvattha tree with its roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedas. He who knows it is the knower of the Vedas.
verses.hindi: अश्वत्थ वृक्ष (पीपल) को ऊर्ध्वमूल (ऊपर जड़) और अधःशाखा (नीचे शाखाएँ) वाला अव्यय (अनश्वर) कहते हैं। उसके पत्ते वेद हैं। जो इसे जानता है वह वेद-वेत्ता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic tree with roots above (in Brahman) and branches below (in the manifest world) is a profound metaphor for existence. Our world of appearances grows downward from a transcendent root. The tree is "ashvattha" — impermanent, never the same tomorrow (ashva = tomorrow; stha = standing = that which does not stand till tomorrow). The only permanent thing is the root — Brahman.
verses.commentary: The cosmic tree with roots above (in Brahman) and branches below (in the manifest world) is a profound metaphor for existence. Our world of appearances grows downward from a transcendent root. The tree is "ashvattha" — impermanent, never the same tomorrow (ashva = tomorrow; stha = standing = that which does not stand till tomorrow). The only permanent thing is the root — Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः | मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ||
verses.transliteration: mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ | manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati ||
verses.translation: The eternal individual soul in the world of living beings is indeed a fragment of My own Self. It draws to itself the senses — of which the mind is the sixth — seated in material nature.
verses.hindi: जीव-जगत में जीव मेरा ही सनातन अंश है। वह प्रकृति में स्थित मन सहित छः इन्द्रियों को अपनी ओर खींचता है।
verses.wordMeaning: A remarkable verse: the individual soul (jiva) is an eternal fragment of Krishna (Brahman). Not a creation, not a copy — a fragment. The fragment and the whole share the same essential nature. The ocean and a drop of ocean are both H2O. The fragment draws the senses to itself — it is what animates the body.
verses.commentary: A remarkable verse: the individual soul (jiva) is an eternal fragment of Krishna (Brahman). Not a creation, not a copy — a fragment. The fragment and the whole share the same essential nature. The ocean and a drop of ocean are both H2O. The fragment draws the senses to itself — it is what animates the body.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च | वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ||
verses.transliteration: sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ ca | vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham ||
verses.translation: I am seated in the heart of all beings. From Me come memory, knowledge, and removal of doubt. By all the Vedas I alone am to be known; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
verses.hindi: मैं सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निहित हूँ। मुझसे ही स्मृति, ज्ञान और अपोहन (संशय-निवृत्ति) होते हैं। सभी वेदों से केवल मैं ही जानने योग्य हूँ। वेदान्त का कर्ता और वेद को जानने वाला भी मैं ही हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals the most intimate truth: he is seated in the heart of every being as the very source of their intelligence. Memory, knowledge, even the removal of confusion — all flow from this inner source. Every moment of clarity, every flash of understanding, is literally a manifestation of the divine intelligence within.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals the most intimate truth: he is seated in the heart of every being as the very source of their intelligence. Memory, knowledge, even the removal of confusion — all flow from this inner source. Every moment of clarity, every flash of understanding, is literally a manifestation of the divine intelligence within.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः।तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी।।15.4।।
verses.transliteration:
tataḥ padaṁ tat parimārgitavyaṁ
yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ
tam eva chādyaṁ puruṣhaṁ prapadye
yataḥ pravṛittiḥ prasṛitā purāṇī
verses.translation: Then, one should seek that goal, attaining which one never returns. One should seek refuge with that Primal Person from whom this ancient activity streamed forth.
verses.hindi: ।।15.4।।उसके बाद उस परमपद-(परमात्मा-) की खोज करनी चाहिये जिसको प्राप्त होनेपर मनुष्य फिर लौटकर संसारमें नहीं आते और जिससे अनादिकालसे चली आनेवाली यह सृष्टि विस्तारको प्राप्त हुई है, उस आदिपुरुष परमात्माके ही मैं शरण हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: tataḥ—then; padam—place; tat—that; parimārgitavyam—one must search out; yasmin—where; gatāḥ—having gone; na—not; nivartanti—return; bhūyaḥ—again; tam—to him; eva—certainly; cha—and; ādyam—original; puruṣham—the Supreme Lord; prapadye—take refuge; yataḥ—whence; pravṛittiḥ—the activity; prasṛitā—streamed forth; purāṇi—very old

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
