verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च।अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते।।15.9।।
verses.transliteration:
śhrotraṁ chakṣhuḥ sparśhanaṁ cha rasanaṁ ghrāṇam eva cha
adhiṣhṭhāya manaśh chāyaṁ viṣhayān upasevate
verses.translation: Presiding over the ear, the eye, the sense of touch, the tongue, the nose, and the mind, It experiences these objects of the senses.
verses.hindi: ।।15.9।।यह जीवात्मा मनका आश्रय लेकर श्रोत्र, नेत्र, त्वचा, रसना और घ्राण -- इन पाँचों इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: śhrotram—ears; chakṣhuḥ—eyes; sparśhanam—the sense of touch; cha—and; rasanam—tongue; ghrāṇam—nose; eva—also; cha—and; adhiṣhṭhāya—grouped around; manaḥ—mind; cha—also; ayam—they; viṣhayān—sense objects; upasevate—savors

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम्।यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्।।15.12।।
verses.transliteration:
yad āditya-gataṁ tejo jagad bhāsayate ’khilam
yach chandramasi yach chāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam
verses.translation: Know that the brilliance which illumines the whole universe in the sun, the moon, and fire is Mine.
verses.hindi: ।।15.12।।सूर्यमें आया हुआ जो तेज सम्पूर्ण जगत् को प्रकाशित करता है और जो तेज चन्द्रमामें है तथा जो तेज अग्निमें है, उस तेजको मेरा ही जान।
verses.wordMeaning: yat—which; āditya-gatam—in the sun; tejaḥ—brilliance; jagat—solar system; bhāsayate—illuminates; akhilam—entire; yat—which; chandramasi—in the moon; yat—which; cha—also; agnau—in the fire; tat—that; tejaḥ—brightness; viddhi—know; māmakam—mine

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते।।15.16।।
verses.transliteration:
dvāv imau puruṣhau loke kṣharaśh chākṣhara eva cha
kṣharaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭa-stho ’kṣhara uchyate
verses.translation: There are two kinds of persons spoken of in the sastra: the perishable (ksara) and the imperishable (aksara). All beings are perishable, while the imperishable is called the unchanging (kutastha).
verses.hindi: ।।15.16।।इस संसारमें क्षर (नाशवान्) और अक्षर (अविनाशी) -- ये दो प्रकारके पुरुष हैं। सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके शरीर नाशवान् और कूटस्थ (जीवात्मा) अविनाशी कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: dvau—two; imau—these; puruṣhau—beings; loke—in creation; kṣharaḥ—the perishable; cha—and; akṣharaḥ—the imperishable; eva—even; cha—and; kṣharaḥ—the perishable; sarvāṇi—all; bhūtāni—beings; kūṭa-sthaḥ—the liberated; akṣharaḥ—the imperishable; uchyate—is said

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः।।15.18।।
verses.transliteration:
yasmāt kṣharam atīto ’ham akṣharād api chottamaḥ
ato ’smi loke vede cha prathitaḥ puruṣhottamaḥ
verses.translation: Because I transcend the perishable person and am also higher than the imperishable one, therefore I am referred to in the Smrti and the Veda as the Supreme Person (Purusotama).
verses.hindi: ।।15.18।।मैं क्षरसे अतीत हूँ और अक्षरसे भी उत्तम हूँ, इसलिये लोकमें और वेदमें पुरुषोत्तम नामसे प्रसिद्ध हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: yasmāt—hence; kṣharam—to the perishable; atītaḥ—transcendental; aham—I; akṣharāt—to the imperishable; api—even; cha—and; uttamaḥ—transcendental; ataḥ—therefore; asmi—I am; loke—in the world; vede—in the Vedas; cha—and; prathitaḥ—celebrated; puruṣha-uttamaḥ—as the Supreme Divine Personality

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः | दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ||
verses.transliteration: abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ | dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam ||
verses.translation: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, and straightforwardness...
verses.hindi: अभय (निर्भयता), सत्त्व की शुद्धि, ज्ञानयोग में स्थिति, दान, दम (इन्द्रिय-संयम), यज्ञ, स्वाध्याय, तप, और आर्जव (सरलता)...
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna lists twenty-six divine qualities that constitute the "daivi sampat" (divine wealth). This is the Gita's most comprehensive character portrait — the ideal human being. These are not commandments but descriptions of the natural qualities that emerge when one lives in alignment with truth. Fearlessness heads the list — it is the foundational quality from which all others flow.
verses.commentary: Krishna lists twenty-six divine qualities that constitute the "daivi sampat" (divine wealth). This is the Gita's most comprehensive character portrait — the ideal human being. These are not commandments but descriptions of the natural qualities that emerge when one lives in alignment with truth. Fearlessness heads the list — it is the foundational quality from which all others flow.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत | श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ||
verses.transliteration: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhāḥ sa eva saḥ ||
verses.translation: The faith of each person, O Bharata, accords with their natural disposition. A person is made of their faith; what their faith is, that, verily, they are.
verses.hindi: हे भारत! प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की श्रद्धा उसके स्वभाव (सत्त्व) के अनुसार होती है। यह पुरुष श्रद्धामय है — जैसी श्रद्धा, वैसा पुरुष।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."
verses.commentary: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."

verses.sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च।अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्।।16.4।।
verses.transliteration:
dambho darpo ’bhimānaśh cha krodhaḥ pāruṣhyam eva cha
ajñānaṁ chābhijātasya pārtha sampadam āsurīm
verses.translation: Pompousness, arrogance, self-conceit, wrath, rudeness, and ignorance—these, O Arjuna, belong to one who is born with a demonic destiny.
verses.hindi: ।।16.4।।हे पृथानन्दन ! दम्भ करना, घमण्ड करना, अभिमान करना, क्रोध करना, कठोरता रखना और अविवेकका होना भी -- ये सभी आसुरीसम्पदाको प्राप्त हुए मनुष्यके लक्षण हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: dambhaḥ—hypocrisy; darpaḥ—arrogance; abhimānaḥ—conceit; cha—and; krodhaḥ—anger; pāruṣhyam—harshness; eva—certainly; cha—and; ajñānam—ignorance; cha—and; abhijātasya—of those who possess; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; sampadam—qualities; āsurīm—demoniac

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः।प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः।।16.9।।
verses.transliteration:
etāṁ dṛiṣhṭim avaṣhṭabhya naṣhṭātmāno ’lpa-buddhayaḥ
prabhavanty ugra-karmāṇaḥ kṣhayāya jagato ’hitāḥ
verses.translation: Holding this view, these men of lost souls and feeble understanding do cruel deeds, leading to the destruction of the world.
verses.hindi: ।।16.9।।उपर्युक्त (नास्तिक) दृष्टिका आश्रय लेनेवाले जो मनुष्य अपने नित्य स्वरूपको नहीं मानते, जिनकी बुद्धि तुच्छ है, जो उग्रकर्मा और संसारके शत्रु हैं, उन मनुष्योंकी सामर्थ्यका उपयोग जगत्का नाश करनेके लिये ही होता है।
verses.wordMeaning: etām—such; dṛiṣhṭim—views; avaṣhṭabhya—holding; naṣhṭa—misdirected; ātmānaḥ—souls; alpa-buddhayaḥ—of small intellect; prabhavanti—arise; ugra—cruel; karmāṇaḥ—actions; kṣhayāya—destruction; jagataḥ—of the world; ahitāḥ—enemies

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः।ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्।।16.12।।
verses.transliteration:
āśhā-pāśha-śhatair baddhāḥ kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ
īhante kāma-bhogārtham anyāyenārtha-sañchayān
verses.translation: Bound by hundreds of fetters of hopes, given over to desire and anger, they strive unjustly to gather wealth for the gratification of their desires.
verses.hindi: ।।16.12।।वे आशाकी सैकड़ों फाँसियोंसे बँधे हुए मनुष्य काम-क्रोधके परायण होकर पदार्थोंका भोग करनेके लिये अन्यायपूर्वक धन-संचय करनेकी चेष्टा करते रहते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: āśhā-pāśha—bondage of desires; śhataiḥ—by hundreds; baddhāḥ—bound; kāma—lust; krodha—anger; parāyaṇāḥ—dedicated to; īhante—strive; kāma—lust; bhoga—gratification of the senses; artham—for; anyāyena—by unjust means; artha—wealth; sañchayān—to accumulate

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः।प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ।।16.16।।
verses.transliteration: aneka-citta-vibhrāntā    moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ prasaktāḥ   kāma-bhogeṣu    patanti narake  'śucau
verses.translation: Bewildered by numerous thoughts, ensnared in the net of delusion, addicted to sensual pleasures, they fall into a wretched Naraka.
verses.hindi: ।।16.16।।कामनाओंके कारण तरह-तरहसे भ्रमित चित्तवाले, मोह-जालमें अच्छी तरहसे फँसे हुए तथा पदार्थों और भोगोंमें अत्यन्त आसक्त रहनेवाले मनुष्य भयङ्कर नरकोंमें गिरते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: aneka—numerous;    citta-vibhrāntāḥ—perplexed  by  anxieties;  moha—of illusions;  jāla—by a   network;    samāvṛtāḥ—surrounded;   prasaktāḥ—attached; kāma—lust;  bhogeṣu—sense  gratification;   patanti—glides  down; narake—into hell; aśucau—unclean.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः।।16.18।।
verses.transliteration:
ahankāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ cha sanśhritāḥ
mām ātma-para-deheṣhu pradviṣhanto ’bhyasūyakāḥ
verses.translation: Depending on their egoism, power, and pride, as well as their desires and wrath, these malicious men hate Me in their own bodies and in those of others.
verses.hindi: ।।16.18।।वे अहङ्कार, हठ, घमण्ड, कामना और क्रोधका आश्रय लेनेवाले मनुष्य अपने और दूसरोंके शरीरमें रहनेवाले मुझ अन्तर्यामीके साथ द्वेष करते हैं तथा (मेरे और दूसरोंके गुणोंमें) दोष-दृष्टि रखते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: ahankāram—egotism; balam—strength; darpam—arrogance; kāmam—desire; krodham—anger; cha—and; sanśhritāḥ—covered by; mām—me; ātma-para-deheṣhu—within one’s own and bodies of others; pradviṣhantaḥ—abuse; abhyasūyakāḥ—the demoniac

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः।न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्।।16.23।।
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ śhāstra-vidhim utsṛijya vartate kāma-kārataḥ
na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṁ na parāṁ gatim
verses.translation: He who, abandoning the injunctions of the Sastras, acts under the influence of desire, attains neither perfection nor pleasure, nor the supreme state.
verses.hindi: ।।16.23।। जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिको छोड़कर अपनी इच्छासे मनमाना आचरण करता है, वह न सिद्धि-(अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि-) को, न सुखको और न परमगतिको ही प्राप्त होता है।
verses.wordMeaning: yaḥ—who; śhāstra-vidhim—scriptural injunctions; utsṛijya—discarding; vartate—act; kāma-kārataḥ—under the impulse of desire; na—neither; saḥ—they; siddhim—perfection; avāpnoti—attain; na—nor; sukham—happiness; na—nor; parām—the supreme; gatim—goal

verses.sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ।ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि।।16.24।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmāch chhāstraṁ pramāṇaṁ te kāryākārya-vyavasthitau
jñātvā śhāstra-vidhānoktaṁ karma kartum ihārhasi
verses.translation: Therefore, let the Sastra be your authority for determining what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing what is enjoined in the injunctions of the Sastra, you should perform work here.
verses.hindi: ।।16.24।।अतः तेरे लिये कर्तव्य-अकर्तव्यकी व्यवस्थामें शास्त्र ही प्रमाण है -- ऐसा जानकर तू इस लोकमें शास्त्र-विधिसे नियत कर्तव्य कर्म करनेयोग्य है।
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—therefore; śhāstram—scriptures; pramāṇam—authority; te—your; kārya—duty; akārya—forbidden action; vyavasthitau—in determining; jñātvā—having understood; śhāstra—scriptures; vidhāna—injunctions; uktam—as revealed; karma—actions; kartum—perform; iha—in this world; arhasi—you should

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत | श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ||
verses.transliteration: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhāḥ sa eva saḥ ||
verses.translation: The faith of each person, O Bharata, accords with their natural disposition. A person is made of their faith; what their faith is, that, verily, they are.
verses.hindi: हे भारत! प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की श्रद्धा उसके स्वभाव (सत्त्व) के अनुसार होती है। यह पुरुष श्रद्धामय है — जैसी श्रद्धा, वैसा पुरुष।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."
verses.commentary: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."

verses.sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः | अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ||
verses.transliteration: śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastattrividhaṃ naraiḥ | aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate ||
verses.translation: When that three-fold austerity is practiced by men of steadfastness and highest faith, without expectation of fruit — that is called sattvic austerity.
verses.hindi: जब वह त्रिविध तप (शरीर, वाणी, मन का) श्रेष्ठ श्रद्धा से युक्त और फल की आकांक्षा रहित पुरुषों द्वारा किया जाता है — उसे सात्त्विक तप कहते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: The highest form of discipline is practiced without expecting personal reward. The person who exercises, meditates, studies, and serves — not for ego gratification but because it is right — performs sattvic austerity. This is the meeting point of Chapter 17 and Chapter 2 (karma yoga): action without attachment to results.
verses.commentary: The highest form of discipline is practiced without expecting personal reward. The person who exercises, meditates, studies, and serves — not for ego gratification but because it is right — performs sattvic austerity. This is the meeting point of Chapter 17 and Chapter 2 (karma yoga): action without attachment to results.

verses.sanskrit: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः।प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः।।17.4।।
verses.transliteration:
yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣha-rakṣhānsi rājasāḥ
pretān bhūta-gaṇānśh chānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ
verses.translation: The sattvic types worship the gods; the rajasic types worship yaksas and rakshasas; and the others, the tamasic types, worship the departed ancestors and hosts of bhutas.
verses.hindi: ।।17.4।।सात्त्विक मनुष्य देवताओंका पूजन करते हैं, राजस मनुष्य यक्षों और राक्षसोंका और दूसरे जो तामस मनुष्य हैं, वे प्रेतों और भूतगणोंका पूजन करते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: yajante—worship; sāttvikāḥ—those in the mode of goodness; devān—celestial gods; yakṣha—semi-celestial beings who exude power and wealth; rakṣhānsi—powerful beings who embody sensual enjoyment, revenge, and wrath; rājasāḥ—those in the mode of passion; pretān-bhūta-gaṇān—ghosts and spirits; cha—and; anye—others; yajante—worship; tāmasāḥ—those in the mode of ignorance; janāḥ—persons

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः।आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः।।17.9।।
verses.transliteration:
kaṭv-amla-lavaṇāty-uṣhṇa- tīkṣhṇa-rūkṣha-vidāhinaḥ
āhārā rājasasyeṣhṭā duḥkha-śhokāmaya-pradāḥ
verses.translation: Foods that are bitter, sour, very salty, excessively heating, highly pungent, dry, and burning are all dear to Rajasika men; they cause pain, sorrow, and disease.
verses.hindi: ।।17.9।।अति कड़वे, अति खट्टे, अति नमकीन, अति गरम, अति तीखे, अति रूखे और अति दाहकारक आहार अर्थात् भोजनके पदार्थ राजस मनुष्यको प्रिय होते हैं, जो कि दुःख, शोक और रोगोंको देनेवाले हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: kaṭu—bitter; amla—sour; lavaṇa—salty; ati-uṣhṇa—very hot; tīkṣhṇa—pungent; rūkṣha—dry; vidāhinaḥ—chiliful; āhārāḥ—food; rājasasya—to persons in the mode of passion; iṣhṭāḥ—dear; duḥkha—pain; śhoka—grief; āmaya—disease; pradāḥ—produce

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्।।17.12।।
verses.transliteration:
abhisandhāya tu phalaṁ dambhārtham api chaiva yat
ijyate bharata-śhreṣhṭha taṁ yajñaṁ viddhi rājasam
verses.translation: But that sacrifice which is offered with the intention of gaining a reward and for the sake of show, know it, O Arjuna, to be Rajasic.
verses.hindi: ।।17.12।।परन्तु हे भरतश्रेष्ठ अर्जुन ! जो यज्ञ फलकी इच्छाको लेकर अथवा दम्भ-(दिखावटीपन-) के लिये भी किया जाता है, उसको तुम राजस समझो।
verses.wordMeaning: abhisandhāya—motivated by; tu—but; phalam—the result; dambha—pride; artham—for the sake of; api—also; cha—and; eva—certainly; yat—that which; ijyate—is performed; bharata-śhreṣhṭha—Arjun, the best of the Bharatas; tam—that; yajñam—sacrifice; viddhi—know; rājasam—in the mode of passion

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः।भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते।।17.16।।
verses.transliteration:
manaḥ-prasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ
bhāva-sanśhuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam uchyate
verses.translation: Serenity of mind, benevolence, silence, self-control, and purity of mind—these are known as austerity of the mind.
verses.hindi: ।।17.16।।मनकी प्रसन्नता, सौम्य भाव, मननशीलता, मनका निग्रह और भावोंकी शुद्धि -- इस तरह यह मन-सम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: manaḥ-prasādaḥ—serenity of thought; saumyatvam—gentleness; maunam—silence; ātma-vinigrahaḥ—self-control; bhāva-sanśhuddhiḥ—purity of purpose; iti—thus; etat—these; tapaḥ—austerity; mānasam—of the mind; uchyate—are declared as

verses.sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्।।17.18।।
verses.transliteration:
satkāra-māna-pūjārthaṁ tapo dambhena chaiva yat
kriyate tad iha proktaṁ rājasaṁ chalam adhruvam
verses.translation: That austerity, practiced with ostentation for the sake of gaining respect, praise, and reverence, is here said to be Rajasa. It is unsteady and impermanent.
verses.hindi: ।।17.18।।जो तप सत्कार, मान और पूजाके लिये तथा दिखानेके भावसे किया जाता है, वह इस लोकमें अनिश्चित और नाशवान् फल देनेवाला तप राजस कहा गया है।
verses.wordMeaning: sat-kāra—respect; māna—honor; pūjā—adoration; artham—for the sake of; tapaḥ—austerity; dambhena—with ostentation; cha—also; eva—certainly; yat—which; kriyate—is performed; tat—that; iha—in this world; proktam—is said; rājasam—in the mode of passion; chalam—flickering; adhruvam—temporary

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा।।17.23।।
verses.transliteration:
oṁ tat sad iti nirdeśho brahmaṇas tri-vidhaḥ smṛitaḥ
brāhmaṇās tena vedāśh cha yajñāśh cha vihitāḥ purā
verses.translation: Om, Tat, Sat—thus, Brahman is denoted by this threefold expression. In the past, Brahmanas, the Vedas, and sacrifices were ordained in association with these.
verses.hindi: ।।17.23।। ऊँ, तत् और सत् -- इन तीनों नामोंसे जिस परमात्माका निर्देश किया गया है, उसी परमात्माने सृष्टिके आदिमें वेदों, ब्राह्मणों और यज्ञोंकी रचना की है।
verses.wordMeaning: om tat sat—syllables representing aspects of transcendence; iti—thus; nirdeśhaḥ—symbolic representatives; brahmaṇaḥ—the Supreme Absolute Truth; tri-vidhaḥ—of three kinds; smṛitaḥ—have been declared; brāhmaṇāḥ—the priests; tena—from them; vedāḥ—scriptures; cha—and; yajñāḥ—sacrifice; cha—and; vihitāḥ—came about; purā—from the beginning of creation

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्।।17.24।।
verses.transliteration:
tasmād oṁ ity udāhṛitya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṁ brahma-vādinām
verses.translation: Therefore, the Veda-enjoined sacrificial acts, gifts, and austerities, expounded by the Vedas, or those belonging to the first three stations, are always begun after pronouncing Om at the beginning.
verses.hindi: ।।17.24।।इसलिये वैदिक सिद्धान्तोंको माननेवाले पुरुषोंकी शास्त्रविधिसे नियत यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप क्रियाएँ सदा 'ऊँ' इस परमात्माके नामका उच्चारण करके ही आरम्भ होती हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: tasmāt—therefore; om—sacred syllable om; iti—thus; udāhṛitya—by uttering; yajña—sacrifice; dāna—charity; tapaḥ—penance; kriyāḥ—performing; pravartante—begin; vidhāna-uktāḥ—according to the prescriptions of Vedic injunctions; satatam—always; brahma-vādinām—expounders of the Vedas

verses.sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि।।17.25।।
verses.transliteration:
tad ity anabhisandhāya phalaṁ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ
dāna-kriyāśh cha vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣha-kāṅkṣhibhiḥ
verses.translation: Acts of sacrifice, austerity, and various gifts are performed without aiming at a reward by those who seek release, after pronouncing Tat.
verses.hindi: ।।17.25।। 'तत्' नामसे कहे जानेवाले परमात्माके लिये ही सब कुछ है -- ऐसा मानकर मुक्ति चाहनेवाले मनुष्योंद्वारा फलकी इच्छासे रहित होकर अनेक प्रकारकी यज्ञ और तपरूप क्रियाएँ तथा दानरूप क्रियाएँ की जाती हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: tat—the syllable Tat; iti—thus; anabhisandhāya—without desiring; phalam—fruitive rewards; yajña—sacrifice; tapaḥ—austerity; kriyāḥ—acts; dāna—charity; kriyāḥ—acts; cha—and; vividhāḥ—various; kriyante—are done; mokṣha-kāṅkṣhibhiḥ—by seekers of freedom from material entanglements

verses.sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते | स गुणान् समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: One who serves Me with undeviating devotion, transcending these three qualities, becomes fit to realize Brahman.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन तीनों गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म-प्राप्ति के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.
verses.commentary: The ultimate way to transcend the gunas is not suppression but transcendence through devotion. The person who acts entirely in service — with no personal agenda, no craving for results — is no longer caught in the web of guna-interactions. They become "gunatita" — beyond the qualities.

verses.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च | तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ||
verses.transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca | tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi ||
verses.translation: For one who has taken birth, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain. Therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि जन्म लेने वाले के लिए मृत्यु निश्चित है, और मृत्यु होने वाले के लिए जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए इस अपरिहार्य विषय में तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.
verses.commentary: Krishna states the fundamental law of existence: the cycle of birth and death is inevitable for all embodied beings. Dhruva (certain, fixed) — both birth and death are certainties. The logic is simple: if you lament the inevitable, you create unnecessary suffering. The wise accept what cannot be changed and focus their energy on what can be transformed — their own inner state.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् | सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvāca | dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen arrayed here eager to fight, my limbs are giving way, and my mouth is drying up.
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले — हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छा से खड़े इन स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुँह सूख रहा है।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.
verses.commentary: Arjuna's physical symptoms — trembling limbs, dry mouth — are signs of acute stress. He calls them "svajanam" (own people), revealing he cannot see them as enemies.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज | अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ||
verses.transliteration: sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja | ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
verses.translation: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.
verses.hindi: सभी धर्मों (कर्तव्यों) को छोड़कर मेरी ही शरण में आओ। मैं तुम्हें सम्पूर्ण पापों से मुक्त कर दूँगा, तुम शोक न करो।
verses.wordMeaning: The culminating message of the entire Gita. Krishna asks for complete surrender (śaraṇāgati). He promises liberation from all sins to those who take refuge in Him alone.
verses.commentary: The culminating message of the entire Gita. Krishna asks for complete surrender (śaraṇāgati). He promises liberation from all sins to those who take refuge in Him alone.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्धो धनुर्धरः | तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ||
verses.transliteration: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ | tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama ||
verses.translation: Wherever there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and wherever there is Arjuna, the bearer of the bow, there will certainly be opulence, victory, prosperity, and righteousness.
verses.hindi: जहाँ योगेश्वर कृष्ण हैं और जहाँ धनुर्धारी अर्जुन हैं, वहीं श्री, विजय, विभूति और अचल नीति है — यही मेरा मत है।
verses.wordMeaning: The final verse of the Gita. It affirms that wherever God and the devotee are united in the spirit of dharma, all auspiciousness follows. This is the ultimate benediction.
verses.commentary: The final verse of the Gita. It affirms that wherever God and the devotee are united in the spirit of dharma, all auspiciousness follows. This is the ultimate benediction.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत | श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ||
verses.transliteration: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhāḥ sa eva saḥ ||
verses.translation: The faith of each person, O Bharata, accords with their natural disposition. A person is made of their faith; what their faith is, that, verily, they are.
verses.hindi: हे भारत! प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की श्रद्धा उसके स्वभाव (सत्त्व) के अनुसार होती है। यह पुरुष श्रद्धामय है — जैसी श्रद्धा, वैसा पुरुष।
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."
verses.commentary: One of the most psychologically precise verses in the Gita. Shraddha is often translated "faith" but it means something richer — one's deepest assumptions about what is real, what is possible, what is worth living for. What you fundamentally believe (consciously or not) shapes everything: what you pursue, how you act, what you become. "You are what you believe."

verses.sanskrit: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः।।18.4।।
verses.transliteration:
niśhchayaṁ śhṛiṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama
tyāgo hi puruṣha-vyāghra tri-vidhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ
verses.translation: Listen to My decision, O Arjuna, concerning abandonment; for abandonment is declared to be of three kinds.
verses.hindi: ।।18.4।। हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन ! तू संन्यास और त्याग -- इन दोनोंमेंसे पहले त्यागके विषयमें मेरा निश्चय सुन; क्योंकि हे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ ! त्याग तीन प्रकारका कहा गया है।
verses.wordMeaning: niśhchayam—conclusion; śhṛiṇu—hear; me—my; tatra—there; tyāge—about renunciation of desires for enjoying the fruits of actions; bharata-sat-tama—best of the Bharatas; tyāgaḥ—renunciation of desires for enjoying the fruits of actions; hi—indeed; puruṣha-vyāghra—tiger amongst men; tri-vidhaḥ—of three kinds; samprakīrtitaḥ—declared

verses.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: uddharedātmanātmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet | ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: One must elevate oneself by the mind; never degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
verses.hindi: अपने आपको अपने आपसे ऊपर उठाओ, अपने आपको गिर्फ्तार न करो। मन ही आत्मा का मित्र है और मन ही आत्मा का शत्रु।
verses.wordMeaning: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.
verses.commentary: The mind can be one's greatest ally or worst enemy. Self-mastery is the essence of yoga.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः | अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ||
verses.transliteration: bandhurātmātmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
verses.translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.
verses.hindi: जिसने अपने मन को अपने आप से जीत लिया है, उसके लिए मन ही सर्वश्रेष्ठ मित्र है। जिसने मन को नहीं जीता, वह मन ही शत्रु की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.
verses.commentary: Victory over the self is true victory. An unconquered mind leads one into bondage despite external achievements.

verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyūthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and rise of adharma, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब भारत! धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं अपना रूप प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.
verses.commentary: The famous declaration of avatarahood. Krishna does not say he incarnates to destroy evil; he incarnates when dharma declines. The focus is on restoration, not destruction. The divine response is not punitive but restorative.

verses.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ||
verses.transliteration: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
verses.translation: To protect the righteous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, I appear in every age.
verses.hindi: साधुओं की रक्षा, दुष्टों के विनाश और धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए मैं युग-युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.
verses.commentary: The purpose of divine descent is not personal but cosmic — restoring the balance of dharma across ages.

verses.sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन।सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः।।18.9।।
verses.transliteration:
kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṁ kriyate ‘rjuna
saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalaṁ chaiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
verses.translation: When actions are performed as they ought to be done, O Arjuna, renouncing attachment and the results thereof, such abandonment is regarded as Sattvika.
verses.hindi: ।।18.9।।हे अर्जुन ! 'केवल कर्तव्यमात्र करना है' -- ऐसा समझकर जो नियत कर्म आसक्ति और फलका त्याग करके किया जाता है, वही सात्त्विक त्याग माना गया है।
verses.wordMeaning: kāryam—as a duty; iti—as; eva—indeed; yat—which; karma niyatam—obligatory actions; kriyate—are performed; arjuna—Arjun; saṅgam—attachment; tyaktvā—relinquishing; phalam—reward; cha—and; eva—certainly; saḥ—such; tyāgaḥ—renunciation of desires for enjoying the fruits of actions; sāttvikaḥ—in the mode of goodness; mataḥ—considered

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः | लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
verses.translation: One who performs actions by offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
verses.hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कर्मों को ब्रह्म में अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, वह जल से कमल-पत्र की तरह पाप से लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.
verses.commentary: Krishna defines renunciation not as withdrawal from life, but as a change in ownership. Action continues, but the ego no longer claims it as 'mine' or clings to its results. The lotus leaf is in water without being soaked by it; the yogi is in the world without being possessed by it.

verses.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ||
verses.transliteration: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase | gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
verses.translation: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the departed or for those who have not departed.
verses.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण बोले — तुम उनके लिए शोक करते हो जो शोक के योग्य नहीं हैं, फिर भी ज्ञान की बातें करते हो। बुद्धिमान न जीवित के लिए शोक करते हैं, न मृत के लिए।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.
verses.commentary: Krishna reveals Arjuna's contradiction — he speaks like a wise man but grieves like an ignorant one. The wise understand that the Self is eternal and never dies.

verses.sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्।भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्।।18.12।।
verses.transliteration:
aniṣhṭam iṣhṭaṁ miśhraṁ cha tri-vidhaṁ karmaṇaḥ phalam
bhavaty atyāgināṁ pretya na tu sannyāsināṁ kvachit
verses.translation: Undesirable, desirable, and mixed—thus, threefold is the fruit of work that accrues after death to those who have not renounced; but to those who have renounced, none accrues whatsoever.
verses.hindi: ।।18.12।।कर्मफलका त्याग न करनेवाले मनुष्योंको कर्मोंका इष्ट, अनिष्ट और मिश्रित -- ऐसे तीन प्रकारका फल मरनेके बाद भी होता है; परन्तु कर्मफलका त्याग करनेवालोंको कहीं भी नहीं होता।
verses.wordMeaning: aniṣhṭam—unpleasant; iṣhṭam—pleasant; miśhram—mixed; cha—and; tri-vidham—three-fold; karmaṇaḥ phalam—fruits of actions; bhavati—accrue; atyāginām—to those who are attached to persona reward; pretya—after death; na—not; tu—but; sanyāsinām—for the renouncers of actions; kvachit—ever

verses.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा | तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ||
verses.transliteration: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā | tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati ||
verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.hindi: जैसे इस शरीर में जीवात्मा बाल्य, यौवन और वृद्धावस्था को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही वह दूसरे शरीर को प्राप्त होता है। धीर पुरुष इसमें मोहित नहीं होते।
verses.wordMeaning: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.
verses.commentary: The Self (Atman) is the inhabitant of the body (dehin). Just as we change clothes, the soul changes bodies. Birth, death, and rebirth are natural transitions for the wise.

verses.sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः | आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ||
verses.transliteration: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata ||
verses.translation: The contact of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, gives rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These are temporary and fleeting. Bear them patiently, O Bharata.
verses.hindi: हे कौन्तेय! इन्द्रियों का विषयों से सम्पर्क शीत-उष्ण, सुख-दुःख को देने वाला है। वे आगम-अपायिन (आने-जाने वाले) और अनित्य हैं, उन्हें तू सहन कर।
verses.wordMeaning: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.
verses.commentary: Krishna introduces the practice of titiksha (patient endurance). The pairs of opposites — cold-heat, pleasure-pain — arise from sense contact, not from reality itself. They come and go; they are impermanent. The key teaching here is that suffering is not caused by external events but by our reaction to them. By developing titiksha, one learns to observe sensations without reaction, which is the foundation of equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः | हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
verses.translation: One by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world — who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety — he is dear to Me.
verses.hindi: जिससे संसार उद्विग्न नहीं होता और जो संसार से उद्विग्न नहीं होता, जो हर्ष, अमर्ष, भय और उद्वेग से मुक्त है — वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.wordMeaning: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.
verses.commentary: The ideal devotee neither disturbs others nor is disturbed by them. Freedom from the pairs of opposites (dvandvas) is the mark of mature devotion.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः।पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः।।18.16।।
verses.transliteration:
tatraivaṁ sati kartāram ātmānaṁ kevalaṁ tu yaḥ
paśhyaty akṛita-buddhitvān na sa paśhyati durmatiḥ
verses.translation: Therefore, he who, due to his uncultivated understanding, perceives only the self as the agent, he of wicked mind does not truly perceive.
verses.hindi: ।।18.16।।परन्तु ऐसे पाँच हेतुओंके होनेपर भी जो उस (कर्मोंके) विषयमें केवल (शुद्ध) आत्माको कर्ता मानता है, वह दुर्मति ठीक नहीं समझता; क्योंकि उसकी बुद्धि शुद्ध नहीं है।
verses.wordMeaning: tatra—there; evam sati—in spite of this; kartāram—the doer; ātmānam—the soul; kevalam—only; tu—but; yaḥ—who; paśhyati—see; akṛita-buddhitvāt—with impure intellect; na—not; saḥ—they; paśhyati—see; durmatiḥ—foolish

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च | प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau tamaso bhavatojñānameva ca ||
verses.translation: From sattva, knowledge arises; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance also.
verses.hindi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान उत्पन्न होता है; रजस से लोभ; और तमस से प्रमाद, मोह और अज्ञान।
verses.wordMeaning: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.
verses.commentary: Each guna produces its characteristic fruit in the mind. Sattva produces clear understanding (jnana). Rajas produces greed — always wanting more, never satisfied. Tamas produces negligence (pramada) and delusion (moha). These are not moral judgments but precise descriptions of how different mind-states produce different thoughts and actions.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः।।18.18।।
verses.transliteration:
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ parijñātā tri-vidhā karma-chodanā
karaṇaṁ karma karteti tri-vidhaḥ karma-saṅgrahaḥ
verses.translation: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower are the threefold incitements to action. The instrument, the act, and the agent are the threefold constituents of action.
verses.hindi: ।।18.18।।ज्ञान, ज्ञेय और परिज्ञाता -- इन तीनोंसे कर्मप्रेरणा होती है तथा करण, कर्म और कर्ता -- इन तीनोंसे कर्मसंग्रह होता है।
verses.wordMeaning: jñānam—knowledge; jñeyam—the object of knowledge; parijñātā—the knower; tri-vidhā—three factors; karma-chodanā—factors that induce action; karaṇam—the instrumens of action; karma—the act; kartā—the doer; iti—thus; tri-vidhaḥ—threefold; karma-saṅgrahaḥ—constituents of action

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर | असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.transliteration: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
verses.translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment. By working without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: इसलिए सदा आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्तव्य-कर्म को भली-भाँति कर। आसक्ति रहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परंब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.wordMeaning: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.
verses.commentary: Action purifies the mind when done without attachment. Inaction binds one to inertia and tamas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः | प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ||
verses.transliteration: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
verses.translation: O King, thereafter, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed and weapons about to clash, the Pandava (Arjuna), whose banner bore the monkey emblem, picked up his bow.
verses.hindi: हनुमान-ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने युद्ध के लिए अपना धनुष उठाया। प्रतीक और आदर्श मन को साहस देते हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is called "kapidhvajaḥ" — one whose banner bears Hanuman. This signifies divine protection. He picks up his bow, showing initial readiness.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः | कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ||
verses.transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhastatholobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
verses.translation: Three are the gates of this hell that lead to the ruin of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.hindi: तीन प्रकार के नर्क के द्वार हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं — काम (वासना), क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को त्यागना चाहिए।
verses.wordMeaning: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.
verses.commentary: "Narak" here is not a place after death but a state of being in this life — the hell of living driven by lust, anger, and greed. These three form a self-reinforcing loop: lust (craving for what you don't have) → frustration when blocked → anger → craving more → greed. Breaking any one of the three weakens all three.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: For those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on Me constantly, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.hindi: जो भक्त अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन नित्य भक्तों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.wordMeaning: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.
verses.commentary: God personally takes care of His devotees. "Yoga" means acquiring what one lacks; "kṣema" means protecting what one has.

verses.sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम्।अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते।।18.23।।
verses.transliteration:
niyataṁ saṅga-rahitam arāga-dveṣhataḥ kṛitam
aphala-prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam uchyate
verses.translation: That obligatory act is said to be Sattvika, which is done without attachment, without desire or aversion, and by one who seeks no fruit.
verses.hindi: ।।18.23।।जो कर्म शास्त्रविधिसे नियत किया हुआ और कर्तृत्वाभिमानसे रहित हो तथा फलेच्छारहित मनुष्यके द्वारा बिना राग-द्वेषके किया हुआ हो, वह सात्त्विक कहा जाता है।
verses.wordMeaning: niyatam—in accordance with scriptures; saṅga-rahitam—free from attachment; arāga-dveṣhataḥ—free from attachment and aversion; kṛitam—done; aphala-prepsunā—without desire for rewards; karma—action; yat—which; tat—that; sāttvikam—in the mode of goodness; uchyate—is called

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्।।18.24।।
verses.transliteration:
yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhankāreṇa vā punaḥ
kriyate bahulāyāsaṁ tad rājasam udāhṛitam
